title.rendered: one out of many suspension bridge
Humla residents continue to suffer as border point remains closed

content.rendered:
Humla, October 9

The closure of Nepal’s Hilsa border point with China has caused severe hardship for residents in the border area. Locals and security personnel have been struggling to access food, drinking water and healthcare after heavy snowfall blocked the cross-border route on September 25.

The border point was closed due to a heavy accumulation of snow, while the access road was also badly affected by a blizzard. With the Dashain festival approaching, people stranded in Hilsa because of the blocked road and border crossing have grown increasingly concerned.

The shortage of daily essentials has hit residents hard, as cross-border movement and transportation remain disrupted. Green vegetables are unavailable in local markets, let alone fish and meat.

Kedar Sapkota, an inspector of police at the Hilsa border security post, said personnel had been forced to make do with lentil soup. Access to medical treatment has also become a major concern.

An Armed Police Force (APF) personnel trained as a community medical assistant has been helping sick people by providing medicines, including paracetamol.

Although the border crossing into China reopened on Thursday, 144 Nepali citizens entered Nepal despite the difficult conditions.

Snow clearance began on Wednesday, with a mini excavator being used to remove the blockage. However, the machine is too small to clear the access road in a timely manner. Concerned about the slow progress, more than 100 people have left Hilsa for other parts of the district and beyond.

Hilsa has 63 government employees, including 35 APF personnel and 20 Nepal Police personnel, along with some residents.

title.rendered: Nepal produces 3.8 million eggs daily against demand for 5 million

content.rendered:
Chitwan, October 9

Nepal produces around 3.8 million eggs a day, falling short of the estimated daily demand of five million, despite a recent increase in the number of farmers raising layer chickens, according to the Nepal Layer Poultry Farmers Association.

Association central president Binod Pokhrel said commercial egg production was picking up as farmers began receiving prices that covered their production costs. He added that the inflow of eggs smuggled from India had stopped in April, providing relief to domestic producers.

The association aims to restore production to pre-pandemic levels of 6.5 million to seven million eggs a day. The number of large-scale layer farmers has risen from around 120 four years ago to 180 now, Pokhrel said.

Eggs are selling for around Rs 600 per crate of 30, while the production cost is approximately Rs 19 per egg. However, consumers pay Rs 25 to Rs 30 per egg at retail outlets.

Pokhrel said extreme heat, disease outbreaks and bird flu in April and May had reduced production. He expects output to increase as winter approaches.

On World Egg Day, the association organised a Zumba dance and an “Egg Walk” in Bharatpur to raise awareness of eggs’ nutritional value. The annual observance falls on the second Friday of October. This year’s theme is “The Mighty Egg: Packed with Protein, Powering and Protecting.”

title.rendered: Govt reaches 3-point agreement with intern doctor on stipend demand

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, October 9

The government has reached an agreement with Dilli Harijan, who was staging a hunger strike for the second time, demanding an increase in the stipend for medical interns.

The three-point agreement provides for his demands to be presented at a meeting of the Medical Education Commission. Harijan had been on a hunger strike for five days.

The agreement was reached between Harijan’s representatives and a government negotiation team led by Jayaram Adhikari, joint secretary at the Ministry of Education and Sports.

Under the agreement, a proposal to provide medical interns pursuing one-year internships in MBBS, BDS and other programmes with a stipend equivalent to 50 per cent of the starting salary at the eighth level of the health service will be presented at a meeting of the Medical Education Commission.

Harijan had also staged a hunger strike. On August 7, the government reached an agreement with him, pledging to address his demands.

Harijan resumed his hunger strike, accusing the government of failing to implement the agreement. He began the strike on the premises of the Medical Education Commission in Bhaktapur. As his health deteriorated, he was taken to Bir Hospital.

title.rendered: Investment approved for two semi-reservoir hydropower projects

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, October 9

The Investment Board has approved investment in two semi-reservoir hydropower projects.

The decision was made at the board’s 68th meeting, held today under the chairmanship of Prime Minister Balen Shah.

The meeting approved investment in the 58.9 MW Nar Khola semi-reservoir hydropower project, costing Rs 10.75 billion, and the 46.72 MW Sani Bheri-3 semi-reservoir hydropower project, costing Rs 10.42 billion.

The meeting also decided that the 900 MW Arun-3 hydropower project will begin commercial generation by February 2028, and that the necessary facilitation will be provided to move ahead immediately with construction of the 900 MW Upper Karnali hydropower project, in line with the provisions of its project development agreement.

To facilitate implementation of the approved projects and the services provided to investors, and to ensure effective performance, the meeting decided to delegate the necessary powers to the chief executive officer of the Investment Board Office.

It also decided to direct the office to make the necessary legal arrangements so that proposals not invited by the board can be advanced through competition under the Swiss challenge method, as required.

In addition, the meeting decided that if investment proposals are received for infrastructure projects based on the latest information technologies, including artificial intelligence, priority will be given to developing such projects, taking into account their contribution to using Nepal’s renewable energy, creating jobs and advancing economic development.

title.rendered: Proposed 55–30 retirement rule triggers resignations at Parliament Secretariat

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, October 9

Seven employees of the Federal Parliament Secretariat have resigned amid concerns over a proposed amendment to the Civil Service Act that would make employees eligible for compulsory retirement after completing 30 years of service or reaching the age of 55.

The government is preparing to introduce an ordinance to amend the civil service law, prompting employees of the Parliament Secretariat to resign as well.

According to a source at the Secretariat, seven employees have resigned since October 2.

Those who have submitted their resignations include technical officers Sudarshan Gautam and Naresh Shrestha, printing officer Rajendra Lamichhane, non-gazetted first-class officer Dipendra KC, section officer Ganesh Simkhada, and office assistants Laxmi Giri and Chirikaji Maharjan.

Gautam, a technical officer, had worked at the Parliament Secretariat for 34 years. Although he had another six years and two months before reaching the retirement age under the existing law, he decided to resign following the proposed changes.

“I still had some time left. When the 55–30 provision came up in the civil service bill, I thought it would be better to resign,” he said.

The government has already registered a federal civil service bill in Parliament that proposes extending the retirement provisions to parliamentary service employees. Under the proposal, employees would be compulsorily retired after completing 30 years of service or reaching the age of 55.

However, with the parliamentary session prorogued, speculation has grown among civil servants that the government may introduce the legislation through an ordinance.

Parliamentary service employees are currently governed by a separate law enacted in 2007. Employees at the Secretariat have expressed concern that the proposed federal civil service legislation would bring them under the same retirement provisions.

One employee said they had resigned because the proposed changes would undermine employee rights and alter the terms and conditions under which they had entered service.

“Who is the permanent government?” the employee asked, raising concerns about the security and continuity of public service employment.

The draft federal civil service bill proposes a one-time transitional provision allowing employees to retire at the age of 58. After this transitional arrangement, the mandatory retirement age would be set at 60, according to the draft legislation.

title.rendered: Government directs essential services to operate regularly during festivals

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, October 9

The government has directed the concerned agencies to keep essential services, including health, drinking water, electricity, telecommunications, airports, transport and hospitals, running regularly during the festival season.

The Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers at Singha Durbar said it issued the directive at a press briefing on Friday.

Speaking at the briefing, Hem Raj Aryal, joint secretary and spokesperson at the office, said the agencies have been told to keep the necessary human resources, medicines and equipment ready so that essential services are not disrupted during the festivals.

“A decision has been made to keep the necessary human resources, medicines, equipment and emergency services ready so that health, drinking water, electricity, telecommunications, airports, transport, hospitals and other essential services continue to operate without interruption during the festivals, and so that citizens are not subjected to unnecessary hardship in accessing essential services. We have written to the concerned agencies about this,” he said.

According to him, the agencies have also been told not to cause citizens unnecessary hardship in obtaining essential services.

Spokesperson Aryal also said the government is preparing a draft procedure to make investment-related services simple, transparent, time-bound and predictable, in order to promote domestic and foreign investment.

“A draft of the ‘National Express Investment System Operation and Management Procedure’ is being prepared to promote domestic and foreign investment and to make investment-related services simple, transparent, predictable and time-bound,” Aryal said. “It is expected and believed that this will improve the investment system and thereby increase domestic and foreign investment.”

Spokesperson Aryal said the procedure is expected to make the investment process orderly and smooth and help increase domestic and foreign investment.

title.rendered: Rain with thunder in four districts of Karnali, people urged to stay alert

content.rendered:
Surkhet, October 9

Rain accompanied by thunder and lightning is falling in Dailekh, Surkhet, Salyan and Rukum West of Karnali Province. The Meteorological Forecasting Division has urged people in these districts to stay alert, citing the possibility of rain.

Most parts of Karnali Province have received rain in the past 24 hours. Rain with thunder and lightning is still falling in districts including Surkhet, Dolpa, Humla, Dailekh and Rukum West.

Rain and snowfall are also possible in the province’s other districts. The division said rain may also fall in some places this Saturday and Sunday.

Continuous rain carries the risk of landslides, road blockages and rising water levels in rivers and streams in the hilly and mountainous areas. This could affect transport services and daily life.

People living in settlements at risk of landslides have been urged to be especially careful. They have been advised not to go into rivers and streams during rain, to avoid unnecessary travel in risky areas, and to travel only after checking road conditions.

title.rendered: All stock market indicators rise, banking gains traction

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, October 9

All sectoral indices, along with the NEPSE benchmark index, rose in the stock market on Friday. The NEPSE index gained 17.15 points to close at 2,591.

Turnover also improved, reaching Rs 4.83 billion today from Rs 3.93 billion the previous day.

Prices of 180 companies rose today, while 89 fell. Ten were unchanged. Banking, the largest sector, saw the strongest interest on Friday, with its sectoral index rising 1.28 percent, the most among all groups.

Among individual stocks, Kutheli Bukhari Small Hydropower rose 4.91 percent, Sindhu Bikas Bank 4.22 percent, Solu Hydropower 4.05 percent and Sanvi Energy 3.86 percent. Ridiline Energy fell 7.85 percent, Mahila Laghubitta 2.09 percent and Sayapatri Hydropower 2.08 percent.

The most actively traded companies today, in order, were Kumari Bank, Ghalemdi Hydropower, Himalayan Distillery, Solu Hydropower, Laxmi Sunrise Bank, Sonapur Minerals, SY Panel and Balephi Hydropower.

title.rendered: Postal service being developed as government courier service, says Communications Minister Timilsina

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, October 9

Minister for Information and Communications Bikram Timilsina has said the plan to make the postal service modern, effective and citizen-friendly, and to develop it as a government courier service, is being implemented effectively.

Speaking at a philatelic exhibition organised by the Department of Postal Services to mark the 152nd World Post Day, he said the government is committed to restructuring the postal service in line with changing times and citizens’ needs and bringing it within the reach of the general public.

Stressing the need to preserve the historical importance of the postal service while connecting it to modern life, Minister Timilsina said, “The postal service has a distinctive history. Now, alongside its history, we must also think of its future and build a modern, practical and citizen-centred service.”

He said the development of modern technology has changed citizens’ needs and the way they receive services. He said it is necessary to make the postal service suit the times.

The department has issued postage stamps bearing the portraits of Bise Nagarchi and Wange Sarki, who contributed to Nepal’s unification and nation-building; Kulbir Thapa Magar and Karna Bahadur Rana Magar, who received the Victoria Cross in the First World War; and John Logie Baird, the inventor of television, to mark 100 years since the invention of television.

The department said each stamp is priced at Rs 10. At the programme, Minister Timilsina applied the seal to the first-day cover of the stamps.

National Dalit Commission Chairperson Devr Raj Bishwakarma said that issuing stamps bearing the portraits of Bise Nagarchi and Wange Sarki shows the state’s recognition of the historic contribution of the Dalit community.

Communications Secretary Rajendra Kumar Paudel said that, in changed circumstances, the postal service should be made an effective means of expanding citizen services. He said the postal network, which extends to the municipal level across the country, can be used to deliver services to citizens’ doorsteps as a government courier service.

Manmaya Bhattarai Pangeni, director general of the Department of Postal Services, said the postal service remains relevant across the world.

title.rendered: Agreement reached with Dilli Harijan on stipend demand after five-day hunger strike

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, October 9

The government and Dilli Harijan, who was staging a hunger strike for the second time demanding an increase in stipends for medical interns, have reached an agreement.

A three-point agreement was reached between the two sides, under which Harijan’s demands will be presented at a meeting of the Medical Education Commission. He had been on a hunger strike for five days.

The agreement was reached between Harijan’s representatives and a government negotiation team led by Jayaram Adhikari, joint-secretary at the Ministry of Education and Sports.

Under the agreement, a proposal to provide interns pursuing MBBS, BDS and other programmes requiring a one-year internship with a stipend equivalent to 50 percent of the entry-level salary of an eighth-level health service employee will be presented at the commission’s meeting.

Harijan had also staged a hunger strike in July, following which the government signed an agreement with him on July 7, pledging to address his demands.

However, accusing the government of failing to implement the agreement, Harijan resumed his hunger strike. He began the protest at the premises of the Medical Education Commission in Bhaktapur.

As his health condition deteriorated, he was taken to Bir Hospital for treatment.

title.rendered: Govt declares flood-hit areas in 6 districts disaster zones

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, October 9

The government has declared local governments affected by floods and landslides between Asoj 8 and 11 as disaster-hit areas.

The Ministry of Home Affairs published a notice in the Nepal Gazette declaring various rural municipalities and municipal wards in Gorkha, Manang, Myagdi, Baglung, Parbat and Nawalparasi (Bardaghat Susta West) as disaster-hit areas. The declaration is expected to facilitate the delivery of international relief supplies to the affected areas.

In Gorkha, Wards 3 and 4 of Shahid Lakhan Rural Municipality have been included on the list. In Manang, the designated areas are Chame Rural Municipality, Naso Rural Municipality and Wards 1 and 4 of Manang Disyang Rural Municipality.

In Myagdi, the designated areas include Annapurna, Raghuganga, Mangala, Dhaulagiri and Malika rural municipalities, as well as Beni Municipality.

In Baglung, the declaration covers Wards 4 and 6 of Nisikhola Rural Municipality, Badigad Rural Municipality, Wards 3 and 4 of Tamankhola Rural Municipality, and Tarakhola Rural Municipality.

In Parbat, the designated areas are Jaljala Rural Municipality; Wards 2, 3, 7, 8, 10 and 11 of Phalebas Municipality; Ward 6 of Bihadi Rural Municipality; Wards 5 and 6 of Mahashila Rural Municipality; and Wards 2 and 3 of Modi Rural Municipality.

Ward 5 of Susta Rural Municipality in Nawalparasi (Bardaghat Susta West) has also been included on the list.

The government has declared the areas disaster-hit zones for three months.

title.rendered: Labour department directs employers to provide mandatory festival allowance

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, October 9

The Department of Labour and Occupational Safety has directed all employers and establishments to provide workers with the mandatory festival allowance.

The department issued the directive following complaints that some employers had failed to provide the allowance.

Section 37 of the Labour Act, 2017, stipulates that every worker is entitled to an annual festival allowance equivalent to one month’s basic salary for festivals celebrated in accordance with their religion, culture and traditions.

The department has urged workers who have not received the allowance to file complaints or applications with the Labour and Employment Office responsible for their workplace or with the Department of Labour and Occupational Safety.

Workers can also submit complaints, grievances and suggestions via email. The department has provided a QR code to facilitate submissions.

Department spokesperson Maninath Gop said complaints had been received that some employers and establishments had failed to provide the festival allowance. He said the concerned establishments had been instructed to comply with the requirement and warned that those failing to do so would face action under the Labour Act.

title.rendered: Man wanted in attempted murder case arrested in Janakpur

content.rendered:
Janakpurdham, October 9

A 24-year-old man was stabbed to death, and another man was seriously injured in an attack near Janaki Temple in Ward 5 of Janakpurdham Sub-Metropolitan City on Thursday evening.

Mohammad Irshad Khan, 22, a resident, allegedly stabbed Aamin Safi, 24, of Daha Chowk in Sonarpatti, Janakpur, to death and seriously injured Imtiaz Rain, 25, Dhanusha police spokesperson DSP Om Prakash Khanal said. The injured man is receiving treatment at the Provincial Hospital in Janakpur.

The incident occurred at around 9:15 pm on Rahim Path. Khanal said Irshad stabbed both men in the chest and abdomen with a knife. Police have arrested him.

According to police, Irshad was already wanted in connection with an attempted murder case. On February 15, he allegedly attacked Mohammad Mustafa Rain, 26, of Rijaul in Ward 14 of Janakpurdham Sub-Metropolitan City, with a khukuri.

On the day of Bakra Eid, Irshad allegedly invited Mustafa to his home and took him to a shop, where he threatened to slit his throat with a khukuri. Other young men were also present. When Mustafa attempted to flee, Irshad chased him and attacked him from behind, injuring his left hand.

Irshad is also a TikTok content creator, with accounts under the name “Gunda” on TikTok and “MD Irshad Khan” on Facebook. He has reportedly posted dozens of videos targeting another community and promoting hatred, violence and abusive language. Calls for his arrest and legal action had been made previously.

Mustafa had filed a complaint against Irshad at the District Police Office in Dhanusha. Police subsequently pursued an attempted murder case against him. On July 16, police obtained an arrest warrant from the Dhanusha District Court.

The District Police Office had written to the Janaki Police Post on July 15, directing it to arrest Irshad. Police said they had been searching for him since then.

“We had already deployed police personnel to arrest Irshad. Officers had visited his home several times but failed to find him,” DSP Khanal said.

Irshad, who had evaded arrest in connection with the alleged khukuri attack on Mustafa, has now been arrested.

Residents allege that Irshad uses drugs. Police said his 42-year-old mother, Saimukh Khatun, was also arrested following Thursday’s incident and is being investigated.

title.rendered: Kathmandu Valley faces possible power cuts for 2 days as NEA upgrades transmission line

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, October 9

The Nepal Electricity Authority (NEA) is set to replace conductors on the Matatirtha-Syuchatar 132 kV transmission line to improve the reliability, quality and sustainability of electricity supply in the Kathmandu Valley.

The authority said the existing conductors would be replaced with higher-capacity ones to increase the transmission line’s capacity and strengthen the power system. As a result, electricity supply in the Kathmandu Valley may be disrupted on Saturday, October 10, and Sunday, October 11.

The 132 kV Transmission Line Upgrade Project, operated under the NEA’s Project Management Directorate, will replace the existing conductors on the Matatirtha-Syuchatar 132 kV double-circuit transmission line with higher-capacity conductors.

The transmission line will need to be shut down from 9 am to 5 pm on both days to carry out the work, the authority said.

The existing low-capacity conductors will be replaced with high-temperature low-sag (HTLS) conductors. Around 400 metres of conductor remain to be replaced on one circuit of the double-circuit line.

Once the work is completed, the transmission line’s electricity-carrying capacity is expected to increase, helping the authority manage growing electricity demand and improve the reliability of the power system.

Electricity supply may be affected in areas served by substations connected to the transmission line, including Matatirtha and Syuchatar, during the shutdown.

The authority said the necessary technical preparations had been made to complete the work within the scheduled timeframe. However, the schedule may change if weather conditions are unfavourable.

title.rendered: Salyan’s paddy fields turn golden as rice ripens (Photos)

content.rendered:
Paddy fields across Salyan have turned golden as the rice crop farmers planted a few months ago ripens. The fields and terraces have taken on a golden hue, creating picturesque scenes across the district’s rural areas. Farmers are now busy in their fields as the harvest season approaches.

Paddy is one of the major food crops grown in Salyan. According to the Agriculture Office, rice is cultivated on around 6,000 to 7,000 hectares of land in the district annually. The office said the district has produced more than 28,000 metric tonnes of paddy in recent years.

Agricultural technicians say rice production in the district could increase further with expanded irrigation facilities, the use of improved seeds and favourable weather conditions.

Marmaparikanda, Bangad Jiula, Gari Jiula, Resham Jiula, Kalimati Rampur and Kalche-Kaprechaur are among the district’s major paddy-producing areas.

This year, however, Bangad Jiula presents a different picture. While paddy has ripened and fields have turned golden across most parts of the district, rice transplantation in Bangad was delayed due to untimely rainfall. As a result, while fields elsewhere have already turned golden, those in Bangad Jiula remain green.

Salyan has so far remained self-sufficient in food grains. Paddy produced in the district meets a significant share of its food requirements.

title.rendered: Khanal pledges action on Nepali community’s suggestions during Canberra visit

content.rendered:
Canberra: Nepal’s Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal, currently on a visit to Australia, has held high-level meetings in the capital, Canberra, and interacted with the local Nepali community.

During the visit, Minister Khanal inspected the Nepali embassy in Canberra and the site of the proposed embassy building. He then interacted with representatives of various Nepali organisations active in Australia. Participants raised the concerns, problems and suggestions of the Nepali community with the minister.

At the programme, Vice-President Lalit Malla and spokesperson Ashok Basnet of the Australian Capital Territory (ACT) chapter of the Non-Resident Nepali Association (NRNA) Australia handed a memorandum to Minister Khanal.

The memorandum covers the protection of Nepali citizens in Australia, the establishment of an emergency assistance fund, effective implementation of non-resident Nepali citizenship, and strengthening economic, social and cultural ties between Nepal and Australia.

Meanwhile, on Friday, Minister Khanal paid a courtesy call on Australia’s Governor-General Sam Mostyn. During the meeting, he expressed heartfelt thanks to the Australian government and people for their support to Nepal after the unimaginable flood in the Bhotekoshi area.

Speaking to Onlinekhabar, Minister Khanal said his Australia visit has been fruitful. He also committed to implementing, on a priority basis, the suggestions received in his meetings with representatives of the Nepali community in Australia.

Having completed his scheduled programmes in Canberra, Minister Khanal left for Melbourne today. He is scheduled to return home on Saturday after completing his programmes in Melbourne.

title.rendered: 111.7 tonnes of fruit imported through Korala crossing in 11 days

content.rendered:
File

Mustang, October 9

A total of 111.7 tonnes of fruit have been imported from China through the Korala border crossing over the past 11 days.

The Quarantine Office at Nhechung, Lomanthang-4, reported that the influx of Chinese fruit continued despite heavy rainfall and snowfall. Bandana Ghartimagar, a technical assistant at the office, said the imports included 87.3 tonnes of apples, 16.1 tonnes of mangoes and 8.316 tonnes of dragon fruit.

However, adverse weather conditions have completely blocked the Beni-Jomsom-Korala road since September 27, making it difficult to transport the fruit to its destinations.

The delay has raised concerns about spoilage, as the imported fruit has remained inside containers for an extended period.

Meanwhile, some dragon fruit transported in a container was distributed to locals in Jomsom, Mustang, on Thursday. Subas Sunuwar, a company representative, said the dragon fruit, valued at around Rs 2.4 million, had been saved from rotting.

He added that the transportation delay had also resulted in estimated losses of Rs 3 million.

title.rendered: Committee formed to investigate school bus accident in Pokhara, report due within five days

content.rendered:
Pokhara, October 9

Pokhara Metropolitan City has formed a committee to investigate the accident involving a Kalika Boarding School bus that was bringing students from Majhthana in Pokhara Metropolitan City-28.

According to Mayor Dhanraj Acharya, the committee has been formed to establish the facts of the accident, identify its causes, and recommend the improvements needed to prevent such accidents from recurring.

The committee is coordinated by Badrinath Subedi, senior education officer at the metropolitan city. Its members are mechanical engineer Saroj Chalise, metropolitan education committee member Dolraj Pandey, city police inspector Purushottam Thapa, and assistant traffic inspector Amrit Bhattarai.

The committee has been tasked with studying and investigating the cause of the accident and related matters in detail and submitting a report within five days. It will also offer recommendations on the safety of school vehicles, the safe commute of students, and the precautions to be taken in future.

Stressing that student safety is a shared responsibility, Acharya called on all concerned parties to ensure regular inspection of school vehicles, strict compliance with safety standards, and effective monitoring.

title.rendered: Biratnagar Kings train in India, practising with Ranji Trophy players

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, October 9

Biratnagar Kings, preparing for the third edition of the Nepal Premier League (NPL), are training at the Purvanchal Cricket Academy in Uttar Pradesh, India.

All players except captain Sandeep Lamichhane have taken part in the training, which began on September 29. Lamichhane is with the national team for the ongoing ICC Cricket World Cup League 2 series in Oman. Lokesh Bam will join the team’s training from October 11.

At the academy, Biratnagar Kings are playing practice matches under floodlights against Indian players who have played in the Ranji Trophy.

The team is being trained by Biratnagar Kings head coach Dhammika Prasad and spin bowling coach Dinuka Sulakshana. Prasad said the training in India is going well. He said the players are receiving good training and are using the practice matches to strengthen their preparation.

“Our training in India is going well. The players are getting good training and are preparing themselves for the NPL through practice matches. The training and match practice here have helped the players’ preparation a great deal,” Prasad said.

With the third edition of the NPL in mind, the team has prioritised match practice alongside training.

title.rendered: Road reaches remote Mukot settlement at 5,700 meters

content.rendered:
Surkhet, October 9

The settlement of Mukot, located at the foothills of Mukot Himal, the source of the Thuli Bheri River, has been connected to the road network. The local government has extended the road to Mukot despite the extremely difficult terrain and the challenges of construction in the high Himalayas.

With road access reaching the Mukot area, considered one of the world’s highest inhabited settlements, locals who have long faced geographical isolation are expected to benefit from easier transportation.

Road construction involved working at extreme altitudes, including 5,700 metres, 5,500 metres, 5,300 metres and 4,846 metres.

According to Bam Bahadur Bhandari, an engineer at Chharka Tangsong Rural Municipality, the road was built through snow-covered terrain at the foothills of the Himalayas. He said construction in the high Himalayan region had been extremely challenging due to limited resources and adverse weather conditions.

65-kilometre road constructed

Around 30 kilometres of road has been constructed from the Mustang side to Ward No. 1 of Chharka Tangsong Rural Municipality. An additional 35 kilometres has been built from there to Mukot, engineer Bhandari said.

The approximately 65-kilometre road from Mustang through Chharka to Mukot has connected the high Himalayan settlement to the road network. Bhandari said the provincial government constructed 10 kilometres of the road, while the rural municipality built the remaining sections.

The road has expanded transport access from the source of the Thuli Bheri River through various settlements to the foothills of Mukot Himal.

Previously dependent on walking routes, locals are expected to find it easier to transport daily essentials, travel between settlements and carry local products to markets now that road access has been established.

Construction amid snow and extreme altitudes

Road construction in the high Himalayas is far more difficult than in ordinary terrain, engineer Bhandari said. Extreme altitudes, snow, cold weather and challenging geography posed numerous obstacles during construction.

“We carried out road construction by cutting through the snow at the foothills of the Himalayas,” Bhandari said.

The local government views the road’s extension to Mukot as more than an infrastructure project, describing it as an important effort to connect a remote Himalayan region with the mainstream of national development. The road is also expected to open up new opportunities in education, healthcare, trade and tourism.

Locals said the road, which extends from the source of the Thuli Bheri River through various settlements to the foothills of Mukot Himal, demonstrates the potential for infrastructure development in high Himalayan areas.

The road connecting Dolpa through Mustang has also shortened the travel route.

title.rendered: MPs cannot intimidate or threaten state institutions, Bartaula says

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, October 9

CPN-UML leader Mahesh Bartaula has said that being a member of parliament is not a licence to intimidate or threaten state institutions.

He made the remarks while urging an impartial investigation into any unlawful acts committed by the chief of the police organisation or any other official, and immediate legal action if they are found guilty.

“However, a ruling party lawmaker has repeatedly made public accusations against the heads and officials of a responsible state security organisation, defamed them, intimidated and threatened them, and used abusive language. This is the height of a ruling party lawmaker’s bullying and display of power,” he said.

Bartaula said such behaviour was contrary to the dignity and decorum of the parliamentary office.

Stating that the position of an MP is a prestigious constitutional responsibility that entails representing the people, he said, “Being an MP is not a licence to vent personal grievances, intimidate or threaten state institutions, undermine the morale of civil servants, or walk around pronouncing people guilty.”

While acknowledging that people have the right to raise questions and criticise state institutions and responsible officials in a democracy, he said, “However, no one has the right to engage in persistent disorder, threats and character assassination in the name of criticism in a way that weakens state institutions. The government and the concerned political party should take this matter seriously.”

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, October 9

Chinese nationals engaged in illegal gold trading from Budhanilkantha, Kathmandu, have been found using the house of a person living in the United States as their base.

Police sources said they had rented the house, owned by a person with the surname Bista, since last Shrawan. The monthly rent was set at Rs 330,000, and police sources said the landlord had been paid four months’ rent in advance.

Acting on information that illegal gold trading was taking place in the rented house, police raided it on Thursday and arrested three Chinese nationals. Police said they also recovered about 21 kg of gold, along with various machines and equipment, from the house.

According to police, one member of the Chinese group first came to Kathmandu to assess the market and the state of business here before returning to China. The other two then came to Nepal. Sources said that after arriving in Nepal, they were seen going to and from the airport three to four times.

title.rendered: Govt proposes interest subsidies for teachers’ vehicle purchases

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, October 9

The Ministry of Education has sent the Education (Eleventh Amendment) Regulations, 2083, which include a provision for interest subsidies on vehicle purchases by teachers, to the Ministry of Finance for approval.

Under the proposed provision, first-class secondary-level teachers will be eligible to purchase vehicles worth up to Rs 5 million, while second-class secondary-level teachers will be eligible for vehicles worth up to Rs 4 million.

Similarly, the provision proposes that third-class secondary-level teachers and teachers of all classes at the lower secondary and primary levels will be eligible to purchase two-wheelers worth up to Rs 400,000.

Under the regulations, the government will subsidise instalment interest on bank financing for vehicle purchases, covering up to 80 per cent of the total cost. Teachers will have to arrange the remaining 20 per cent themselves.

The government will cover the instalment interest charged by the concerned bank for as long as the teacher remains in service.

title.rendered: Four of five died in Pokhara school bus accident identified

content.rendered:
Pokhara, October 9

Four of the five people who died in this morning’s school bus accident in Pokhara, Kaski, have been identified.

The identified victims are Mamata Tiwari, 15, Asim Kandel, 13, Baburam Tiwari, 65, and Subechchha Tiwari, 15. The fifth victim, a girl thought to be about 15 years old, has not yet been identified.

The bus, which belongs to Kalika Boarding School in Shanti Maidan, met with the accident at a place called Okhlebhir while returning from Majhthana in Pokhara Metropolitan City-28 Friday morning. Those involved were rescued and brought to Western Regional Hospital for treatment.

According to a statement issued by the hospital, five of the 17 people brought in were already dead on arrival. The remaining 12 are undergoing treatment. Ashmi Kandel, 16, is being treated in the ICU.

Other injured include Sonia Tiwari, 13, Sneha Khatri, 14, Ankit Parajuli, 13, and Smriti Khatri, 15.

Supriya Acharya, 14, Merina Tiwari, 15, Akriti Budhathoki, 14, Arjun Shahi, 31, Yaman Magar, 16, and Tul Bahadur Gurung, 57, are also receiving treatment.

title.rendered: Businesses may have to conduct mandatory energy audits every three years under proposed bill

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, October 9

The government has proposed making energy audits mandatory for businesses and commercial sectors that consume energy above a threshold set by the government.

Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha has registered the Renewable Energy and Energy Efficiency Bill, 2026, in the House of Representatives, proposing new requirements for energy conservation and efficient energy use.

Sections 6 and 7 of the bill require businesses and sectors listed in its schedule that meet the prescribed energy-consumption threshold to maintain energy-use records, set energy-saving targets and undergo regular energy audits.

Under the proposed provisions, businesses would have to prepare and implement annual energy-efficiency plans, maintain monthly records of energy consumption, use energy-efficient technologies and equipment, and develop plans to replace equipment that consumes excessive energy.

They would also be required to conduct energy audits of the technologies, equipment and systems used for energy production, supply or consumption, and implement recommendations made in the audit reports.

The bill proposes that businesses conduct their first energy audit within three years of starting operations and subsequent audits every three years. Businesses already operating when the law comes into force would have to complete their first audit within three years of its commencement.

Businesses would also be required to appoint an energy manager to oversee compliance with the proposed obligations.

Under Section 7, energy audits would have to be conducted by qualified energy auditors. Their reports would need to cover energy audit policies and standards, energy-use data, technologies and equipment used in energy production and distribution, the state of energy consumption, and measures adopted to save energy.

The auditors would be required to provide a copy of the report to the concerned business or sector and the designated central authority.

The proposed provision would introduce a mandatory energy-audit requirement that is not currently in place. The requirements would take effect only if the bill is passed and becomes law.

title.rendered: Gagan Thapa pledges to bring all Nepali Congress leaders together, including rivals

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, October 9

Nepali Congress presidential candidate Gagan Thapa has pledged to bring together party leaders who stayed out of the ongoing General Convention process as well as those who lose the leadership election.

Speaking to journalists at the convention’s polling venue, Thapa said he would work to address discontent within the party and ensure that leaders and cadres from all sides have a place in the organisation.

Referring to the Deuba faction, which did not participate in the convention process, Thapa said the party would try to bring back those who had stayed away.

“Some of our colleagues and leaders are currently outside the process because they chose not to participate. We will try to bring them in. If someone chooses to form a new party, that is their choice. But if their dissatisfaction is with the Congress, we will try to address it,” he said.

Thapa also said those who contest the ongoing election but fail to win would be included in the party’s future plans. He stressed that every member of the Congress was important and that defeated candidates could be given roles in the Central Committee or other responsibilities.

Thapa cited his own experience of electoral defeat within the party, saying he had once contested from the same position and lost with very few votes before staying with the party, continuing his work and winning with a much larger vote count in a subsequent election.

He said electoral victories and defeats should be treated as a normal part of party politics, adding that losing an election should not fundamentally change political decisions.

“I do not believe that winning or losing an election should change political decisions. That would be an apolitical attitude,” Thapa said.

title.rendered: Trump honours Elon Musk with National Medal of Science, calls him ‘modern-day Thomas Edison’

content.rendered:
Washington, October 9

US President Donald Trump on Thursday honoured Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk with the National Medal of Science, praising him as a “national treasure” and a “modern-day Thomas Edison” for his contributions to space exploration, technology and innovation.

The award was presented at the White House’s Science: A New Golden Age Summit, which brought together scientists and technology leaders to discuss scientific breakthroughs, artificial intelligence and private-sector investment.

Before presenting the medal, Trump described Musk as “an industrial titan, a brilliant engineer, and one of the greatest technology founders to ever live”.

“Few Americans in history have done more to advance America’s national interest than Elon in one field after another,” Trump said. “His genius and determination have made science fiction into reality.”

Trump highlighted SpaceX’s role in advancing the US space programme, saying it had reduced NASA’s reliance on foreign countries to send astronauts into space. He also congratulated the company on the safe return of Crew-12 from the International Space Station earlier that day.

The president praised SpaceX’s Starship programme and Starlink satellite network, recalling an incident in North Carolina during which he said Starlink helped restore communications during a hurricane and contributed to saving hundreds of lives.

Trump also credited Musk’s Tesla with helping establish electric vehicles as a commercially viable alternative and advancing consumer self-driving technology. He praised Musk’s work through Neuralink and in artificial intelligence, claiming it was helping restore sight, speech and movement to people with disabilities.

“Elon is our modern-day Thomas Edison,” Trump said, congratulating Musk on his achievements.

Michael Kratsios, director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, said Musk was being recognised for “engineering achievements of extraordinary ambition and scale” that had advanced space exploration, intelligent systems, communications and manufacturing.

The recognition comes after a public fallout between Trump and Musk last year, following Musk’s departure from the Department of Government Efficiency. Musk criticised Trump’s tax-and-spending legislation, while Trump threatened to review the billionaire’s government contracts.

The two have since renewed their ties. Musk recently appeared alongside Trump at a lunch with technology leaders and was also present during Chinese President Xi Jinping’s visit. He has returned to an advisory role in the administration, co-leading the Pentagon’s Project Meridian, which examines future warfare and technologies intended to maintain US military technological superiority.

Other recipients of the National Medal of Science included Google co-founder Sergey Brin, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and AMD CEO Lisa Su. Dell Technologies CEO Michael Dell and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella received the National Medal of Technology and Innovation.

The ceremony marked the first time Trump had presented either the National Medal of Science or the National Medal of Technology and Innovation during his two presidential administrations.

Established by the US Congress in 1959, the National Medal of Science is the country’s highest recognition for scientists and engineers. It recognises outstanding contributions to physical, biological, mathematical, engineering, social and behavioural sciences in service to the nation.

The bus plunged around 200 metres down a slope at a place known as Okhle Bhir, according to police.

Police said a team had reached the hospital to collect details about the incident. Further information about the cause of the accident and the identities of the victims was not immediately available.

title.rendered: ANFA president, general secretary and two others charged over alleged financial irregularities

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, October 9

The District Government Attorney’s Office in Lalitpur has filed a case against All Nepal Football Association (ANFA) President Pankaj Bikram Nembang, General Secretary Kiran Rai and two other officials over alleged financial irregularities, including suspected collusion surrounding Nepal’s 2024 FIFA World Cup qualifying match against Bahrain.

The other defendants are ANFA Treasurer Rabindra Joshi and accounts officer Sanjiv Pandey. The case was filed at Lalitpur District Court under Section 33(g) of the National Sports Development Act, 2020, and Section 249(3)(a) of the National Penal Code, 2017.

The case follows an investigation by the Central Investigation Bureau (CIB) of Nepal Police, which concluded that ANFA’s leadership was involved in irregularities related to the Bahrain match, sports equipment procurement, FIFA World Cup tickets and sponsorship arrangements.

The allegations have not yet been established by a court.

CIB alleges collusion over Bahrain match

According to the CIB report, ANFA’s leadership played a role in making Dasharath Stadium unfit to host Nepal’s World Cup qualifying match against Bahrain in 2024.

The report says around five months remained between Nepal’s match against Yemen and the scheduled game against Bahrain. During that period, ANFA allegedly allowed non-international events to take place at the stadium, leaving the pitch unsuitable for international matches.

The CIB also said ANFA President Nembang and General Secretary Rai did not meet Asian Football Confederation (AFC) match commissioner Mindu Dorji when he visited Nepal to inspect the pitch.

The report further states that Rai had signed an agreement to hold the match in Bahrain four days before the AFC formally instructed ANFA, on March 8, 2024, to propose a neutral venue.

According to investigators, the agreement was signed without a decision from ANFA’s executive committee and without informing the Ministry of Youth and Sports or the National Sports Council (NSC). The CIB also said the delegation’s overseas trip had not received the required approval. A total of 23 players and 17 officials travelled to Bahrain.

The bureau alleged that ANFA representatives colluded with the opposing side in a manner intended to disadvantage Nepal and benefit Bahrain. It said the alleged conduct could violate Sections 31 and 32(g) of the National Sports Development Act, 2020.

$20,000 in ticket revenue unaccounted for

The CIB report says Rai and Bahrain Football Association General Secretary Rashid Al Zabi agreed that Bahrain would pay US$20,000 to ANFA as revenue from ticket sales for the match.

However, investigators found that the money had not been deposited into ANFA’s institutional account. Treasurer Joshi told investigators that he was unaware of the transaction, according to the report.

The report also found that more than Rs 3.858 million had been deposited into ANFA’s account to cover air tickets for Bahrain’s players and officials.

Irregularities alleged in equipment procurement

The CIB also concluded that ANFA suffered financial losses through the purchase of Kelme-branded sports equipment.

Under the applicable procurement rules, purchases worth more than Rs 1 million require a competitive bidding process. Investigators said ANFA did not follow that requirement.

A subcommittee formed by the NSC found that the three companies that submitted quotations — Kamaru Trading Pvt Ltd, Kamakhya Inc Pvt Ltd and Ugratara Sports Hub — were under the same ownership, raising questions about the competition and transparency of the procurement process.

According to the subcommittee’s findings, ANFA purchased sports equipment worth around Rs 140 million to Rs 150 million over the past three and a half years. The report also identified serious irregularities in the distribution of the equipment.

Questions over FIFA World Cup tickets

The CIB also found alleged irregularities in the handling of tickets for the 2026 FIFA World Cup. FIFA had provided ANFA with 330 online tickets intended for distribution among district and provincial associations, clubs, referees, coaches and players. ANFA had also corresponded with stakeholders regarding ticket purchases.

However, investigators found that ANFA did not have records detailing the prices at which the tickets were sold or the people who purchased them.

ANFA member Sarila Shrestha acknowledged taking four tickets under her name and giving them to people she did not know, according to the CIB report.

The bureau also identified alleged irregularities involving sports equipment purchases from Sherpa Outdoors and sponsorship payments linked to the company.

Four officials named as defendants

The CIB said the findings pointed to possible organised criminal intent within ANFA’s leadership. Its report attributed roles to Nembang, Rai, Joshi and Pandey in agreements made without approval from the relevant ministry and the NSC, overseas trips undertaken without authorisation, procurement through quotations and decisions allegedly contrary to the organisation’s interests.

Based on the investigation, the District Government Attorney’s Office in Lalitpur filed charges against all four officials.

Treasurer Joshi and accounts officer Pandey are in CIB custody. The government attorney’s office has asked the court to issue arrest warrants for Nembang and Rai.

Advance booking for bus tickets for Dashain travel opened on Friday, drawing crowds to ticket counters at Kathmandu’s New Bus Park.

title.rendered: Three Chinese nationals arrested with 21kg of gold in Kathmandu

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, October 9

Three Chinese nationals have been arrested after police raided a rented house in Budhanilkantha, Kathmandu, where an illegal gold processing operation was allegedly being run. Police seized around 21kg of gold from the two-and-a-half-storey house.

A team from the Crime Investigation Office in Teku raided the house on Thursday evening and found the suspects melting gold, according to police sources. A brief scuffle reportedly took place as officers moved to take them into custody.

During a search of the house, police also recovered equipment used to melt, test the purity of and mould gold into different shapes.

“They were found to be bringing in gold in both solid and liquid forms, then moulding it into different shapes as needed before supplying it,” a senior police official told Onlinekhabar.

Preliminary findings suggest the three men had been operating from the house in an organised manner, with a security gate and CCTV cameras installed on the premises, according to the official.

Investigators are yet to establish through which border points the gold was brought into Nepal, who received the supplies and whether other people were involved in the operation.

Police are also working to determine the exact quantity and purity of the seized gold, with assistance from officials of the Department of Quality and Measurement and representatives of the gold and silver traders’ association.

Police said they would hold a press conference to provide further details about the three arrested Chinese nationals, the seized gold and the investigation.

title.rendered: Probe panel recommends dismissal of APF AIG Banshiraj Dahal

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, October 9

A probe committee has recommended action against suspended Armed Police Force (APF) Additional Inspector General (AIG) Banshiraj Dahal under Rule 113 of the Armed Police Force Regulations, 2015, over allegations of conduct unbecoming of a police officer.

The one-member inquiry committee led by AIG Anjani Kumar Pokharel submitted its recommendation to Home Minister Sudan Gurung, an APF source told Onlinekhabar.

Rule 113 provides for the removal or dismissal of an APF personnel found to have acted in breach of conduct, without disqualifying them from future government service. The Home Minister has the authority to decide on the recommended action.

“The recommendation for action under Rule 113 was submitted along with a statement of around 12 to 13 pages,” an APF source said.

Banshiraj Dahal was suspended by the Home Ministry on October 5 over allegations of leaking sensitive information. The inquiry committee was formed the same day, with Pokharel given three days to investigate and recommend action.

Dahal had drawn scrutiny after visiting the Kathmandu Valley Crime Investigation Office in Teku to meet former chief justice Cholendra Shumsher Rana when Rana was in police custody.

A team from the office had arrested Rana from his Kathmandu residence on the night of September 26 and released him the following afternoon. The office said Rana had been brought to the residence after it received information about a security threat.

Dahal is also accused of having links with another alleged middleman from Jhapa and leaking confidential information.

Before his suspension, Dahal was serving as chief of the APF’s Border Department. He was due to retire at midnight on May 10, 2027, unless the government extended his tenure.

Under Rule 65(c) of the Armed Police Force Regulations, the tenure of an AIG is four years. Dahal was promoted to the rank on May 11, 2022. However, the regulations allow the government to extend an AIG’s tenure by one year on the recommendation of the APF inspector general.

The APF headquarters had recommended extending Dahal’s tenure by a year to the Home Ministry before he was suspended over the alleged leak of sensitive information.

title.rendered: Beni-Jomsom-Korala road set to reopen Monday after flood damage

content.rendered:
Myagdi, October 9

The Beni-Jomsom-Korala road, a key route linking Nepal’s only currently operational border crossing with China, is expected to reopen to traffic on Monday after extensive repairs following floods and landslides, although challenges remain in ensuring safe and smooth travel.

The 202-kilometre road, which runs from Maldhunga in Parbat through Myagdi to the Korala border point in Mustang, was severely damaged by floods and landslides between September 24 and 27.

Landslides, subsidence and river erosion damaged the road at around 50 locations, while the Kali Gandaki River washed away sections at 10 sites. Repair work is now in its final stage.

On Thursday evening, emergency vehicles were able to cross the repaired sections at Kunaunta cliff in Raghuganga Rural Municipality-2 and the approach road to the bridge at Pokharebagar in Annapurna Rural Municipality. Both locations had posed major challenges because of damage caused by the Kali Gandaki floods.

Tejaswi Sharma, chief of the Beni-Jomsom-Korala Road Project, said the road currently allows one-way passage only for vehicles carrying fuel, ambulances, equipment needed to restore road, electricity and communication services, and relief supplies.

“Initial repairs have been completed, but landslide debris still needs to be cleared, damaged and eroded sections filled, road levels adjusted and crossings constructed,” Sharma said. “Since traffic at the moment would be chaotic and pose accident risks, we plan to complete repairs by Sunday and resume traffic from Monday.”

Rs 900 million in damage, Rs 3 billion needed for reconstruction

The damage has been particularly severe along the Myagdi section, where more than 20 kilometres of the 33-kilometre stretch have been badly damaged. The section had recently been blacktopped, while concrete paving was underway in landslide-affected areas.

Narendra Subedi, chief of the Federal Road Supervision Office in Pokhara and a former head of the Beni-Jomsom-Korala road project, said the latest floods had caused the most extensive damage since the project began.

He estimated the damage at around Rs 900 million and said an additional Rs 3 billion would be required to rebuild the road under a new design.

Subedi attributed the scale of destruction to heavy rainfall, damaged feeder roads, muck dumped along the riverbanks by hydropower projects, weak geological conditions, newly formed landslides and rising flood levels in tributaries of the Kali Gandaki River.

Although the government has prioritised reopening the route within two weeks because of its importance for trade with China, restoring it to its previous condition will require substantial investment and infrastructure work, he said.

More than 500 containers stranded

The road’s reopening is particularly important ahead of Dashain and Tihar, with more than 500 containers carrying goods imported through the Korala border crossing for the Dashain season stranded at various locations in Mustang and Myagdi.

Authorities are also preparing for increased traffic linked to cargo transport, exports of Mustang apples and potatoes, and the peak tourist season.

Myagdi Chief District Officer Ganesh Gaire said officials, including security personnel and elected representatives, inspected the road on Thursday to plan traffic management.

“We have discussed prioritising essential services, freight vehicles, local traffic and tourist vehicles. Security personnel may also be deployed at narrow and dangerous stretches to prevent traffic congestion,” Gaire said.

He urged tourists planning leisure trips to Mustang to postpone their visits for a few days until road conditions improve, given the need to prioritise essential supplies, local travel and vehicles transporting apples and potatoes to market.

A joint meeting of the security committees of Myagdi and Mustang was scheduled for Friday morning to finalise plans for managing traffic once the road reopens.

title.rendered: Voting begins in Nepali Congress leadership election

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, October 9

Voting to elect the new Central Working Committee of the Nepali Congress under its 15th General Convention has begun on Friday, a day later than originally planned.

The election, initially scheduled for Thursday, was postponed due to delays in preparations. Election Committee coordinator and senior advocate Prem Bahadur Khadka said all necessary preparations had been completed, but voting was deferred to Friday morning to avoid inconveniencing voters if the process began late in the evening.

Election Committee member-secretary Raju Katuwal also cited bad weather, technical issues and the difficulties delegates would face if voting continued through the night.

A total of 7,317 convention delegates are eligible to vote. Each delegate will have to cast votes on 23 ballot papers, with the process estimated to take around 30 minutes per voter.

The Election Committee expects voting to conclude by around 3pm if it begins as scheduled.

Voting at National Assembly Hall and Khula Manch

Polling booths have been set up at the National Assembly Hall and Khula Manch along Exhibition Road in Kathmandu.

Delegates from Bagmati Province will vote at the National Assembly Hall, while representatives from the remaining six provinces and Nepali Janasamparka Samitis abroad will cast their ballots at Khula Manch.

At Khula Manch, delegates from Koshi and Madhesh provinces will vote in the Tarai-Madhesh Hall, while those from Gandaki Province will vote in the Himal Hall.

The Pahad Hall will accommodate delegates from Lumbini, Karnali and Sudurpashchim provinces, along with representatives elected through Nepali Janasamparka Samitis.

Before voting, each delegate’s identity card and name on the voter list will be verified. Only after verification will delegates be allowed to cast their ballots.

The Election Committee said ballot boxes would be collected after voting concludes and taken to the party’s central office in Sanepa, Lalitpur, where counting will begin.

title.rendered: Why flying to Delhi can cost less than flying to Dhangadhi

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, October 8

Every Dashain and Tihar, a familiar debate resurfaces on social media and in the media — why does flying to Delhi sometimes cost less than flying to Dhangadhi?

The comparison, however, often pits the lowest fare to Delhi against the highest fare to Dhangadhi, overlooking the very different economics of the two routes.

The Kathmandu–New Delhi route is served by both narrow-body and wide-body aircraft, with capacities ranging from more than 150 passengers to around 300. The route also has intense competition, allowing airlines to set fares according to market demand as they compete for passengers.

India also has lower aviation fuel prices than Nepal. Airlines operating larger aircraft can carry more passengers while paying less for fuel, allowing fares on the Delhi route to fall significantly when demand is low. During peak periods, however, fares on the same route can exceed Rs 100,000.

The situation is different on domestic routes in Nepal. Aviation fuel in Nepal currently costs Rs 249 per litre, while aircraft operating between Dhangadhi and Kathmandu generally have a maximum capacity of 72 passengers. Airlines also pay substantial fees to the Civil Aviation Authority of Nepal (CAAN).

During Dashain, the imbalance becomes more pronounced. Flights leaving Kathmandu are packed with passengers, while return flights to Kathmandu can operate with empty or only partially occupied seats. Airlines therefore offer lower fares on flights returning to the capital.

A former CAAN director general says comparing Delhi’s lowest fare with Dhangadhi’s highest fare is misleading.

“If you want to compare, compare Dhangadhi’s low fare with Delhi’s low fare,” he said. “It is not appropriate for the state to politicise airfares.”

Under Nepal’s current system, the government sets minimum and maximum airfare limits but allows airlines to determine fares within that range. Prices can therefore rise or fall depending on demand and supply.

“If you think Rs 22,000 for Dhangadhi is too high, then determine what the appropriate fare should be. Why politicise it unnecessarily?” the former director general said.

The debate has once again drawn the government into the issue. The Prime Minister’s Office said CAAN officials and representatives of domestic airlines held discussions on airfares on Thursday, with airlines being requested not to charge fares at the upper end of the permitted range.

But the government cannot simply penalise airlines or impose a different fare unless they are found to have breached the existing rules. CAAN spokesperson Gyanendra Bhul said there was no indication that airlines were charging above the maximum fares permitted by law.

That is why the dispute, which resurfaces almost every festive season, may have less to do with the airlines than with the regulatory framework itself.

The state has other options

The former CAAN director general argues that if the government believes fares charged by private airlines are too high, it has other ways to intervene.

One is to strengthen domestic operations of Nepal Airlines. The national flag carrier’s domestic service has effectively collapsed, with its two more than four-decade-old Twin Otter aircraft operating only limited flights, mainly to smaller airports.

“If the fare charged by private airlines in Dhangadhi is considered too high, why doesn’t the government operate Nepal Airlines flights to help control fares?” he asked.

The government could also use aircraft and helicopters operated by the Nepal Army if its priority is to provide cheaper air travel to the public, he said.

Airline operators, meanwhile, say a large share of the money passengers pay for tickets ultimately goes to government agencies.

According to airline companies, around 70 percent of the fare revenue goes to entities including Nepal Oil Corporation, CAAN and other government agencies. Airlines are left with around 30 percent, from which they must pay pilots and staff, operate their businesses, replace spare parts and make a profit.

“If the state ultimately wants tax revenue but also wants people to fly at lower prices, it should either reduce fuel costs or cut the charges imposed by CAAN for using airports,” the former director general said. “If the state is unwilling to give up anything, why blame the airlines alone?”

Airline operators say they are frustrated at being made the target of criticism for a problem they say is largely driven by state-imposed costs.

One airline operator told Onlinekhabar that the airfare ceiling was set when aviation fuel cost Rs 127 per litre. It has now risen to Rs 249.

“Let’s calculate the fares based on all these factors,” the operator said.

The price of the US dollar has also risen by around Rs 30 since the current airfare structure was set, the operator said, adding that this has pushed up the cost of spare parts as well.

Buddha Air says it is not charging the maximum fare

Buddha Air has separately clarified that it has not been charging the maximum permitted fare this year and accused social media users of spreading misleading information through AI-generated and Photoshop-edited material.

In a statement issued Thursday, the airline said a one-way ticket from Kathmandu to Dhangadhi was being offered for Rs 10,800. It said tickets at the minimum fare had been sold out on most flights on many days because of high demand.

Buddha said it had introduced minimum fares during the Dashain-Tihar period after devastating floods and landslides in Rasuwa severely damaged highways and disrupted road transport.

The airline said it had announced the reduced fares until road connectivity returned to normal in an effort to provide passengers with affordable air services during the disruption.

It urged passengers not to form opinions about airfares based on misleading information or screenshots circulating on social media and other unauthorised platforms, and advised them to check Buddha Air’s official sales channels, website and mobile app for fare and ticket information.

title.rendered: France’s student protests are echoing 1968 — but the politics are very different

content.rendered:
The student demonstrations that have spread across France in recent weeks are not unprecedented. Indeed, commentators have been quick to point to comparisons with the events of May and June 1968, where, at their peak, more than 10 million students and workers took to the streets.

In 1968, as now, there were legitimate reasons for protest. The unrest began at the Nanterre campus of the University of Paris, which was miles from the city centre and poorly equipped for the changing social norms of the 1960s. In particular, the ban on women and men being able to enter each other’s accommodation was the catalyst for initial demonstrations that then spread into central Paris and beyond.

Today’s parallels with the past are unmistakable. What began in September as a demonstration at the poor quality of high school (lycée) buildings in the Parisian suburbs (this time Saint-Denis) has escalated into wider protests about the conditions facing young people in France today.

In addition to the disproportionate number of missed days of teaching in underprivileged areas, students have been complaining about the appalling insulation of school buildings and the complexity of the post-school training and education application platform.

In 1968, the regime of General Charles de Gaulle came under severe pressure. De Gaulle was so convinced that he would lose control of the situation that he travelled to Germany to meet representatives of the French Army, who would be prepared to “invade” France to protect the general if required.

Despite the best efforts of de Gaulle’s prime minister, Georges Pompidou, police actions against the students, and later the millions of striking workers, were brutal. Now – as then – the police across France have also been accused of heavy-handedness, including firing tear gas directly at protesters. The use of stun grenades has been banned, after a 15-year-old reportedly lost a hand after picking one up at a protest.

Sébastian Lecornu, France’s beleaguered prime minister, has stated that he believes the students and young people have genuine concerns, while also defending the police response.

Revolt and rebellion are nothing new in France. There is a strong history of taking to the streets to protest, dating back to the revolution of 1789 via various revolutions and rebellions – in 1830, 1848, 1871 and 1944, along with many others.

No president of the current Fifth Republic has avoided some form of protest during their time in office. But what makes this wave of demonstrations so interesting is the way that political actors have sought to capitalise on events.

In May and June 1968, the Parti Communiste Français (the French Communist Party, once the biggest political party under the Fourth Republic) condemned the students as bourgeois and were slow to realise the potential of the demonstrations.

Far-left gets the 1968 spirit

By contrast, Jean-Luc Mélenchon of La France Insoumise (LFI), also on the far-left, has been quick to respond. Elected LFI representatives have joined the protests in the street and have in some cases put themselves between police and students. A savvy media operator, who in the past has used holograms to appear in multiple locations at the same time, Mélenchon has made much use of social media to garner support among the youth.

Many of the images developed by LFI and indeed by the protesters themselves have evoked the spirit of May and June 1968. One student was caught on camera with a placard proclaiming that the “6-7” Generation, after the popular meme, was “redoing” May 68.

This nostalgia for protests of the past is serving the far left rather than the political centre. Indeed, Emmanuel Macron, already the least popular president of the current Fifth Republic, is hamstrung by the political stalemate in the National Assembly caused by his own disastrous decision to call elections in June and July 2024.

Those associated with Macron and the centre, especially the two candidates most likely to represent the moderate branch of French politics, Gabriel Attal and Édouard Philippe, seem not to have caught the mood of the protests. Having both served as prime ministers under Macron, they are seen by protesters to be complicit in the declining standards in French schools.

Far-right nostalgia

Nostalgia is not limited to the far-left, though. The protests come at a time where the far-right Rassemblement National party and its presidential candidate, Marine Le Pen, continue to question accepted versions of France’s past.

Le Pen has her own appeal to young people through a protectionist economic approach. It looks to limit the power of the European Union in shaping the French economy and has always challenged the notion that the French state was responsible for atrocities during the Algerian War of Independence and the second world war.

The release of a recent film, A Man of His Time, focusing on the experiences of an “ordinary” man under the Vichy government has reignited this debate ahead of next year’s presidential elections. The four-years of Vichy rule during the Occupation of France continue to prove disturbing for the French: 76,000 Jews were deported to their deaths at the instigation of the Vichy government. https://www.youtube.com/embed/1jVoGPd7OpM?wmode=transparent&start=0 The trailer for A Man of His Time.

Importantly, this reexamining of the past appeals to a group of young people unlikely to take to the streets with Mélenchon and the far-left. Le Pen is especially convincing to a youth that is unconvinced by “wokeism” and she continues to poll well among 18-24 year olds.

It remains to be seen whether Macron and his government can do enough to address the concerns of young people in the coming weeks. If not, he and his Renaissance party – and the rest of the moderate centre – may well lose the debate when France goes to the polls in April and May 2027.

title.rendered: ICC board meeting may be held in Nepal during NPL

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, October 8

The International Cricket Council (ICC) is preparing to hold its upcoming board meeting in Nepal during the Nepal Premier League (NPL) 2026, according to Cricket Association of Nepal (CAN) Vice-President Roshan Singh.

Singh said discussions to host the ICC board meeting in Nepal during the NPL have reached an advanced stage, with only a few issues remaining before an official announcement.

“The discussions to hold the ICC board meeting in Nepal in connection with the NPL have reached a certain stage. A few things are still pending, and official information will be announced soon,” Singh said.

He said the visit of ICC representatives would not only boost cricket in Nepal but also have a positive impact on the country’s tourism sector.

Singh said the meeting could be held toward the latter part of the NPL, when only a few matches remain.

“We want to create an environment where, after seeing the cricket atmosphere here, the ICC’s perception of Nepal also changes,” he said.

The third edition of the NPL is scheduled to begin on October 26. Preparations for the tournament are currently underway at the TU Cricket Ground in Kirtipur.
