title.rendered: Durgabahadur BK: The Nepali turning Qatar’s waste into a business

content.rendered:
Even today, remembering his childhood makes Durgabahadur BK shudder. His family was so poor that having three meals a day was often a struggle. With no money to continue his education, he left school before completing his SLC and, while still a child, travelled to India in search of work.

Born in Madhuwan Municipality-3 of Bardiya, Durgabahadur had been studying at the village’s Dhanaura National Secondary School when he left for India. He went to Himachal Pradesh, where he worked as a labourer, wielding a shovel and carrying heavy loads in baskets and sacks on his back.

The money he earned was what kept his family going. His father had already died, and as the only son, much of the responsibility for the household fell on his young shoulders.

Born in 1987, Durgabahadur was not yet 14 when he first went to India in 2000. For five years, he worked among the hills of Himachal Pradesh, climbing the steep paths and stairways of Shimla and carrying loads wherever work was available. For a period, he even worked as a domestic servant in his employer’s house in Shimla.

Leaving home at such a young age and doing hard labour was not a choice he made willingly. He simply saw no alternative.

“My family’s financial condition was extremely poor. We did not have enough even for food and clothes, so I left my studies and went to India. I worked continuously for five years,” he recalls.

For another two years after those five years of continuous work in Himachal Pradesh, he travelled between India and Nepal from time to time. During that period, he was also looking for a way out of the life he had known in India.

Some people from his village were leaving for countries such as Qatar and Malaysia. Some encouraged him to leave India and look for work elsewhere.

That was when his plans began to change.He started dreaming of Qatar.

He obtained a passport, borrowed money and, in 2008, travelled to Qatar. He had been just 14 when he first left Nepal for India. By the time he left for Qatar, he was 21. But Qatar did not immediately offer him the breakthrough he had imagined.

He was still a labourer.

“I was initially paid 400 riyals a month. Then it increased to 500 and 600,” he says.

He had travelled to Qatar to work for the Lotus company. He had been told he would work as a carpenter. The reality was different. But after years of hard labour in India, he was not someone who gave up easily.

When the company needed a driver, Durgabahadur saw an opportunity.

He had handled a steering wheel while in India, although he was far from an experienced driver. Still, he took the chance. He practised driving in Qatar, gradually became more confident and eventually obtained his driving licence.

That licence changed his earnings overnight. His salary rose to 1,000 riyals.

For someone who had been earning around 550 riyals, doubling his income was an extraordinary moment.

“The day I received a salary of 1,000 riyals instead of around 550, I was so happy that I could not even sleep,” he recalls.

He remained with Lotus for eight years, until 2016, working as a driver. Then he moved to another company that was looking for a salesperson-driver for its water business.

His career was beginning to move beyond the jobs he had first taken simply to survive.

The company’s management had noticed his honesty and dedication. Although he had been hired as a driver and salesperson, the managing director gradually entrusted him with greater responsibility. He became a senior storekeeper and eventually rose to become a supervisor.

For Durgabahadur, it was proof that the years of hard work had not been wasted.

The boy who had once carried loads through the streets of India and worked in his employer’s household had become a company supervisor.

“I have been shaped by hard work. I have reached where I am through dedication and labour. My difficult past brought me to where I am today. I am proud of my past,” he says.

By then, he had experienced almost every rung of the working life he had once known only as survival — from porter to driver, salesperson to storekeeper and finally supervisor.

And another thought began to take shape.

Working for someone else would only take him so far. If he wanted to build something of his own, he would have to take the risk himself.

There was just one problem. He had no money. Whatever he earned was largely spent on his daily needs and sent home to his family. Still, he refused to let that stop him.

He borrowed 1,000 riyals and started working on his own.

That small loan would become the starting point of a business that would eventually make him a millionaire and create jobs for dozens of people in Qatar.

His first venture involved municipal waste-management supplies. He supplied dustbins, plastic products and other materials needed for waste collection, buying and selling the items according to demand.

“I delivered whatever was needed in different areas. I worked according to the demand,” he says.

The business grew quickly. According to Durgabahadur, it reached monthly sales of around 250,000 riyals.

As competitors entered the market, he began looking for another opportunity.

Because he had already been working closely with municipalities, he saw an opening in waste management itself.

In 2020, he established a waste-management company. This time, he moved beyond supplying materials. He began handling waste collection and management directly.

He bought vehicles for the business, including one that he says cost 370,000 riyals. He says some of the vehicles were purchased from Switzerland.

Today, he says his company operates 17 vehicles.

They collect and manage waste in the Al Rayyan and Al Daayen areas of Qatar. He has also opened his own garage to maintain the vehicles.

Across the business, he says he now employs 37 people.

Every day, his company manages between 50 and 60 tonnes of waste, according to Durgabahadur.

The scale of the business is a striking contrast to where he began.

Yet he says he still works between 18 and 20 hours a day.

He does not see the contrast between his childhood poverty and his present circumstances as something that should make him bitter.

Instead, he sees the hardship as the foundation of everything that came later.

“My past made me strong. The struggles I went through made me more responsible. I am standing where I am today on the foundation of yesterday,” he says.

He says Qatar’s employment market began facing difficulties after 2022. But his company, which works in cleaning and waste management, was less affected.

For now, his business is in Qatar. But his long-term plans are closer to home.

Durgabahadur says he wants to return to his village and eventually build his life there.

His mother, wife and three children currently live in the village. The family occasionally visits him in Qatar before returning home, and he also travels back when he can.

He has never moved his family permanently to Kathmandu or another city. Nor does he plan to settle them in Qatar.

“I want to return to the village and do something there,” he says.

For a man who left that village at 14 carrying little more than the burden of his family’s survival, the idea of returning home is perhaps the next chapter in a journey that began with a shovel in the hills of India and eventually led to a business of his own in Qatar.

title.rendered: Milei renews Argentina’s Falklands claim at UN, calls for ‘peaceful solution’

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, September 24

Argentine President Javier Milei has renewed his country’s claim to sovereignty over the Falkland Islands, known as the Malvinas in Argentina, calling for negotiations with Britain to resolve the long-running dispute.

Addressing the United Nations General Assembly in New York on Wednesday, Milei described the Malvinas as a “national cause” for Argentina and urged Britain to resume talks over the sovereignty of the islands.

“The Malvinas for us is a national cause,” Milei said, accusing the United Nations of failing to enforce resolutions calling on both sides to avoid unilateral actions while the dispute remains unresolved.

He said the issue was not only a dispute between Argentina and the United Kingdom but also a test of the UN’s ability to enforce its own resolutions.

“The Malvinas issue is not merely a matter between Argentina and the United Kingdom,” Milei said. “It is also a question regarding this organization’s ability to enforce its own resolutions.”

Dispute intensifies

Milei has stepped up Argentina’s focus on the islands in recent weeks, following criticism of his closer ties with Britain and his stated admiration for former British Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher.

Thatcher led Britain during the 1982 Falklands War, which began after Argentina’s military government invaded the islands. Britain sent a task force to the South Atlantic and regained control of the islands after 73 days.

The conflict killed 649 Argentine and 255 British military personnel.

Earlier this month, Milei announced measures aimed at stopping an oil project near the British-controlled islands. He also praised US President Donald Trump for saying Washington could reconsider its longstanding neutral position on the sovereignty dispute.

Argentina’s government last week introduced a security bill that would increase penalties for companies exploiting natural resources around the islands without Argentine authorisation. The proposed legislation would also establish a national security council chaired by Milei and expand the military’s role in protecting critical infrastructure.

Milei used his UN address to intensify his criticism of the international body.

“Today I come to say that Argentina will not sit and wait for the UN and the international community to live up to their own mandate,” he said.

He also accused the UN of becoming an ineffective organisation dominated by what he called arrogant bureaucrats.

Britain says it will stand firm

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham also addressed the dispute during the UN General Assembly week, saying Britain’s position remained unchanged.

“We will defend the right of the Falkland Islanders to self-determination and to remain British,” Burnham told reporters after meeting Trump on the sidelines of the UN gathering on Tuesday.

He said Britain would “stand firm” in response to any threats.

Trump said in August that he was reviewing the United States’ neutral position on the islands while criticising Britain over its support for the US war against Iran.

The Falkland Islands, known as the Malvinas in Argentina, are an archipelago of about 3,500 people in the South Atlantic, around 480 kilometres east of Argentina’s southeastern coast.

Britain has controlled the islands since 1833, while Argentina continues to claim sovereignty over them.

In a 2013 referendum, 99.8 percent of voters on the islands backed remaining a British overseas territory, with only three votes cast against.

title.rendered: Sita Air plane loses wheel while landing at Jufal Airport; all 13 passengers safe

content.rendered:
Dolpa, September 24

A wheel came off a Sita Air plane while it was landing at Jufal Airport in Dolpa.

The aircraft, carrying 13 passengers from Nepalgunj, lost one of its rear right-side wheels during landing.

Chief District Officer Junu Hamal Dhakal said there was a minor issue with the wheel and that everyone was safe.

The plane is currently on the runway, and technicians are inspecting it, she said.

DSP Anil Raj Giri of the District Police Office, Dolpa, said the rear wheel came off during landing at around 8:25 this morning.

According to him, the plane was carrying 13 passengers,7 foreigners and 6 Nepalis, including 11 men and two women. All of them are safe, DSP Giri said.

title.rendered: Heavy rain risk persists as Bay of Bengal weather system weakens

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, September 24

The deep depression that has developed over the Bay of Bengal is likely to weaken gradually after the next 24 hours, but its influence is expected to continue bringing heavy to very heavy rainfall to parts of Nepal, the Meteorological Forecasting Division said.

Meteorologists have warned that the ongoing rainfall could affect normal life and urged people in areas vulnerable to floods and landslides to maintain high alert.

The weather system has already brought rain to many parts of the country since early Thursday morning. Meteorologist David Dhakal said the intensity and coverage of rainfall were expected to increase further on Thursday.

The Meteorological Forecasting Division has advised people to exercise caution in flood- and landslide-prone areas and avoid travelling at night as far as possible.

The department has also warned of the possibility of heavy snowfall in high Himalayan areas.

Which districts face higher risks?

The division released a four-day risk map on Wednesday evening based on its five-day weather forecast.

For Thursday, orange alert has been issued for eastern hill districts of Koshi, Bagmati and Gandaki provinces and eastern hill districts of Lumbini Province. Orange indicates a potentially hazardous situation requiring caution.

Yellow alert has been issued for the Terai districts of Koshi, Madhesh, Bagmati, Gandaki and Lumbini provinces, as well as some districts in Karnali Province. People in these areas have been advised to remain updated on weather conditions.

The risk is expected to increase on Friday.

On Friday, red alert has been issued for high Himalayan areas of Koshi, Bagmati and Gandaki provinces, indicating the need for response and preparedness.

The districts under the red alert are Taplejung, Sankhuwasabha, Solukhumbu, Ramechhap, Dolakha, Sindhupalchok, Rasuwa, Dhading, Gorkha, Manang and Mustang.

Yellow alert has been issued for Jhapa, Morang and Sunsari in Koshi Province and Saptari, Siraha, Dhanusha, Mahottari, Sarlahi, Rautahat, Bara and Parsa in Madhesh Province.

The department revised its earlier risk assessment for five districts in Sudurpaschim. Kailali, Kanchanpur, Doti, Dadeldhura and Baitadi, which were marked orange on Wednesday evening, have been placed under yellow alert in the latest update.

Karnali, Sudurpaschim face higher risk on Saturday

The risk is expected to shift towards Karnali and Sudurpaschim provinces on Saturday.

The department has placed Dolpa, Jajarkot, Jumla, Mugu, Kalikot, Bajura, Bajhang, Humla and Darchula under red alert.

Orange alert has been issued for Lamjung, Kaski, Syangja, Parbat, Baglung, Myagdi, Palpa, Nawalparasi West, Rupandehi, Kapilvastu, Arghakhanchi, Gulmi, Pyuthan, Dang, Rolpa, Rukum East, Rukum West, Banke, Bardiya, Salyan, Surkhet, Dailekh, Kailali, Kanchanpur, Achham, Doti, Dadeldhura and Baitadi.

Rainfall is expected to decrease somewhat on Sunday compared with Thursday, Friday and Saturday.

On Sunday, yellow alert has been issued for all districts west of Bagmati Province, while all districts in Koshi, Madhesh and Bagmati provinces have been marked green.

Yellow indicates that there is no significant risk but people should remain updated on weather conditions.

Weather system weakening

The weather system developed as a deep depression over the west-central Bay of Bengal and adjoining northwestern areas.

The system crossed the coast near the area southwest of Kalingapatnam, between Visakhapatnam and Gopalpur in India, and moved across northern Andhra Pradesh and adjoining southern Odisha.

The India Meteorological Department has said the system is likely to move north-northwestwards and gradually weaken over the next 24 hours.

Nepal’s Meteorological Forecasting Division has also said in its latest bulletin that the system is expected to gradually weaken after the next 24 hours.

However, meteorologist Dhakal said the system could continue to cause heavy rainfall in parts of Nepal, increasing the risk of floods and landslides in vulnerable areas.

The division has warned that rainfall could trigger soil erosion, floods, landslides and debris flows, while urban and Tarai areas could face inundation. Rising water levels in major and minor rivers and streams could also disrupt daily life, agriculture, health, tourism, construction activities near rivers, roads and air transport.

The department has also warned of the possibility of heavy snowfall in mountainous areas and urged mountaineers and others staying in the high Himalayas to exercise heightened caution.

The Meteorological Forecasting Division said it was continuously monitoring the weather system and would update forecasts and warnings as conditions change. It has urged the public and concerned agencies to regularly follow official weather forecasts and alerts.

title.rendered: Nepal Rastra Bank to issue new Rs 1000 notes from Friday

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, September 24

Nepal Rastra Bank is set to put new Rs 1,000 banknotes into circulation from Friday.

According to the Currency Management Department of Nepal Rastra Bank, the new notes will be brought into circulation from Friday.

The new Rs 1,000 notes will retain the same dimensions as the existing notes but will feature a different colour scheme. The notes will be light green with a purple border, according to the central bank.

The front of the note features an image of Mount Everest on the left and a rhododendron watermark on the right. A watermark bearing the numeral “1000” is placed below it.

The central section of the note features images of two rare twin elephants, Ram and Laxman, born to an elephant named Devkali at the government-owned elephant breeding centre in Chitwan.

The new Rs 1,000 notes belong to the 2025 series and carry serial numbers ranging from 92000001 to 50999999.

The central bank said only notes bearing serial numbers from 68000001 to 91440000 from the previous 2019 series, which was introduced into circulation on July 22, 2020, had been issued.

The new notes will circulate alongside existing Rs 1,000 notes.

title.rendered: Prithvi Highway resumes two-way traffic after landslides cleared

content.rendered:
Dhading, September 24

The Prithvi Highway has resumed two-way traffic after landslides at two locations in Dhading were cleared, police said.

According to the District Police Office, Dhading, debris from landslides near Krishnabhir in Benighat Rorang Rural Municipality-7 and at a place called Jyamire in Ward No. 9 was removed, allowing vehicles to operate in both directions.

The highway had been reduced to one-way traffic on Friday morning after continuous rainfall triggered landslides carrying mud and debris at the two locations.

The Prithvi Highway had only recently reopened after being blocked for 18 days following major floods in the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli rivers on August 26 and 30.

The floods damaged and washed away sections of the highway at Krishnabhir, disrupting one of Nepal’s major road links between Kathmandu and the western districts.

A new track was opened at Krishnabhir, and the highway was brought back into operation from September 17.

Authorities have continued to monitor the highway as rainfall increases the risk of further landslides and road disruptions in the area.

title.rendered: PM Shah to meet Guterres before addressing UN General Assembly

content.rendered:
New York, September 23

Prime Minister Balendra Shah has arrived in New York to attend the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly.

Shah was welcomed upon arrival by Nepal’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Ambassador Lok Bahadur Thapa, Acting Nepali Ambassador to the United States Sharad Raj Aran, and Consul General of Nepal in New York Dadhiram Bhandari.

Shah is leading the Nepali high-level delegation to the General Assembly. His team includes Chief Adviser Kumar Ben, among other officials.

Considerable interest has been generated over what Shah will say in his address to the General Assembly, as this will be his first appearance at the UN’s largest annual gathering since becoming prime minister.

There is also interest in who Shah will meet — and who he will not meet — during his stay in New York.

According to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Shah is scheduled to address the high-level general debate of the General Assembly on September 24.

Before addressing the General Assembly, Shah is also scheduled to meet UN Secretary-General António Guterres, according to a source close to the prime minister.

The meeting with Guterres has been scheduled ahead of Shah’s address to the General Assembly.

Eighteen heads of state or government are scheduled to address the General Assembly during the daytime session on Thursday. Shah is 17th on the speakers’ list.

The General Assembly has allocated 15 minutes for each speaker. However, heads of government are not strictly required to conclude their addresses within that time.

“Some leaders speak for longer while others finish within 15 minutes,” a source said. “Accordingly, Prime Minister Shah’s turn is expected to come at around 4 or 5am Nepal time on Friday.”

The most important high-level segment of the UN General Assembly began in New York on Tuesday.

UN Secretary-General Guterres, US President Donald Trump and General Assembly President Annalena Baerbock were among those who addressed the opening session.

Shah’s address comes as Nepal faces growing impacts from climate-related disasters.

Nepal has been seeking greater international attention to the challenges faced by climate-vulnerable countries and discussions over climate justice and the rights of countries suffering disproportionate losses from climate change.

According to sources familiar with the prime minister’s preparations, Shah is expected to use his address to highlight the damage Nepal has suffered from climate-related disasters and press the case for the rights and interests of vulnerable countries.

The prime minister’s decision to attend the General Assembly is particularly significant because he had initially indicated after taking office that he would not undertake foreign visits for a year.

He later decided to travel to New York following the devastating floods in the Bhotekoshi area, with the government saying he would use the international forum to raise Nepal’s concerns over climate change and climate justice.

title.rendered: PM Balen Shah likely to visit India in third week of November

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, September 24

Prime Minister Balendra Shah is expected to visit India in the third week of November, with preparations for the visit set to begin after Shah and Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal return from New York, according to sources familiar with the matter.

The exact date has not yet been finalised, but discussions between Nepal and India have progressed to the point where the visit is being planned for the third week of November, a source told Onlinekhabar.

Shah and Khanal are currently in New York to attend the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly.

The two sides also discussed Shah’s proposed India visit during a meeting between Khanal and Indian External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York.

The meeting was described as a courtesy call, with the ministers holding only preliminary discussions on the possible agenda for Shah’s visit.

“The meeting was a courtesy call, so there was no detailed discussion. However, preparations will move ahead rapidly once the delegation returns home,” the source said.

Foreign Ministry spokesperson Lok Bahadur Chhetri said preparations were underway to arrange the visit at a mutually convenient time, but that the date had not yet been fixed.

Shah is understood to want the visit to result in some concrete outcomes.

Among the issues expected to feature in discussions are the longstanding Nepal-India border dispute and India’s approval for flight routes to and from Gautam Buddha International Airport in Bhairahawa.

“The prime minister wants the visit to create a concrete foundation by reaching agreement on at least one of these issues,” the source said.

India had formally confirmed in July that it had invited Shah to visit the country. Indian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said on July 28 that an invitation had been extended to the Nepali prime minister.

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi had also invited Shah to visit India in his congratulatory message after Shah assumed office on March 27. Shah had responded that he would visit India at an appropriate time.

Preparations for the visit have been underway for several months. Shah’s chief political adviser Kumar Byanjankar is also reported to have made an unofficial visit to India in late June in connection with preparations for the proposed visit.

Khanal and Jaishankar had earlier discussed Shah’s India visit during Khanal’s official visit to India in June. During that visit, the two sides held extensive discussions on trade and economic cooperation, connectivity, energy, water resources and people-to-people ties.

According to the Nepali side, the government had proposed first reviewing Nepal’s foreign policy and the various dimensions of Nepal-India relations before setting the date for a high-level visit. It had also proposed identifying bilateral priorities and using existing bilateral mechanisms for further discussions.

Nepal and India have more than 40 bilateral mechanisms covering different areas of cooperation. Sources said the two countries have agreed to activate these mechanisms and intensify bilateral engagement.

The agreement to strengthen these mechanisms was also discussed during the Khanal-Jaishankar meeting in New York, according to sources.

Shah had initially said after becoming prime minister in March that he would not undertake foreign visits for a year. He had also indicated that he would not attend the UN General Assembly.

However, following the devastating floods in the Bhotekoshi area, Shah decided to travel to New York, saying he would use the international platform to raise the issue of climate justice.

His proposed India visit would therefore become his first bilateral foreign visit since taking office. India has been among the countries maintaining high-level engagement with the new government, with Indian Ambassador Naveen Srivastava reminding Shah in August of Modi’s invitation to visit India.

title.rendered: Work on BP Highway upgrading to be suspended amid heavy rain forecast

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, September 23

The government is preparing to suspend ongoing upgrading work on the BP Highway for a few days in view of the forecast of heavy rainfall across various parts of the country.

Minister for Infrastructure Development Sunil Lamsal said preparations were underway to halt track construction work on the highway temporarily, citing the risks posed by heavy rain, landslides and other weather-related hazards.

“The decision to suspend construction work for a few days has been made in light of potential rainfall, landslides and other challenges that could affect the road,” Lamsal said.

He said the temporary suspension was intended to minimise potential risks and ensure safer and smoother traffic movement along the highway.

Lamsal also urged travellers and the general public to exercise caution while travelling, particularly as heavy rain could increase the risk of landslides and other hazards.

He advised the public to avoid unnecessary travel and not to take risks in areas that could be affected by adverse weather conditions.

content.rendered:
Pokhara, September 23

Flydubai has started commercial flights from Pokhara Regional International Airport, with its first flight arriving from Dubai on Wednesday carrying 113 passengers.

The Flydubai aircraft landed at the airport with 113 passengers on board. It is scheduled to depart for Dubai with 153 passengers.

The aircraft was given a ceremonial water-cannon welcome after landing at the airport.

Local residents also gathered at the airport to welcome the passengers arriving on the inaugural commercial flight. Relatives and family members of some passengers were also present to receive them.

The launch of Flydubai’s regular service has raised hopes of strengthening international connectivity from Pokhara and increasing the flow of international passengers through the airport.

title.rendered: Daily Digest: The biggest stories, developments and updates of the day

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, September 23

There is a lot happening every day. The Daily Digest brings together some of the most important stories and developments in one place—from Nepal’s latest affairs to international news, business, sports and stories that deserve a closer look.

Nepal’s public debt nears Rs 3 trillion, while debt payments outpace capital spending

Nepal’s public debt has reached nearly Rs 3 trillion, even as the government’s total debt burden declined slightly in the first two months of the current fiscal year. According to the Public Debt Management Office, Nepal owed Rs 2.973 trillion by the end of Bhadra, the second month of the fiscal year 2026/27. The figure is slightly lower than the Rs 2.981 trillion recorded at the end of the previous fiscal year.

Egg prices rise again, large eggs cost Rs 600 per crate

Egg prices have increased again in the market. The Nepal Layers Poultry Farmers Association said the price of eggs has increased by Rs 10 to Rs 15 per crate, effective from Tuesday. According to the price list issued by the association, the depot and dealer price for extra-large eggs has been set at Rs 4,300 per box, while the price of large eggs has been fixed at Rs 4,200 per box.

Madhesh government begins printing and distributing driving licences itself

The Madhesh provincial government has started printing and distributing driving licences on its own, aiming to reduce the long waiting time faced by service recipients. The Ministry of Labour and Transport of Madhesh printed 3,081 driving licences in its first batch and handed them over to transport management offices under the provincial government for distribution.

Manaslu season ends without a summit as bad weather forces climbers to turn back

Climbers who arrived in the Himalayas with dreams of standing atop Mount Manaslu have returned without reaching the summit this autumn, after persistent snowfall, strong winds and growing avalanche risks made further attempts increasingly dangerous.

Government steps up preparedness for heavy rainfall, puts security forces on high alert

The government has stepped up preparations to deal with the risks of floods and landslides that could result from possible heavy rainfall, with plans to continuously monitor river conditions and potential disasters and provide the public with hourly updates.

Brokerages step up margin lending as 11 firms begin offering the service

Brokerage companies in Nepal have started expanding margin lending services, allowing investors to purchase shares by contributing part of the required amount and borrowing the rest from their brokers.

Government moves to allocate 2% hydropower IPOs to serving security personnel

The government has initiated the process to allow serving security personnel to participate in initial public offerings (IPOs) of hydropower projects.

Speaking at the House of Representatives meeting on Wednesday, Minister for Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation Biraj Bhakta Shrestha said legal procedures were being advanced to ensure that serving security personnel receive a two per cent share in hydropower project IPOs in recognition of their contribution during disasters.

Free education up to Bachelor’s level for Gen-Z Movement martyrs’ families and injured

The government has decided to provide free education up to the bachelor’s level to the families of martyrs of the Gen-Z movement and those who were seriously or critically injured. According to the Guidelines for Providing Free Education to Families of Martyrs and the Injured of the Gen-Z Movement, 2083, prepared by the Ministry of Education and Sports, beneficiaries include the children and siblings of martyrs, as well as holders of IDs certifying serious or critical injuries.

title.rendered: Manaslu season ends without a summit as bad weather forces climbers to turn back

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, September 22

Climbers who arrived in the Himalayas with dreams of standing atop Mount Manaslu have returned without reaching the summit this autumn, after persistent snowfall, strong winds and growing avalanche risks made further attempts increasingly dangerous.

With weather conditions deteriorating, expedition teams have chosen to put safety before the summit and begin their journey home.

“Mountains will always be there, but life comes first,” said Furte Sherpa of Satori Adventures. “Once it became clear that the safest decision was to turn back because of the weather, our team decided to return home safely.”

Writing about the decision, Sherpa urged climbers still in the mountains to remain strong and trust their judgment.

“No summit is worth putting your life at risk,” he said, adding that the teams would return to Manaslu in 2027.

The Summit Force team also reported that strong winds and continuous snowfall had forced climbers to reconsider their summit plans and descend from Camps 1 and 2 to base camp.

Miles Sherpa of the team said an approaching late-monsoon weather system could deposit more snow on a mountain that was already facing a significant avalanche threat.

Climbers forced to abandon summit plans

Nangsyal Chhoden, who reached Camp 3 on Manaslu, said climbers had been forced to turn back after the weather failed to improve for nearly two weeks.

“We had to return because the weather did not cooperate. If we are alive, the mountain can wait,” Chhoden said.

By Tuesday, climbers who had reached Camp 3 had descended to base camp, while many began returning towards Samagaun on Wednesday morning.

“The base camp is almost empty now,” Chhoden said. “Some climbers and Sherpa teams are packing up their tents. We are also preparing to descend to Samagaun.”

According to Chhoden, apart from some members of the rope-fixing team, most climbers were unable to attempt the summit this season.

Some expedition companies may still consider an attempt in October, he said, but most climbers are already preparing to return to Kathmandu.

American climber Charlie Engle, who had been preparing for the Manaslu expedition, said many people were descending from the mountain while rescue operations were still continuing for some who were unable to make their way down independently.

“Looking at the weather, it seems we may have to wait another week or 10 days,” Engle said. “For now, we are waiting, watching the weather and trying to understand what is happening before making a decision.”

‘This year’s snowfall is unlike anything I have seen’

Prabal Lama, who was at base camp, said another summit attempt later in the same season was unlikely.

Climbers arriving from different countries face visa limitations, while expedition equipment, guides and Sherpa staff would also have to be mobilised again, making it difficult for teams to return after leaving the region.

“I have been coming to Manaslu since 2012, but I have never seen rainfall and snowfall as heavy as this year,” Lama said.

Manaslu Base Camp, where rainfall is generally limited, has experienced continuous rain for nearly two weeks, according to Bir Bahadur Lama of Samagaun.

He said hotels in Samagaun had become crowded with climbers returning from base camp.

“Some are preparing to walk back through the Manaslu Circuit, while most are returning by helicopter,” he said.

Five feet of new snow raises avalanche concerns

The 8,163-metre Manaslu is considered a technically demanding peak with significant avalanche exposure.

Its climbing routes include glaciated terrain, an active icefall between Camps 1 and 2, and steep slopes and seracs in the higher sections.

Following several days of unexpectedly heavy snowfall, around five feet of new snow has accumulated in parts of the mountain, significantly changing climbing conditions.

The route between Camps 3 and 4 is considered particularly exposed to avalanche danger.

A recent avalanche has also affected members of the rope-fixing team.

With another major weather system expected to enter Nepal around October 8 and 9, expedition operators have made the difficult decision to end their Manaslu summit attempts for this season.

The decision comes despite unusually high interest in Manaslu this year. Around 500 climbers had obtained permits to attempt the world’s eighth-highest mountain, while around 500 Nepali high-altitude guides and support staff had travelled to the region.

A total of 493 climbers received permits this year, compared with 410 last year.

Last year, climbers from 67 countries, organised into 41 expedition groups, generated Rs 224.814 million in government revenue through Manaslu climbing permits.

The mountain can wait

The decision to turn back has been framed by expedition teams not as a failure to summit, but as a recognition of the risks posed by rapidly changing conditions in the high Himalayas.

Snowfall, rainfall, wind speed and the stability of the mountain can change quickly, making judgment and timing critical during an expedition.

Previous seasons have also shown the consequences of deteriorating conditions. In autumn 2012, 11 climbers were killed on Manaslu after an avalanche struck a camp.

This year, however, expedition teams have chosen to withdraw before attempting to push higher into increasingly unstable terrain.

Himalaya Summit Club similarly told its climbers that returning safely should be considered an achievement in itself.

“Not every success is reaching the summit,” the club said. “Sometimes, returning home safely is the greatest achievement.”

The message was accompanied by a simple farewell to the mountain — and a promise to return.

“Thank you, Manaslu, for teaching us another lesson in humility, patience and respect for nature,” the club said. “See you again in 2027.”

title.rendered: Madhesh government begins printing and distributing driving licences itself

content.rendered:
Janakpur, September 23

The Madhesh provincial government has started printing and distributing driving licences on its own, aiming to reduce the long waiting time faced by service recipients.

The Ministry of Labour and Transport of Madhesh printed 3,081 driving licences in its first batch and handed them over to transport management offices under the provincial government for distribution.

Madhesh has eight transport management offices. Of the licences printed in the first batch, 1,172 are for the Birgunj Transport Management Office, 932 for Janakpur, 460 for Lahan, 303 for Bardibas, 119 for Gaur, 52 for Rajbiraj, 32 for Malangwa and 11 for Kalaiya.

Minister for Labour and Transport Sharada Devi Thapa handed over the printed licences to Basudev Malla, chief of the Janakpur Transport Management Office, during a press conference held at the ministry.

Thapa instructed the transport offices to distribute the licences to service recipients as soon as possible.

She said the provincial government’s decision to print licences itself would reduce the waiting period for people who have already completed the required procedures.

“Now that the Madhesh government has started printing and distributing licences itself, service recipients will not have to wait for a long time,” Thapa said.

The ministry’s acting secretary Ranjit Yadav and other officials were also present at the press conference.

The provincial government said the move is aimed at making driving licence distribution more efficient and reducing delays in the service.

title.rendered: Bodies of 2 climbers brought to Kathmandu

content.rendered:
Gorkha, September 23

The bodies of two people who died after being buried in an avalanche at the base of Mt Manaslu have been brought to Kathmandu. The District Police Office in Gorkha said the bodies were airlifted from Chumunubri-1 in Samagaun to Kathmandu by helicopter on Wednesday morning.

Dhruvjyoti Guha, a German citizen of Indian origin, and his companion, Phursemba Sherpa of Makalu-2, Sankhuwasabha, died after being buried in an avalanche at the mountain’s third camp last Sunday night. Their bodies were brought to Samagaun three days after the incident, on Tuesday.

From there, they were airlifted to Teaching Hospital in Maharajgunj, Kathmandu, early Wednesday morning, said DSP Raj Kumar Shrestha.

The two had joined a mountaineering expedition organised by Makalu Adventure Company Pvt. Ltd.

With their deaths, the number of people who have died on Mt Manaslu this season has reached four. Earlier, 50-year-old Singaporean climber Lauwi Seng died at the second camp. Similarly, 20-year-old Nepali assistant Tasi Sherpa died at the base camp.

This season, 493 foreign climbers have obtained permits to climb Mt Manaslu, also known as Killer Mountain. However, no climber has successfully summited the mountain so far this season due to bad weather.

Heavy snowfall and continuous rainfall have forced climbers to return to Kathmandu.

title.rendered: Tourism Department issues advisory for trekkers, mountaineers as heavy rain forecast

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, September 23

The Department of Tourism has issued a safety advisory for trekkers, mountaineers and support staff amid forecasts of heavy rainfall across Nepal later this week.

The department issued the advisory on Wednesday, urging climbers and trekkers who have already reached Himalayan destinations or are travelling there for the autumn season to remain alert and plan their activities according to the weather forecast.

According to the Nepal weather bulletin, heavy rainfall accompanied by thunderstorms, lightning and strong winds is possible across the country from Friday, September 25, to Sunday, September 27.

The forecast has also raised the risk of landslides, floods and soil erosion, while snowfall is possible in high-altitude areas.

The department said the adverse weather could affect trekking routes and mountaineering activities and advised people to avoid travelling during the period wherever possible.

Those who need to travel have been urged to do so with heightened caution and by taking the latest weather conditions into account.

The department has also asked trekkers, climbers and expedition organisers to review their plans based on weather forecasts and make necessary arrangements in advance.

It has particularly called on health facilities in areas where trekking and mountaineering permits have been issued, including Samagaun in Gorkha, the Khumbu region and Manang, to ensure uninterrupted and accessible medical services.

Health facilities in Kathmandu and Pokhara that provide treatment for altitude-related illnesses have also been asked to remain prepared and provide services without disruption.

The Department of Hydrology and Meteorology continues to monitor rainfall, flooding and other weather-related risks through its warning and monitoring systems.

The advisory comes as Nepal enters the autumn trekking and mountaineering season, when thousands of domestic and international visitors travel to the country’s mountain and trekking destinations.

title.rendered: Government steps up preparedness for heavy rainfall, puts security forces on high alert

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, September 23

The government has stepped up preparations to deal with the risks of floods and landslides that could result from possible heavy rainfall, with plans to continuously monitor river conditions and potential disasters and provide the public with hourly updates.

The early warning system has been strengthened as most parts of the country are forecast to receive heavy rainfall from September 24 to 26 as part of preparations for disaster risk reduction and response.

According to Dharmaraj Upreti, executive chief of the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority, river water levels and risks will be monitored in real time through continuous coordination with the Department of Hydrology and Meteorology and the Flood Forecasting Division.

He said information would be updated every hour based on technical analysis of when rivers could reach dangerous levels and the possible impacts.

“We will update the early warning system and monitor the situation every hour. We are coordinating with the Flood Forecasting Division to determine when a river could reach a dangerous level and what impact it could have,” he said. “We monitor rainfall in real time. Citizens will receive SMS alerts on their mobile phones, so I urge them to take these alerts seriously.”

The authority is also directly monitoring the development of a major storm system forming over the sea and the possibility of changes in its direction.

A red alert has been issued for the high Himalayan areas in view of the possibility of heavy snowfall, as weather conditions could change rapidly.

Moderate to heavy rainfall has been forecast in the mid-hill and lower coastal areas.

In view of the risks, tourists in vulnerable Himalayan and hilly areas have been urged to immediately move to safer locations. Travel agencies have also been advised not to accept new bookings and to remain alert and make preparations for helicopter flights.

The authority said vehicular movement on highways and roads could be completely prohibited if the disaster risk increases. According to Executive Chief Upreti, preparations are underway to urge passengers not to travel unless absolutely necessary on Friday and Saturday and to ask transport operators not to operate services.

Dozers have been kept on standby along major highways to clear roads immediately in case of landslides.

As rainfall could cause significant damage to the agricultural sector, farmers have been urged to take special precautions to protect ripened paddy crops in the fields and stored grain. The Ministry of Agriculture has already issued a separate advisory on the matter.

The authority has also strongly warned the public against risking their lives by filming videos, making TikTok content or posting material on social media during floods.

Upreti urged people not to enter rivers to collect firewood or other materials carried downstream by floods, saying such activities could be dangerous.

Security agencies across the country have been placed on high alert, while preparations for real-time monitoring of weather conditions and disaster response have been intensified through command posts involving chief district officers (CDOs) from all 77 districts.

title.rendered: Brokerages step up margin lending as 11 firms begin offering the service

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, September 23

Brokerage companies in Nepal have started expanding margin lending services, allowing investors to purchase shares by contributing part of the required amount and borrowing the rest from their brokers.

According to the Nepal Stock Exchange (NEPSE), 11 brokerage companies have so far started providing margin trading services.

The companies are NASA Securities (58), Trishakti Securities (48), Imperial Securities (45), Aryatara Investment and Securities (57), Crystal Kanchanjunga Securities (50), Nepal Stock House (14), Dakshinkali Investment and Securities (33), Vision Securities (34), Dipshikha Securities (38), Sunny Securities (42), and Kalash Stock Market (74).

Another 50 brokerage companies have started the process of launching the service, while around a dozen have already obtained approval to conduct margin trading.

Under margin trading, investors contribute a portion of the amount required to purchase shares, while the broker lends the remaining amount.

At present, brokers generally finance up to 70 percent of the purchase value. This means investors can contribute 30 percent of the amount and borrow the remaining 70 percent from the broker.

More investors turning to broker-based lending

Madan Paudel, managing director of NASA Securities, said the company has already extended around Rs 1.25 billion in margin loans.

“Margin trading is increasing. Borrowing directly from brokers is quicker and more convenient, while the fees and interest rates are not very high,” he said.

According to Paudel, the introduction of margin lending has made it easier for investors to access funds for share purchases.

The system also differs from taking a loan from a bank against existing shares.

When shares are pledged as collateral for a bank loan, investors generally have to repay the loan and release the collateral before selling those shares. Under margin trading, however, investors do not have to pledge their existing shares and can sell the shares purchased through the facility when they choose, subject to the applicable margin requirements.

Paudel said margin lending could increase significantly as the stock market expands. Brokers also expect the facility to help reduce the problem of credit transactions within brokerage firms.

The margin lending period has been set at one year.

Brokerage operators say the service could expand further if intraday trading is introduced in Nepal. Intraday trading allows investors to buy and sell securities within the same trading day, seeking to benefit from short-term price movements.

How investors can use margin trading

Investors must first open a separate margin trading account with their brokerage company.

After completing the required procedures, the broker activates margin trading facilities in the investor’s Trading Management System (TMS) account.

When placing an order through TMS, investors using the facility can select the ‘MST’ option before placing a purchase order.

Santosh Paudel, chairman of Sunny Securities, said customers must first visit their brokerage company and complete an agreement form.

“Once the agreement form is completed and the process is finalised, the facility can be used immediately,” he said.

However, margin trading also exposes investors to additional risks.

If the price of shares purchased through margin trading falls by 20 percent or more, the broker can issue a margin call.

Under the Margin Trading Directive, brokers can demand additional margin based on the customer’s risk assessment, market conditions and the risks associated with the shares of listed companies.

The directive requires brokers to maintain a minimum maintenance margin equivalent to 20 percent throughout the margin trading period, taking into account market conditions and the investor’s risk.

For example, if an investor purchases shares worth Rs 1 million by contributing Rs 300,000 and borrowing Rs 700,000 from a broker, a decline in the share value to Rs 800,000 would reduce the investor’s equity to Rs 100,000.

Since the investor must maintain equity equivalent to at least 20 percent of the current value, or Rs 160,000, the investor would have to provide an additional Rs 60,000.

If the investor fails to meet the margin requirement, the broker can sell the shares to recover the amount owed.

Brokers charge 7-10 percent interest

The service fee and interest charged for margin trading vary among brokerage companies.

Most brokers charge a service fee of around 0.25 percent of the amount borrowed. Some brokers, however, do not charge a separate service fee and instead charge only interest.

“We do not charge a service fee. We charge only interest,” said NASA’s Paudel.

Interest rates currently range from around 7 percent to 10 percent annually, depending on the brokerage company.

Sunny Securities, for example, charges an annual interest rate of 7 percent.

Paudel said the interest and service charges levied by brokers are not significantly different from the rates charged by banks.

Brokerage companies can arrange funds for margin lending from their own resources, by borrowing from banks and financial institutions, or through unsecured loans from their shareholders or directors.

Under existing provisions, a broker can borrow up to 4.5 times its net worth for margin trading purposes. A broker cannot provide more than 10 percent of its total margin lending amount to a single individual or household.

With bank interest rates currently relatively low, brokerage operators say some firms have begun using their own funds to provide margin loans to investors.

Which shares qualify for margin trading?

Investors cannot use margin loans to purchase shares of every listed company.

Only securities of companies designated by NEPSE as eligible for margin trading can be purchased using the facility.

Under the Margin Trading Directive, an eligible company must have at least 2.5 million publicly held shares, net worth equal to or greater than its paid-up capital, and must have recorded profits in at least two of the previous three fiscal years. Its shares must also have been listed for at least two years.

Based on these criteria, NEPSE determines which listed companies qualify for margin trading.

Currently, eligible companies include all 19 commercial banks, 11 development banks, 11 finance companies, 28 hydropower companies, 12 life insurance companies, 11 non-life insurance companies and 17 microfinance institutions.

The list also includes six investment companies, three hotel and tourism companies, two manufacturing and processing companies, one trading company and two companies from other sectors.

With more brokers entering the margin lending business, investors now have greater access to borrowed funds for share purchases. However, the facility also exposes investors to margin calls and the risk of forced sales if share prices fall and they fail to meet the required maintenance margin.

title.rendered: Alternative energy being explored to ensure smooth winter power supply: NEA Managing Director Shrestha

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, September 23

Newly appointed Nepal Electricity Authority Managing Director Dirghayukumar Shrestha has said that alternative energy sources are being explored to ensure a smooth electricity supply during the winter season.

Assuming office at the authority’s Darbar Marg office on Wednesday, Shrestha said the reconstruction of hydropower projects damaged by the Bhotekoshi flood in Rasuwa on August 26 was his top priority.

He said work had already begun to reconnect projects damaged by floods in the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli rivers in Rasuwa to the national power system.

“We are also considering alternatives to ensure a smooth electricity supply during the winter. The Ministry of Energy and the Nepal Electricity Authority have formed a task force for this purpose. We will not allow problems in electricity supply during the winter. Providing services and quality electricity to the people will remain my priority,” he said.

Shrestha said the authority would work on both immediate and long-term strategies for the reconstruction of hydropower projects damaged by the floods.

He also said a decision had been made to form a separate committee to conduct a detailed design and engineering study of the Sunkoshi-3 Hydropower Project.

Due to the floods, 135 megawatts of electricity currently generated at the Chilime Hub has been disconnected from the national power system. Shrestha said he was committed to ensuring convenient and quality electricity distribution to consumers.

“The Bhotekoshi flood in Rasuwa on August 26 caused significant damage to the state and the Nepal Electricity Authority. We are preparing immediate and long-term plans to recover from the damage. Initially, our focus will be on restoring the damaged transmission lines,” he said.

“Currently, only 135 megawatts of generation capacity at the Chilime Hub is operational. Our first target will be to reconnect two or four other hydropower plants to the national power system. The authority has already started work on this. Our strategy is to clear the debris from the hydropower projects, assess the damage after the debris is cleared, and then move ahead with reconstruction plans,” he said.

Minister for Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation Biraj Bhakta Shrestha administered the oath of office to Managing Director Shrestha at the ministry on Wednesday morning.

A Cabinet meeting held on September 18 appointed Shrestha as managing director of the authority.

title.rendered: PM Shah urges public to avoid unnecessary travel as heavy rain forecast

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, September 23

Prime Minister Balendra Shah has urged the public to remain alert as heavy to extremely heavy rainfall is forecast across several parts of Nepal from Friday to Sunday.

Shah, who is currently in New York to attend the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, cited the Department of Hydrology and Meteorology’s forecast in urging people to take precautions. He is scheduled to address the UN General Assembly on Thursday.

According to the forecast, parts of Gandaki and Lumbini provinces could receive heavy to extremely heavy rainfall from September 25 to 27, while heavy rainfall is also likely in some areas of Koshi, Bagmati, Madhesh, Karnali and Sudurpaschim provinces.

Recent weather alerts have warned of increased risks of flooding and landslides as a weather system develops over the Bay of Bengal.

Shah said the rainfall could trigger floods, landslides, debris flows and inundation, while also disrupting road and air transportation.

He urged people to avoid highway travel during rainfall and, as far as possible, refrain from travelling at night.

The prime minister also advised people to remain cautious in areas near rivers and streams, particularly locations considered vulnerable to flooding.

He has urged people planning trekking or travel to mountainous areas to postpone their trips until weather conditions improve.

Shah also called on the public to regularly follow weather updates issued by the Department of Hydrology and Meteorology and instructions from local administrations.

He urged relevant government agencies to strengthen preparedness, coordination and vigilance in response to the forecast.

The Department of Hydrology and Meteorology maintains a warning system covering rainfall, floods, landslides and other weather-related hazards.

title.rendered: Government moves to allocate 2% hydropower IPOs to serving security personnel

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, September 23

The government has initiated the process to allow serving security personnel to participate in initial public offerings (IPOs) of hydropower projects.

Speaking at the House of Representatives meeting on Wednesday, Minister for Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation Biraj Bhakta Shrestha said legal procedures were being advanced to ensure that serving security personnel receive a two per cent share in hydropower project IPOs in recognition of their contribution during disasters.

“Respecting their dedication and contribution, necessary procedures have been initiated to establish a legal provision ensuring two per cent participation for serving security personnel in hydropower project IPOs,” Minister Shrestha said.

According to Sudarshan Shrestha, undersecretary at the Ministry of Energy, the provision will apply to serving security personnel. He said legal procedures were being advanced to ensure two per cent IPO participation from hydropower projects for personnel of all three security agencies.

He said a policy decision had been taken to involve security personnel in hydropower project ownership in recognition of their dedication and strong sense of responsibility towards the nation.

Minister Shrestha also said a decision had been made to provide immediate relief to the dependent families of Nepal Electricity Authority employees who died or went missing during disasters.

He said the families of authority employees who died or went missing in the Trishuli River while serving the nation would receive Rs 500,000 in immediate relief and 50 per cent of their salaries for six months.

Minister Shrestha also praised the coordinating role played during the Bhotekoshi disaster by employees of agencies under the ministry, the Nepal Electricity Authority, the Department of Irrigation, and the Department of Hydrology and Meteorology.

“We need to assess the damage as well as build technologies and infrastructure capable of reducing such risks in the future,” he said.

Shrestha said subordinate agencies had been instructed to give high priority to safety standards when planning future hydropower projects to make them disaster-resilient.

Meanwhile, citing information from the Meteorological Forecasting Division that a low-pressure system developing over the Bay of Bengal could bring heavy to very heavy rainfall to Nepal again, Minister Shrestha urged people to remain alert.

He said subordinate agencies had already been instructed to maintain high vigilance, particularly in central and western Nepal and recently flood-affected areas including Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading, and to regularly monitor weather information.

title.rendered: Free education up to Bachelor’s level for Gen-Z Movement martyrs’ families and injured

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, September 23

The government has decided to provide free education up to the bachelor’s level to the families of martyrs of the Gen-Z movement and those who were seriously or critically injured.

According to the Guidelines for Providing Free Education to Families of Martyrs and the Injured of the Gen-Z Movement, 2083, prepared by the Ministry of Education and Sports, beneficiaries include the children and siblings of martyrs, as well as holders of IDs certifying serious or critical injuries.

At the basic level, beneficiaries will receive free education, along with uniforms and learning materials, from Grades 1 to 8. Cash assistance will also be provided through local governments in accordance with prevailing laws, according to the guidelines.

At the secondary level, the provision covers uniforms, learning materials and cash assistance for students in Grades 9 and 10, as well as Grades 11 and 12.

Similarly, for studies up to the bachelor’s level, universities are required to reserve a certain quota of scholarships for eligible beneficiaries. Students who are not selected under the reserved quota will be eligible for cash scholarships through the University Grants Commission.

The guidelines stipulate that public schools must include eligible beneficiaries in scholarship quotas provided under existing laws.

Students at the basic and secondary levels must apply through their schools to the local government to receive the benefits. At the undergraduate level, students must apply to the University Grants Commission through their respective campuses.

According to the guidelines, applications must include the beneficiary’s ID, citizenship certificate or birth certificate, documents proving the relationship with the martyr, and a recommendation from the educational institution where the student is enrolled.

The guidelines aim to ensure equal access to education for the families of martyrs and those injured in the Gen-Z movement and provide educational opportunities from the basic to undergraduate levels.

title.rendered: After Nepal’s Bhotekoshi flood, who pays for the damage?

content.rendered:
On 26 August 2026, when a colossal wedge of bedrock and glacial ice broke free from the northern flank of Mount Langtang Lirung at precisely 28.288°N, 85.528°E into Lhende Khola, it triggered devastating floods across Nepal, destroying villages, fertile land, bridges, roads, and 13 hydropower projects with a combined capacity of around 759 MW. Initial government reports recorded over 1,399 bodies recovered and more than 5,170 people missing. However, the full human and economic cost is still being assessed, although the overall recovery could run to NPR 723.31 billion, roughly a tenth of Nepal’s yearly GDP.

As the floodwaters receded, a single question echoed across Nepal and beyond: “Nepal emits almost no greenhouse gas, yet feels devastating climate risks. Who will pay for it?” That question was repeated by survivors, officials, activists, researchers and citizens. It is the question this article seeks to answer.

The science behind the flood

The avalanche from Mount Langtang Lirung plummeted 1,200 vertical meters straight down into the valley floor, travelling a horizontal distance of 14 kilometres in just 7 minutes before striking Nepalese border infrastructure. Driven by immense gravitational forces, the initial rock-ice avalanche and the flash flood it triggered swept down the upper reaches of the Lhende Khola valley at an average velocity of 193 kilometres per hour (120 mph). This devastating torrent then cascaded through the Upper Trishuli Watershed, destroying the critical Rasuwagadhi border crossing and multiple major downstream hydropower corridors.

Avalanches and ice falls are natural mountain processes that have occurred for centuries. However, climate change is making the Himalayas increasingly unstable.

The Bhotekoshi catastrophe illustrates how fossil fuel combustion, such as coal, petrol, diesel, and natural gas, drives global warming. Global temperatures have risen by approximately 1.2°C above pre-industrial levels, with the Himalayas warming faster than the global average. This accelerates the thawing of permafrost, the frozen ground that helps hold mountain slopes together.

The injustice: Who emits, who suffers

According to the Global Carbon Project, IEA, and Our World in Data, the United States, China and India are the world’s three largest annual CO₂ emitters, collectively accounting for over half of global emissions. The United States emits 13.83 tonnes, China 9.24 tonnes, and India 2.19 tonnes, compared with the global average of 4.67 tonnes per capita.

Nepal emits just 0.54 tonnes per person, contributing approximately 0.05% of global annual emissions and 0.01% of cumulative historical emissions since industrialisation.

The loss and damage fund: Promises, pleas and responsibility

Established at COP27 in 2022, the Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage (FRLD) helps vulnerable developing countries address climate-related losses beyond adaptation. However, it is not a compensation mechanism: the Paris Agreement’s Decision 1/CP.21, Paragraph 51, explicitly excludes liability or compensation. Funding is provided through grants, while contributions remain voluntary.

By mid-2026, the Fund had received about $822 million in pledges, with $631 million transferred, while 119 developing countries had submitted requests totalling $2.8 billion. Rapid-response projects are currently capped at $5–20 million, and no funds had yet been disbursed; first allocation decisions were deferred to December 2026.

Government of Nepal submitted an urgent request on 1 September 2026 for $20 million, the maximum rapid-response amount, following the 26 August Bhotekoshi disaster. This represents only a fraction of its estimated $4-5 billion reconstruction needs. FRLD has warned that without substantially greater contributions, the Fund’s resources could be exhausted by the end of 2027.

This raises a central question of climate justice: when countries that have contributed little to historical emissions face disproportionate losses, should reconstruction finance remain voluntary assistance or become a stronger international obligation? The principle of Common but Differentiated Responsibilities (CBDR) holds that countries with greater historical responsibility and capacity should contribute more towards climate finance.=

Yet international law remains limited. The gap between differentiated responsibility and voluntary climate finance therefore remains.

The path forward

To prevent such disasters again, the priority must be to drastically reduce global carbon emissions. The transition to a green economy, green infrastructure, and green energy must begin now, not tomorrow. Even if this transition may take 20, 30, 40 years or more, delaying it will only increase future risks. Nepal’s commitment at COP26 to become carbon neutral by 2045 must therefore be treated as a long-term national priority.

Nepal should work with other mountain nations, such as Bhutan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Peru; Small Island Developing States, including Tuvalu, Vanuatu, Fiji and the Maldives; and other highly climate-vulnerable countries, such as Bangladesh, Pakistan, India and Ethiopia, to form a climate justice coalition and jointly advocate for stronger adaptation finance, loss-and-damage support, technology transfer and climate accountability.

Additionally, loss-and-damage finance should move beyond voluntary pledges toward predictable and stronger international financial obligations, particularly for countries with greater historical emissions and greater financial capacity.

Glaciers, permafrost, glacial lakes, avalanches and river systems across Nepal, Tibet and the wider at-risk regions must be tracked continuously.

High-risk glacial lakes, specifically the 25 critical transboundary danger lakes in China (Tibet), the 21 internal high-risk lakes in Nepal, and the broader networks of 52 hazardous lakes in Pakistan and 65 in Bhutan must be identified and monitored using satellites, sensors, drones and remote-sensing technology, with shared data and early-warning systems.

Nepal should also expand automated weather and multi-hazard monitoring systems, particularly in high-risk mountain areas. Water-level, rainfall, temperature, seismic and avalanche sensors can provide real-time warnings. Automated systems should also be deployed in rivers and as well as in mountains which are above 5,000 meters, where timely human monitoring is difficult, to detect hazards and alert communities before avalanches, floods or GLOFs occur.

Schools, communities, local governments and infrastructure operators should receive regular disaster preparedness and climate-risk awareness training, including evacuation routes, emergency communication, first aid and response drills. Dedicated disaster management centres with trained personnel and technical expertise should also be established in high-risk areas.

Nepal must shift from reactive reconstruction to risk-informed development, ensuring infrastructure is built away from flood channels, unstable slopes and other hazard-prone areas. Hydropower and tunnel projects must undergo proper geological, hydrological, glacial-lake and climate-risk assessments before construction.

Development must be region-specific: mountain areas need GLOF and avalanche protection, hills require slope stabilisation and controlled road-cutting, and the Terai needs flood-resistant infrastructure, better drainage and flood-risk zoning. Every new development project should incorporate climate projections, disaster-risk assessments, resilient design, renewable energy and nature-based solutions. Safety and resilience must guide development, and Nepal’s model must shift from simply rebuilding after disasters to preventing avoidable losses before they occur. 

Climate disasters cannot be addressed through relief alone. The burden must be shared more fairly: countries with greater historical emissions and financial capacity should contribute more to the recovery of vulnerable countries like Nepal through stronger and more predictable loss-and-damage finance.

At the same time, Nepal must reduce future risks by decarbonising, building climate-resilient infrastructure and strengthening early-warning systems.

Kathmandu, September 23

The Rastriya Prajatantra Party (RPP) will hold its provincial conventions on October 7. According to party spokesperson Mohan Kumar Shrestha, who also heads the party’s Publicity Department, conventions in all seven provinces have been scheduled for that date.

He said district-level conventions have so far been completed in 72 districts. The RPP’s central general convention is set to take place in Kathmandu from December 12-14. He said preparations for the provincial conventions began once the district conventions were completed.

“The schedule called for finishing district conventions by the third week of September. The August 26 flood affected the timeline somewhat. Flood-affected Rasuwa, Nuwakot, and Dhading have been given until October 1 to hold their conventions,” he said. “The party has also directed Jumla and Dhankuta, which still need to hold theirs, to complete them by October 1.”

He said the election committee for the provincial conventions has already assigned election representatives to the provinces.

According to Shrestha, central election representatives have been assigned as follows: Bharat Pathak for Koshi, Rajaram Shrestha for Madhesh, Pro. Jayanta Nath Khanal for Bagmati, Amrit Pudasaini for Gandaki, Toran Bahadur Gurung for Lumbini, Ramanand Neupane for Karnali, and Shyam Bahadur Shahi for Sudurpashchim.

Under the RPP’s constitution, participants in the provincial convention will include representatives selected by district chairs and district working committees, representatives selected by the regional chairs and working committees of House of Representatives constituencies, and representatives selected by the chairs and working committees of Provincial Assembly constituencies.

Chairs of municipal and rural municipality working committees will also be able to participate as representatives at the provincial convention. Similarly, the deadline for applying for active membership and submitting details for the central general convention has been set for October 1.

title.rendered: Santosh Shrestha appointed chairperson of Advertising Board

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, September 23

The government has appointed Santosh Shrestha as chairperson of the Advertising Board. Shrestha, a resident of Kathmandu Metropolitan City-14, has been appointed chairperson of the board for a maximum term of four years, according to a Cabinet decision made on September 18.

The newly appointed chairperson took the oath of office and secrecy before Minister for Information and Communications Dr Bikram Timilsina on Tuesday.

Following the oath-taking ceremony at the ministry, Minister Timilsina instructed Shrestha to work in a results-oriented manner to regulate, manage and improve the advertising sector. He said the board should play an effective role in accordance with its authority and responsibilities to improve the management of the advertising sector.

Minister Timilsina emphasised the need to move forward with an action plan that further establishes the necessity, rationale and acceptability of the board. He said the board’s current status, problems, opportunities and potential should be seriously reviewed and addressed through clear improvement plans.

Timilsina said ineffective implementation of existing laws and regulations was currently a major challenge. In this context, he said the board needed to identify its weaknesses and make necessary improvements.

He also stressed the need to make the distribution of public welfare advertisements scientific, objective, transparent and lawful. Referring to questions raised by the Office of the Auditor General regarding transparency in the distribution of public welfare advertisements, he emphasised the need to ensure the transparent and effective use of public resources.

Newly appointed chairperson Shrestha expressed his commitment to effectively implementing policies, acts and laws related to advertising. He said he would develop a new action plan to improve the advertising sector, keeping good governance and accessible service delivery for citizens at the centre.

Shrestha also expressed his commitment to making the regulation, management and operation of the advertising sector more effective.

Shrestha, who previously served as president of the Nepal Advertising Association, has extensive experience in the advertising and communications sector. He has also taught at educational institutions including King’s College and Don Bosco College in Kathmandu.

title.rendered: One arrested for stealing offerings at Tripura Sundari Temple in Dolpa

content.rendered:
Dolpa, September 23

Police have arrested one person in connection with the theft of offerings from Bala Tripura Sundari Temple in Tripura Sundari Municipality-1, Dolpa.

The offering money kept at the temple’s main worship site was stolen on Saturday. In the course of investigating the incident, police arrested 37-year-old Jayanand Upadhyay of Tripurakot, Tripura Sundari Municipality-1.

According to the District Police Office, Dolpa, Upadhyay was arrested on Tuesday from the district headquarters, Dunai. He was also taken to the Dolpa District Court on Wednesday, and a seven-day remand was obtained to begin the investigation, said Police Inspector Padam Rawal of the District Police Office, Dolpa.

The theft of Rs 55,080 in cash kept at the main worship site of Bala Tripura Sundari Temple on Saturday had come to public attention.

Money found in different locations

As the investigation continued, Rs 55,000 was found Monday evening in a Timur tree to the west of the temple. The Shree Bala Tripura Sundari Shushankadari Yogini Udyan Pith announced in a statement that this was the missing offering money, saying it was found during the search.

The recovered amount was handed over to priest Ramprasad Upadhyay by police constable Indra Bahadur GC, in charge of the temple security post.

Then, on Tuesday afternoon, it was reported that around Rs 54,000 more had been found within the temple premises. The priest stated that this amount also belonged to the temple.

The fact that money reported missing in a single theft has now turned up in two separate locations has raised further questions about the case.

Police say documentation has been prepared for both amounts, and the investigation into the unanswered questions is ongoing.
