title.rendered: Bhotekoshi floods cause massive human losses and billions in material damage across three districts

content.rendered:
The flood in Rasuwa’s Bhotekoshi River has caused massive human and material losses. According to the latest Nepal Police update, 157 bodies have been recovered so far.

Riverside settlements in Rasuwa, Dhading, and Nuwakot districts have suffered major damage, with some settlements swept away entirely.

With whole settlements washed away, it is still not clear what has happened to many people. Reports of hundreds of missing persons continue to come in.

According to police, bodies have been recovered as follows: Rasuwa 3, Nuwakot 13, Dhading 64, Gorkha 19, Tanahun 9, and Nawalparasi East 22.

Among the missing are personnel from the Nepal Army, Nepal Police, Armed Police Force, civil servants, and workers from various hydropower projects. Nepal Police has also reported that 28 police personnel remain out of contact so far.

Among those injured in the floods, 20 are being treated at TU Teaching Hospital Maharajgunj, 4 at the Trauma Centre, 3 at Bir Hospital, 1 at Birendra Military Hospital Chhauni, 3 at Norvic Hospital, and 9 at Trishuli Hospital.

The floods have left 403 tourists out of contact, including 341 foreigners and 62 Nepalis, 203 men and 200 women.

The largest number of missing tourists are Indian (133), followed by Americans (47), Australians (34), and Britons (33).

Foreign and domestic tourists out of contact

The number of tourists left out of contact due to the Rasuwa flood has reached 403. According to the Nepal Tourism Board, 341 are foreign, and 62 are Nepali, comprising 203 men and 200 women.

Indians make up the largest group among those out of contact, at 133, followed by 47 Americans, 33 Britons, 34 Australians, 24 Canadians, 19 Malaysians, 7 Ukrainians, and 6 South Africans. Also out of contact are 6 Singaporeans, 5 each from New Zealand and Japan, 4 Germans, 3 French, and 2 Spanish nationals.

Preliminary estimate: over 200 billion rupees in economic damage

According to the government’s preliminary estimate, Wednesday’s flood caused damage exceeding 200 billion rupees to the economy. Minister for Physical Infrastructure Sunil Lamsal said that infrastructure damage alone is estimated at over 200 billion rupees. He said the flood has caused extensive infrastructure damage, and that the government will prioritise rebuilding bridges and roads. Beyond roads and bridges, the flood has caused unimaginable damage to the energy and tourism sectors.

According to a Disaster Risk Reduction Authority update as of 11:30 PM Wednesday, 35 concrete bridges and 45 suspension bridges have been swept away.

The 40-kilometre road from Betrawati to Rasuwagadhi has been completely washed away. The Ministry of Finance reported that the Rasuwagadhi customs point has been destroyed. According to the ministry, the physical infrastructure of Rasuwagadhi customs has been fully damaged, and some staff remain out of contact. According to the Nepal Truck Transport Entrepreneurs’ Federation, cargo vehicles, transport operators, and labourers have been affected by the floods.

The flood caused the greatest human and material damage ever seen in the Rasuwagadhi customs area (Timure).

Goods worth billions of rupees imported from China ahead of the upcoming major festivals, Teej, Dashain, Tihar, and Chhath, along with hundreds of cargo containers and the businesspeople, customs agents, and transport workers stationed there, have been caught in the flood’s grip. Along with ready-made goods at the customs yard, a large number of expensive imported electric vehicles (EVs) were also swept away. Businesspeople say 500–700 vehicles were washed away. According to Ram Hari Karki, chairman of the Nepal Himalaya Cross-Border Commerce Association, more than 200 trucks that had arrived at the Rasuwagadhi border point for cargo transport are estimated to have been swept away.

Transmission lines disrupted

Six transmission lines have been disrupted by the severe flooding in Rasuwa. According to the Nepal Electricity Authority, the 220 kV substation at Trishuli has been destroyed, and power flow has been disrupted due to damage to other transmission lines. The 220 kV 3B Hub substation at Trishuli has been destroyed.

The Chilime 220 kV hub tower has shut down due to obstruction. The Samundratar–Trishuli 132 kV transmission line is disrupted, as is the Chilime–Trishuli 66 kV line. The Chilime Hub–Trishuli 3B Hub–Matatirtha 220 kV line and the Trishuli–Balaju 66 kV line are also disrupted. The authority says some other transmission line towers have also been damaged.

Three districts declared crisis-hit

The government has declared the three flood-affected districts crisis zones and has appealed for humanitarian and material assistance for them. Several donor agencies have pledged support to Nepal for flood relief; India has sent 10 tonnes of humanitarian aid.

Following the massive crisis caused by the floods, all political parties have appealed for unity in supporting the government’s response. Representatives of all parties in parliament pledged united support for the government. Ruling RSP chairman Rabi Lamichhane has called an all-party meeting to discuss the disaster tomorrow (Thursday).

title.rendered: Rasuwa flood: Death toll reaches 95 as hundreds remain missing

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 26

The Rasuwa flood has killed at least 95 people and left hundrends missing after a sudden surge of water swept down from the Tibet side of the Nepal-China border on Wednesday morning.

The flood struck the Timure area of Rasuwa at around 9am before surging downstream through Syaphrubesi, Mailung and Betrawati and into the Trishuli River. It caused widespread destruction across Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading and other downstream areas.

Homes, markets, roads, bridges, hydropower projects, transmission infrastructure and border trade facilities have been damaged or swept away.

Nepal Police said 95 bodies had been recovered as of Wednesday evening. Of them, 27 were women, 37 men, six girls, five boys and 20 people whose identities have yet to be established.

A large number of people remain missing, although authorities have yet to determine the exact number.

85 security personnel missing

The Rasuwa flood has also caused major losses among security personnel deployed in the affected areas.

According to officials from Nepal Police, the Armed Police Force and the Nepal Army, 85 security personnel remain unaccounted for.

Nepal Police Central Spokesperson DIG Abinarayan Kafle said 32 police personnel were missing.

Nine Armed Police Force personnel deployed at the Border Outpost in Timure are also missing, according to APF spokesperson DSP Shailendra Thapa.

Nepal Army spokesperson Brigadier General Rajaram Basnet said 44 soldiers deployed for the security of Langtang National Park and hydropower projects had not yet made contact.

Police personnel stationed at the Area Police Offices in Timure and Syaphrubesi, as well as police posts in Rasuwagadhi and Mailung, are among those missing.

Police Assistant Head Constable Santosh Rijal, who was stationed at Betravati, said the scale of destruction was so extensive that it was difficult to assess the damage.

Rijal had been using a loudspeaker to warn residents about the approaching flood when the water suddenly surged. He managed to escape.

403 tourists out of contact

The disaster has also disrupted tourism in the region.

According to the Nepal Tourism Board, 403 tourists are out of contact, including 341 foreign nationals and 62 Nepali tourists.

The group includes 203 men and 200 women.

Indian nationals account for the largest number, with 133 tourists reported out of contact. The list also includes 47 Americans, 33 Britons, 34 Australians, 24 Canadians, 19 Malaysians, seven Ukrainians and six South Africans.

Six Singaporeans, five New Zealanders, five Japanese, four Germans, three French nationals and two Spanish nationals are also among those reported missing.

Timure, Syaphrubesi among worst-hit areas

Timure, near the Nepal-China border, was among the areas hardest hit by the Rasuwa flood.

Homes, shops, vehicles, commercial goods, roads and other infrastructure were swept away. The area around the Timure customs office was also badly affected, disrupting a major route for Nepal-China trade.

The Rasuwagadhi customs yard reportedly lost all vehicles parked there. The Rasuwagadhi hydropower project’s powerhouse and substation also suffered serious damage.

Syaphrubesi was another major centre of destruction. Homes, hotels, shops, a police post and roads were swept away or severely damaged.

The road connecting Syaphrubesi with Timure has been cut off. Tourist buses and other vehicles were swept away, while tourists staying at hotels in the area were left stranded.

Local residents described the flood as resembling a sudden dam break.

Hydropower projects and power network damaged

The Rasuwa flood has caused extensive damage to hydropower and electricity infrastructure.

The Nepal Electricity Authority said the Chilime Hydropower Centre, Rasuwagadhi Hydropower Project and Trishuli-3A Hydropower Project were affected.

The Trishuli 3B Hub 220 kV substation was completely damaged, while several transmission lines were disrupted.

The affected lines include the Samundratar–Trishuli 132 kV line, Chilime–Trishuli 66 kV line, Chilime Hub–Trishuli 3B Hub–Matatirtha 220 kV line and Trishuli–Balaju 66 kV line.

The Chilime 220 kV hub tower has also been affected.

The authority said it was attempting to restore electricity through alternative systems where possible.

The 216MW Trishuli hydropower project has also suffered serious damage, while the Mailung Khola and Devighat hydropower facilities were affected.

Preliminary assessments indicate that 13 to 15 hydropower projects have been affected by the disaster.

Around 19 bridges swept away

The flood has destroyed or damaged roads and bridges along the Bhotekoshi-Trishuli corridor.

Around 19 bridges have reportedly been swept away, including a bridge connecting Dhading district headquarters.

In Nuwakot’s Trishuli area, around 60 houses were reportedly swept away in preliminary assessments, while two concrete bridges were destroyed.

Betravati, Galchhi and Gajuri have also suffered damage to roads, bridges, houses and agricultural land.

Floodwater and debris have covered farmland in several locations, causing significant losses for farmers.

The impact extended downstream towards Muglin. Authorities warned residents and travellers along the Trishuli and downstream areas to remain on high alert.

Muglin itself suffered comparatively less damage after residents had time to move to safer areas.

Cause of Rasuwa flood remains unclear

The exact cause of the Rasuwa flood has yet to be established.

Experts have offered several preliminary explanations involving the high-altitude areas of Tibet.

Some believe a glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) may have triggered the disaster after one or more unstable glacial lakes suddenly released large volumes of water.

Professor Ranjan Kumar Dahal of Tribhuvan University’s Central Department of Geology said the volume and force of water suggested that a glacial lake may have burst, potentially in combination with an avalanche.

Researcher Amrit Thapa of the University of Alaska Fairbanks has suggested that an ice-rock landslide may have caused the sudden flooding of the Lhende River.

The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority, citing Planet Labs satellite imagery, said a snow-rock landslide occurred around 20 kilometres northeast of the Rasuwagadhi border point on the Nepal-China border.

The authority said the landslide caused a debris-laden flood in the Lhende River, which then flowed through Timure and into the Trishuli.

Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal told Parliament that preliminary information suggested an earthquake occurred in the area at around 8:37am, potentially triggering a landslide and subsequent flooding.

The US Geological Survey recorded a magnitude 4.4 earthquake in the Nepal-China border region.

However, experts have cautioned that the earthquake alone cannot yet be established as the cause of a flood of this scale.

Scientists have also pointed to potentially dangerous glacial lakes in the Tibetan region above Rasuwa. Further scientific investigation is required to determine what triggered Wednesday’s disaster.

Government intensifies rescue operations

The government has mobilised all three security agencies for search and rescue operations following the Rasuwa flood.

The Cabinet held an emergency meeting and decided to declare the affected local levels as flood crisis areas. It also authorised the Home Minister to mobilise helicopters and other available resources for rescue operations.

The Nepal Army deployed teams from Dhunche and Trishuli, as well as a specialised disaster management team from its No. 6 Brigade headquarters in Gajuri.

An MI-17 helicopter equipped with an emergency medical rescue team was deployed, while the Armed Police Force mobilised around 1,100 personnel.

A total of 15 helicopters—seven from the Nepal Army and eight from the private sector—were involved in the rescue operation.

At least 97 people have been evacuated by air, according to the Army.

Hospitals including Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital, the National Trauma Centre and the APF Hospital were placed on standby to receive those rescued from the affected areas.

At least 63 injured people had been taken to hospitals, according to an earlier Nepal Police update, with patients receiving treatment at facilities in Kathmandu, Rasuwa and Nuwakot.

Relief efforts begin

Prime Minister Balen Shah said saving lives, locating missing people and protecting affected residents were the government’s immediate priorities.

The government has called for food, drinking water, medicine and temporary shelter to be provided to affected families.

The Ministry of Agriculture has appealed to national and international non-governmental organisations to immediately mobilise food and relief supplies.

Home Minister Sudhan Gurung has held discussions with representatives of the private sector, including the Federation of Nepalese Chambers of Commerce and Industry, Confederation of Nepalese Industries, Nepal Chamber of Commerce, Nepal Bankers’ Association and Federation of Contractors’ Associations of Nepal, seeking support for relief and reconstruction.

The Civil Aviation Authority of Nepal has also instructed airlines not to increase airfares amid the disruption of road connectivity caused by the disaster.

Meanwhile, search and rescue teams continue to work in the affected areas as authorities try to identify recovered bodies, locate missing people and assess the full extent of the damage caused by the Rasuwa flood.

title.rendered: Which towns and settlements were worst affected by the Rasuwa flood?

content.rendered:
The Rasuwa flood has caused widespread destruction along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river corridors, affecting settlements, markets, roads, bridges and hydropower infrastructure across several districts.

The flood entered Nepal from the Tibet side on Wednesday morning and swept downstream from the Timure area in Rasuwa towards Nuwakot and Dhading, with its impact extending further into Gorkha, Chitwan and other downstream areas.

The full extent of the damage is still being assessed, but several towns and settlements have reported significant destruction.

Timure

Timure, near the Nepal-China border, was among the worst-hit areas.

The Rasuwa flood swept away houses, shops, vehicles and goods in the market area. Infrastructure around the Rasuwagadhi customs point was also severely damaged.

The flood disrupted roads and access to the area, making rescue operations and damage assessment difficult.

Syafrubesi

Syafrubesi was another of the hardest-hit settlements in Rasuwa.

Houses, hotels, shops, roads and a police post were damaged or swept away. Tourist buses and other vehicles were also carried away by the flood.

The main road connecting Syafrubesi with Timure has been disrupted, while several tourists staying at hotels in the area have been left stranded.

Local residents described the force of the flood as extraordinary, saying it appeared as though a huge volume of water had suddenly been released upstream.

Mailung

Mailung and surrounding settlements also suffered extensive damage.

Houses were swept away and roads were damaged, leaving the area difficult to access. The flood also eroded farmland and destroyed crops.

Security personnel rescued several people from the area, with some injured survivors airlifted to Kathmandu for treatment.

Betrawati

The Rasuwa flood continued downstream to Betrawati in Nuwakot, where houses, roads and bridges were damaged.

The settlement, located along the Trishuli River, was inundated by floodwater and debris. Agricultural land in the area was also covered with mud and sediment.

Trishuli Bazaar

Trishuli Bazaar in Nuwakot suffered major damage as the flood moved downstream.

Preliminary reports indicate that around 60 houses were swept away, while two concrete bridges were destroyed.

Water and debris inundated the market, damaging homes, shops and other structures. The Tribhuvan Trishuli Multiple Campus and surrounding infrastructure were also affected.

Galchhi

The flood reached Galchhi in Dhading, where rising water levels in the Trishuli put riverbank settlements at risk.

A concrete bridge was swept away, while roads and houses were also affected. Flood debris and mud covered sections of the area.

Authorities have urged people to avoid travel through the affected areas.

Gajuri

Gajuri and surrounding areas were also affected by the rising Trishuli River.

Residents reported damage to houses, roads and agricultural land. People living in vulnerable areas were moved towards safer locations, although the full extent of the damage has yet to be established.

Malekhu

At Malekhu, the Trishuli River rose above the danger level.

The flood affected areas around the market and damaged roads and bridges. Several houses near the river were inundated.

Ruwakot and Majhimtar

Riverbank settlements including Ruwakot and Majhimtar also experienced the impact of the Rasuwa flood.

Houses and farmland were damaged, while floodwaters deposited rocks, mud and debris across agricultural land.

Authorities are still collecting details of the damage in these areas.

Muglin

The flood also triggered warnings for communities around Muglin further downstream.

Authorities advised people to avoid the Prithvi Highway and the Muglin–Narayanghat road and asked residents in vulnerable riverbank areas to move to safer locations.

Muglin, however, appears to have avoided the scale of destruction reported in settlements further upstream.

Widespread destruction

The Rasuwa flood has affected dozens of settlements along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli rivers, damaging homes, businesses, roads, bridges, customs infrastructure and hydropower projects.

The Nepal Electricity Authority has reported damage to several hydropower and transmission facilities, disrupting electricity generation and supply in Rasuwa and surrounding areas.

With several roads and bridges damaged or washed away, access to affected settlements remains difficult. Rescue operations and detailed assessments of the human and physical losses are continuing.

title.rendered: Rasuwa flood survivor clings to hope as wife, four children remain missing

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 26

For 38-year-old Girilal Budhathoki of Salyan, the Dashain-Tihar holidays were supposed to mark the end of a five-year struggle in Timure, Rasuwa.

He had planned to return to his hometown with his family after years of working in the Himalayan settlement.

But the devastating flood that swept through Timure on Wednesday morning took away more than his home.

On his own, Budhathoki is now receiving treatment in the emergency ward of Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital in Maharajgunj, Kathmandu, with injuries across his body. His wife, two sons and two daughters were swept away before his eyes. He has received no information about their whereabouts.

“My two sons, two daughters and wife were swept away by the flood,” Budhathoki said through tears. “I have never seen such a flood. I have no hope that my family survived.”

Budhathoki had been living in Timure with his family for around five years and supported them by driving a garbage truck.

He had gone out for work on Wednesday morning. At around 9:10 a.m., he noticed traffic had come to a standstill and decided to return home after having breakfast.

As he approached his home, the flood suddenly arrived.

“I was reaching the courtyard when it suddenly came from there,” he recalled. “I did not even know the flood had arrived.”

Within moments, the man who had been returning home to meet his family was running for his own life.

His family was inside a temporary shelter when the flood struck.

“I ran from the corner of the courtyard and managed to survive,” he said, breaking down in tears. “But the flood swept away the shelter with them right in front of my eyes.”

‘We were planning to return home for Dashain’

Budhathoki had spent five years working in Timure and was looking forward to returning home.

“We were planning to go home for Dashain,” he said.

He had worked and earned money for his family, dreaming of taking them back to Salyan. Instead, the flood has left him alone.

He survived by holding on to a metal rod

Budhathoki himself was trapped when the force of the flood began destroying the house.

“When the house we were staying in collapsed, I was trapped inside,” he said, pointing to his injuries. “My hand was pinned underneath and I was trapped against the wall.”

He managed to hold on to a metal rod from a railing.

“I had made a railing and there was a rod fixed into it,” he said. “I held on to that rod.”

As the force of the flood shifted downstream, he eventually managed to escape. Bleeding heavily, he began climbing toward higher ground.

“I slowly made my way up,” he said. “I had already lost a lot of blood.”

Friends and fellow workers later rescued him, and he was flown to Kathmandu by helicopter for treatment.

The flood came so suddenly and with such force that people nearby had little chance to help one another.

“It took everything away in an instant,” Budhathoki said. “No one survived.”

He still hopes that some people who were outside or managed to see the flood coming and run to safety may have survived.

But for his wife and four children who were inside the shelter, he fears there may be no such hope.

His body is injured, his eyes are filled with grief, and the life he had spent years building has been swept away in a matter of moments.

title.rendered: What caused the Rasuwa flood? Experts point to possible glacial lake outburst

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 26:

A devastating flood that struck Rasuwa’s Bhote Koshi River on Wednesday morning is believed to have been triggered by a possible glacial lake outburst or a landslide in the Tibetan region of China, although the exact cause has yet to be scientifically confirmed.

The flood hit Timure at around 8:30 am, causing extensive loss of life and destroying settlements and infrastructure along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli rivers.

Experts estimate that the source of the flood may lie around 40–50 kilometres upstream from the Nepal-China border, where several potentially dangerous glacial lakes are located.

Some experts believe one or more of these lakes may have suddenly released a massive volume of water. Others suspect that a landslide or avalanche blocked the Lhende River, creating a temporary natural dam that subsequently burst.

Possible glacial lake outburst

Ranjan Kumar Dahal, a professor at Tribhuvan University’s Central Department of Geology, said a flood of this magnitude would be difficult to explain without a major avalanche and subsequent glacial lake outburst.

Dahal said three glacial lakes located close to each other in the upper Lhende River area could have been involved.

“We cannot say at this stage which lake failed or how,” Dahal told Onlinekhabar, adding that the lakes had previously been considered high-risk.

Researcher Amrit Thapa of the University of Alaska Fairbanks also believes an avalanche may have triggered the flood in the Lhende River. He said the assessment was based on preliminary discussions with scientists from Nepal and China.

The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) said a snow-and-rock landslide occurred around 20 kilometres northeast of the Rasuwagadhi border point, citing satellite imagery from Planet Labs.

According to the authority, the landslide caused a debris-laden flood in the Lhende River, which then flowed through Timure and entered the Trishuli River.

Experts divided over exact mechanism

Experts have not yet reached a consensus on whether the disaster should be classified as a glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF).

Some believe a glacial lake itself burst, while others argue that a snow-and-rock avalanche blocked the river before the resulting temporary dam collapsed.

Bishnu Maharjan, an academic working in geographical information systems (GIS) and remote sensing, said the incident appeared to be linked to a GLOF but stressed that further scientific investigation was required before reaching a definitive conclusion.

When a lake formed on the surface of a glacier — known as a supraglacial lake — suddenly drains, a large volume of water, rocks, soil and debris can rush downstream within a short period, creating a highly destructive flood.

Small glacial lakes also pose a major risk

Experts have warned that even apparently small glacial lakes can contain significant volumes of water beneath or within glaciers.

Researcher Thapa said several small lakes in the Tibetan region near Rasuwa had merged in recent years to form larger water bodies. He also said satellite studies conducted after last year’s flood showed significant changes in the area.

The International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD) has previously identified 47 potentially dangerous glacial lakes that could affect Nepal.

Experts say rising temperatures and changes in glaciers are increasing the risks associated with such lakes. Thapa said the underlying cause of these increasingly unstable glacial systems is climate change.

Was an earthquake responsible?

Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal told Parliament earlier on Wednesday that preliminary information suggested an earthquake at around 8:37 a.m. may have triggered an avalanche, which in turn caused the flood.

However, he stressed that the information still needed to be verified.

The US Geological Survey (USGS) recorded a magnitude 4.4 earthquake in the Nepal-China border region. Some experts, however, have questioned whether an earthquake of that magnitude alone could have generated a flood of such scale.

The Department of Hydrology and Meteorology said there had been no particularly heavy rainfall in the Rasuwa area before the disaster.

Authorities and experts are continuing to investigate the exact source and mechanism of the flood, including through satellite imagery and coordination with Chinese authorities.

title.rendered: Home Minister calls on private sector to support Rasuwa flood relief and rehabilitation

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 26

Home Minister Sudan Gurung has initiated coordination with the private sector to support relief and rehabilitation efforts for people affected by the devastating floods in Rasuwa.

Gurung held discussions with the leadership of the Federation of Nepalese Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FNCCI), Confederation of Nepalese Industries (CNI), Nepal Chamber of Commerce, Nepal Bankers’ Association and Federation of Contractors’ Associations of Nepal, urging them to work alongside the government during the disaster.

The government has called on the private sector to provide urgently needed food, medicines, clothing, temporary shelters and other relief materials to flood-affected communities.

Gurung said disaster management was not solely the responsibility of the government but a shared responsibility of the government, private sector and civil society.

He urged all stakeholders to work together to ensure assistance reaches families affected by the Rasuwa floods as quickly as possible.

title.rendered: Rasuwa floods disrupt six transmission lines, 220 kV substation destroyed

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 26

Six power transmission lines have been disrupted following the devastating Rasuwa floods, according to the Nepal Electricity Authority (NEA).

The floods completely destroyed the 220 kV Trishuli 3B Hub Substation, while damage to transmission infrastructure has disrupted power flow across several lines.

The affected transmission lines include:

  • Chilime 220 kV Hub, which has been shut down after its tower was damaged
  • Samundratar–Trishuli 132 kV transmission line
  • Chilime–Trishuli 66 kV transmission line
  • Chilime Hub–Trishuli 3B Hub–Matatirtha 220 kV transmission line
  • Trishuli–Balaju 66 kV transmission line

The NEA said some other transmission towers have also sustained damage.

The authority is working to restore electricity through alternative arrangements wherever possible.

Electricity supply has already been restored in the Samundratar area toward Sindhupalchok, while efforts are underway to bring the Chaughoda substation back into operation.

Similarly, the NEA is working to restore electricity supply to areas between Gajuri and Galchhi through the Dhadingbesi substation.

title.rendered: Rasuwa floods: 95 bodies recovered, 63 injured receiving treatment

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 26

The death toll from the devastating floods in Rasuwa’s Bhote Koshi River has reached 95, according to the latest data provided by Nepal Police.

The recovered bodies include 27 women, 37 men, six girls, five boys and 20 people whose identities have yet to be established.

Of the 95 bodies, one man was found in Rasuwa, while 11 — five women and six men — were recovered in Nuwakot.

Dhading has reported 18 bodies, including 11 women, five men and two unidentified people.

In Gorkha, police have recovered the bodies of one woman, four men, one boy and 10 unidentified people.

In Chitwan, 33 bodies have been recovered, including 10 women, 10 men, two girls, three boys and eight unidentified people.

Police said five bodies — three men, one girl and one boy — were found in Tanahun, while 11 bodies, including eight men and three girls, were recovered in Nawalparasi East.

63 injured receiving treatment

According to Nepal Police, 63 people injured in the floods have been rescued and are currently receiving treatment at various hospitals.

They include 21 patients at Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital in Maharajgunj, seven at the National Trauma Centre, one at Birendra Hospital in Chhauni, 21 at Rasuwa Hospital and 16 at Trishuli Hospital.

Three injured people are being treated at Norvic Hospital and one at Green City Hospital.

28 police personnel missing

Nepal Police said 28 police personnel deployed in the affected areas remain out of contact.

They include 10 from Timure, eight from Rasuwagadhi, three from Syafrubesi, five from Mailung, one from Betrawati and one from Haku.

title.rendered: PM Balen Shah assures flood victims of government support

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 26

Prime Minister Balen Shah has expressed grief over the deaths and devastation caused by the Rasuwa floods, assuring affected families that the government stands with them during the crisis.

In a statement posted on Facebook, Shah said the scale of the human and physical damage had left the country shocked. He offered condolences to those who lost family members and said the government would take responsibility for the rescue, treatment, food and shelter of those affected.

Shah said security agencies were mobilised immediately after the disaster, with the Nepal Army, Armed Police Force and Nepal Police deployed for search and rescue operations. More than 250 people have so far been rescued by Nepal Army helicopters, he said, with injured survivors brought to Kathmandu for treatment.

He said 100 beds have been reserved at Bir Hospital and the National Trauma Centre for free treatment of flood victims, while other major hospitals in Kathmandu have also been kept on standby.

Medical teams, including doctors and health workers from the security agencies, have been deployed to affected areas for rescue and emergency treatment. The Nepal Scouts and World Health Organization have also sent medical personnel, rescuers and health supplies, according to Shah.

The government is coordinating with blood transfusion centres, the Bagmati and Gandaki provincial health ministries, Nepal Red Cross Society, Lions Club and Nepal Scouts to ensure adequate emergency healthcare, medicines and blood supplies.

Shah said search efforts for those still missing would be intensified and that a detailed assessment of the casualties and physical damage was still underway. Rescue operations would continue throughout the night, he added.

The prime minister identified Vidur in Nuwakot; Uttargaya and Gosainkunda in Rasuwa; Gajuri, Galchhi, Benighat, Tripurasundari and Siddhalek in Dhading; and Shahid Lakhan and Gandaki rural municipalities in Gorkha as among the worst-affected areas.

He said the government would immediately provide food, clean drinking water, medicines and temporary shelter to affected families.

Shah also pledged to prioritise the reconstruction of damaged roads, bridges, electricity and drinking water infrastructure and to relocate displaced families to safer areas.

“State is standing with you with all its resources and means,” Shah said, urging affected people to remain patient and calling on social organisations, businesses, youth volunteers and citizens to support the relief and rescue efforts.

content.rendered:

A total of 403 tourists remain unaccounted for following the devastating Rasuwa floods, according to the Nepal Tourism Board.

The board said 341 foreign tourists and 62 Nepali tourists are currently reported missing. Of the total, 203 are men and 200 are women.

Indian nationals make up the largest group of foreign tourists reported missing, with 133 people.

The breakdown by nationality is:

  • India: 133
  • United States: 47
  • Australia: 34
  • United Kingdom: 33
  • Canada: 24
  • Malaysia: 19
  • Ukraine: 7
  • South Africa: 6
  • Singapore: 6
  • New Zealand: 5
  • Japan: 5
  • Germany: 4
  • France: 3
  • Spain: 2

The Tourism Board is coordinating with relevant authorities to establish the whereabouts and status of those reported unaccounted for as search and rescue operations continue in the flood-affected areas.

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 26

The Civil Aviation Authority of Nepal (CAAN) has directed domestic airlines to ensure ticket availability without increasing current airfares amid disruptions caused by the Rasuwa floods.

The regulator instructed airlines to make tickets available at rates below the maximum permitted fare and not increase existing prices, taking into account the current emergency situation.

Several highways connecting Kathmandu with other parts of the country have been closed or declared unsafe following the floods originating from Tibet, increasing pressure on air travel.

CAAN said airlines should facilitate passenger movement by ensuring adequate ticket availability and maintaining current fares.

The directive has been issued to Nepal Airlines, Buddha Air, Yeti Airlines, Shree Airlines, Summit Air, Tara Air and Sita Air.

The airlines have been asked to maintain smooth public transportation during the ongoing disaster situation.

title.rendered: Rasuwa flood: Here’s what the government has done so far

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 26

The government has stepped up search, rescue, medical response and relief operations following the massive flash flood in Rasuwa’s Bhote Koshi River that caused widespread damage across Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading on Wednesday.

Here is what the government has done so far:

13 helicopters deployed for rescue

The government has deployed 13 helicopters, operated by the Nepal Army and private companies, for search and rescue operations in Rasuwa and Nuwakot.

Additional air and ground resources are being mobilised as needed.

Free treatment for flood victims

The government has decided to provide free medical treatment to people injured in the disaster.

Five hospitals, including Trauma Centre, Bir Hospital and Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital, have been kept on standby to treat seriously injured victims.

A medical team comprising 15 Army doctors, 12 Nepal Police doctors and 15 Armed Police Force doctors has also been sent to Nuwakot District Hospital.

Emergency rescue system activated

The government has prioritised the search and rescue of missing and stranded people.

A toll-free number, 1234, has been set up to receive information about people who are missing, trapped or in need of immediate assistance.

Warnings issued along river corridors

Authorities have urged people living along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river corridors in Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Gorkha and Chitwan to remain alert and move to safer locations where necessary.

People have also been asked to avoid travel on high-risk routes, including Galchhi, Nuwakot, Syafrubesi and the Muglin–Narayanghat road.

Emergency funds released

The government has released an additional:

  • Rs 10 million to Rasuwa’s disaster management fund
  • Rs 10 million to Nuwakot’s disaster management fund
  • Rs 5 million to Dhading’s disaster management fund

Roads, electricity and communications to be restored

The Cabinet has directed the concerned ministries to urgently restore infrastructure damaged by the flood, including:

  • Roads and bridges
  • Drinking water systems
  • Electricity supply
  • Telecommunications services

Resources are also being coordinated for the reconstruction of damaged public infrastructure.

Shelter and relief for displaced people

People who have lost their homes are to be moved to safer locations and provided with food and shelter.

The Home Ministry, National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority and local disaster management committees have been tasked with coordinating this response.

Affected areas declared disaster crisis zones

The Cabinet has decided to declare local governments in the flood-affected districts disaster crisis areas for three months under the Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act.

Support for families of victims

Families of people killed in the disaster will receive financial assistance according to existing laws.

The government has also called on provincial governments, local authorities and organisations to support search, rescue, relief and medical operations.

Government still investigating the cause

The government has not yet established the definitive cause of the flood.

Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal told Parliament that preliminary information indicated an earthquake at around 8:37 a.m. may have triggered a landslide or avalanche, leading to the sudden flooding.

Nepal is coordinating with Chinese authorities to establish where the flood originated and what triggered it.

title.rendered: 26 bank employees out of contact after Rasuwa floods

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 26

At least 26 employees of eight commercial banks remain out of contact following the devastating floods that swept through Rasuwa and surrounding areas, according to the Nepal Bankers’ Association.

The employees were working at eight bank branches located around the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli river corridors, including in Timure and Syafrubesi, when the floods hit.

Anil Sharma, CEO of the Nepal Bankers’ Association, said several bank branches in the affected areas have been completely damaged.

“Branches in Timure, Syafrubesi and other locations have been damaged. The employees who cannot be contacted are also from these areas,” Sharma said.

The association said branches of Prabhu Bank, Global IME Bank, Sanima Bank, Nepal Investment Mega Bank, Laxmi Sunrise Bank, NMB Bank and Machhapuchchhre Bank were among those affected. The total number of damaged branches is nine, although employees at eight branches remain out of contact.

The Development Bankers’ Association said development banks operating in the affected areas have not reported any damage so far.

Bank officials are currently prioritising locating and ensuring the safety of employees before assessing the extent of physical damage.

Sharma said access to the affected areas remains difficult, while damage to telephone and internet towers has further disrupted communication.

“Once we establish the whereabouts of the employees, we will assess the physical damage,” he said.

title.rendered: Rasuwa flood cause remains unclear as Nepal, China investigate possible quake-triggered landslide

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 26

The cause of the devastating flood in the Bhotekoshi River in Rasuwa remains unclear, with Nepal and China investigating preliminary reports that an earthquake may have triggered a landslide or avalanche that caused the sudden surge.

The flood struck the Bhotekoshi area at around 8:40 am on Wednesday, causing extensive damage in Timure, Rasuwagadhi and Syafrubesi. Settlements, markets, police offices, roads and hydropower infrastructure have been damaged.

Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal said preliminary information suggested an earthquake occurred in the area at around 8:37 am, potentially triggering a landslide or avalanche that led to the flood.

“According to preliminary information, an earthquake occurred in the area at 8:37 am, followed by an avalanche, which may have caused the flood. However, this needs further verification,” Khanal said.

The government has launched rescue operations, but officials say they remain uncertain about the flood’s source and how far its impact could extend.

Rastriya Swatantra Party chief whip Kabindra Burlakoti said the situation remained uncertain as authorities were still trying to assess the scale of the disaster.

China also investigating flood source

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs said Chinese authorities have also been unable to establish the exact source and cause of the flood.

Officials based in Chengdu are coordinating with Chinese experts and relevant agencies to determine where the flood originated and what triggered it. However, as of Wednesday evening, the exact starting point of the flood had not been established.

Communication difficulties in the suspected source area have complicated efforts to gather information. Chinese authorities have been using various channels to investigate the incident and have shared updates with Nepal.

Satellite technology is also being used to identify the possible source of the flood.

Based on the information available so far, officials believe a large landslide or avalanche may have blocked the river, creating a temporary natural dam that subsequently burst and released a sudden surge of water.

However, experts have yet to officially verify this explanation, and authorities have cautioned that the exact cause cannot be confirmed until further investigation is completed.

title.rendered: In pictures: Rasuwa flood leaves trail of destruction from Rasuwagadhi to Bidur

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 26

Communities along the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli rivers were going about their normal routines on Wednesday morning when a sudden flood swept through the area, destroying structures that had taken decades to build within minutes.

An aerial assessment by Onlinekhabar several hours after the flood showed widespread destruction across the affected areas, from the Rasuwagadhi border point to Bidur in Nuwakot.

Floodwaters reached settlements as high as 270 feet above the river level, with homes destroyed and the number of people swept away still unclear.

Survivors have moved to higher ground for safety, while some residents stranded on the roofs of flooded houses have been calling for rescue. Many people were still waiting to be evacuated as helicopters flew over the affected areas.

The destruction was visible across Timure, Dhunche, Mailung, Syafrubesi and Betrabati, with settlements reduced to ruins and hydropower infrastructure swept away.

The Rasuwagadhi customs office was also destroyed, with little trace of the facility remaining.

The Nepal Army, Nepal Police and Armed Police Force have been deployed for rescue operations. However, the scale of destruction across Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading has made rescue efforts difficult.

The flood has caused extensive loss of life and property along the Bhotekoshi-Trishuli corridor, while authorities continue search, rescue and relief operations.

title.rendered: Indian PM Modi speaks to PM Balen, offers India’s support after Rasuwa floods

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 26

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke with Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah on Wednesday and expressed condolences over the loss of life and property caused by the floods in Rasuwa.

Modi said India stands in solidarity with the Nepali people during the difficult situation and is ready to provide all possible humanitarian assistance to Nepal.

Following the conversation, Modi said Indian officials were coordinating with their Nepali counterparts on rescue and relief efforts.

The floods, which entered Rasuwa from the Tibetan side before moving downstream through the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli rivers, have caused extensive damage in Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading and other downstream areas.

title.rendered: Energy Minister directs immediate assessment of flood damage

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 26

Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha has directed officials to immediately collect details of the damage caused by the sudden flooding of the Bhotekoshi River in Rasuwa and surrounding areas and accelerate rescue, relief and rehabilitation efforts.

Minister Shrestha convened a meeting of the ministry’s Senior Management Team (SMT) to assess the initial situation. At the meeting, he directed officials to prioritise the rescue and rehabilitation of employees, workers and residents affected by the disaster, coordinate with the Ministry of Home Affairs and other relevant agencies, and immediately mobilise mechanisms in the affected areas.

Shrestha said the ministry should remain active in ensuring the systematic and rapid flow of disaster-related information. He also directed officials to assess the actual damage to energy and other physical infrastructure and begin rehabilitation efforts.

He also instructed the concerned agencies to prepare alternative and emergency arrangements to ensure a regular, safe and sustainable electricity supply across the country, including in the Kathmandu Valley.

The ministry said it is coordinating with the Ministry of Home Affairs to identify the status of employees, workers and residents who remain out of contact following the floods and facilitate their rescue.

The Nepal Electricity Authority (NEA) has already deployed seven vehicles to the affected areas for rescue operations, while another 14 vehicles have been kept on standby.

The ministry also said it is coordinating aerial rescue efforts. A joint secretary of the ministry has also been deployed to the affected areas for rescue and coordination.

Eight hydropower projects in Rasuwa—five operational and three under construction—have been affected by the floods.

The total capacity of the operational projects is 236 MW, while the projects under construction have a combined capacity of 342.42 MW. The affected projects include Upper Trishuli-1, Rasuwagadhi, Rasuwa Bhotekoshi, Sanjen Khola, Upper Mailung A, Mailung Khola, Langtang Khola and Chilime hydropower projects.

Similarly, six projects in Nuwakot—four operational and two under construction—have also been affected by the floods. Their combined capacity is 123 MW for the operational projects and 52.6 MW for those under construction.

The affected projects include Trishuli, Devighat, Upper Trishuli-3A, Upper Trishuli-3B, Middle Trishuli Ganga and a 25 MW solar project.

The NEA has mobilised technical teams to prevent disruptions to the electricity supply. The ministry said efforts are underway to assess the condition of affected infrastructure and restore electricity services as soon as possible.

The Hydrology and Meteorology-related authorities have sent more than 200,000 SMS alerts to residents in downstream areas to provide early warnings about flood risks.

However, damage to some structures, including gauge stations installed by the authorities, has made it difficult to provide further risk-related information.

Meanwhile, the ministry also held discussions with the Independent Power Producers’ Association, Nepal (IPPAN) to gather information on the damage to hydropower projects, the rescue of affected personnel and the rehabilitation of the projects.

The discussions also covered the need to quickly collect details of damage to private-sector projects and coordinate the necessary rehabilitation efforts.

According to the ministry, detailed damage assessments and technical evaluations of the affected projects are being carried out by the concerned agencies. Once the actual extent of the damage is established, the ministry will move forward with a rehabilitation action plan.

The ministry said a committee has also been formed under the coordination of a joint secretary from the Planning Division to oversee the overall assessment and compilation of the damage.

title.rendered: 62 flood victims receiving treatment at hospitals in Kathmandu, Rasuwa and Nuwakot

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 26

At least 62 people injured in the Rasuwa floods are currently receiving treatment at hospitals in Kathmandu, Rasuwa and Nuwakot, authorities said.

The injuries were reported after a devastating flood entered Rasuwa from the Tibetan side of China and swept through downstream areas, causing widespread destruction and casualties.

According to Nepal Police, 25 injured people are being treated at hospitals in Kathmandu.

Four people — Bhakta Bhandari, Sita Bhandari, Bivek Kumal and Rihana Lamichhane, all from Bidur Municipality-5 of Nuwakot — are receiving treatment at the National Trauma Centre.

At Birendra Army Hospital in Chhauni, police said Dawa Dolma from Gosainkunda, Rasuwa, is receiving treatment.

Several other injured people are being treated at Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital in Maharajgunj. They include people from Nuwakot, Rasuwa, Sindhupalchok, Salyan, Jajarkot and Gorkha, as well as some whose identities or addresses have not yet been established.

Police said one of the patients, Karmu Nagarkoti from Timure, Gosainkunda-7, is accompanied by a three-month-old infant.

Meanwhile, 21 injured people have been brought to Rasuwa Hospital, according to Sumitra Gautam, secretary at the Bagmati Province Ministry of Health.

Another 16 injured people are being treated at Trishuli Hospital in Nuwakot, Gautam said. Some of the injured are reported to be in serious condition.

The government has activated emergency health mechanisms and hospitals in Kathmandu and surrounding areas have been placed on standby as rescue operations continue in the flood-affected areas.

title.rendered: India, China and World Bank offer emergency aid to flood-hit Nepal

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 26

India, China and the World Bank have moved to coordinate immediate financial and humanitarian assistance for flood-affected Nepal, as rescue and relief operations continue in Rasuwa and downstream districts.

Soon after reports of the disaster emerged, World Bank Country Director for Nepal David Sislen contacted Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle at around 10:35 a.m. and informed him that up to Rs 25 billion in emergency assistance could be mobilised from various sources.

India has asked the Nepal government to provide a list of relief materials urgently needed for flood victims so that assistance can be sent accordingly.

Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal said preparations were underway to bring Indian relief supplies to Kathmandu on Wednesday itself, following coordination with Prime Minister Balen Shah, Finance Minister Wagle and other senior ministers.

China has also offered immediate cash assistance to Nepal. Chinese Ambassador Zhang Maoming has asked the government, through the Finance Ministry, to initiate the process for transferring the funds.

The government has expressed gratitude for the support offered by Nepal’s neighbours and development partners. Finance Minister Wagle is coordinating with the relevant governments and agencies to determine the mechanism for receiving and deploying the assistance.

The Cabinet on Wednesday declared affected local units in Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading as disaster crisis-hit areas, opening the way for the mobilisation of domestic and international assistance.

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 26

The Nepal Truck Transport Entrepreneurs Federation has reported significant damage to cargo vehicles, transport businesses and workers following the flood that entered Rasuwa from the Tibetan side of China.

According to the federation, cargo vehicles parked at the Timure customs yard were swept away by the flood. Preliminary reports also indicate extensive damage to cargo vehicles parked in the Betrawati area.

The federation said some vehicle operators and workers affiliated with its member organisations remain out of contact. It has urged them to remain in contact with their respective organisations and reach out to security authorities if possible.

With the flood risk still ongoing, the federation has urged transport operators, workers and the general public to exercise extreme caution around rivers and nearby areas and follow instructions issued by security agencies.

It has also appealed to transport businesses and others to support rescue and disaster-risk reduction efforts wherever possible.

title.rendered: 1,000 inmates at Nuwakot Central Prison safe after flood

content.rendered:
Nuwakot, August 26

Around 1,000 inmates at the Central Prison in Nuwakot have been rescued from the impact of the floods that swept through areas from Tibet in China to Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading and Chitwan.

The prison, located at Khampacamp in Bidur Municipality-3 along the Trishuli River, sustained partial damage but was spared from being swept away by the floodwaters.

According to prison chief Bhesh Bahadur Kunwar, the prison’s administrative building and the Nepal Police security unit building were damaged. Other structures around the prison were swept away by the flood.

Floodwaters entered the first floor of the building where inmates are housed, but the building itself was not swept away, Kunwar said.

Around 1,000 inmates and the security personnel guarding them are safe. Following the flooding, all inmates were moved to a secure block.

Floods have caused extensive damage in various riverside areas of Rasuwa and Nuwakot.

title.rendered: Man arrested for allegedly threatening to kill PM Balen Shah on Instagram

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 26

Police have arrested a 23-year-old man for allegedly issuing a death threat against Prime Minister Balen Shah through social media.

The arrested man has been identified as Pushkar Dahal, a resident of Bhadrapur-9, Jhapa, who is currently living in Kirtipur. A team from the Kathmandu Valley Crime Investigation Office arrested him from Kirtipur New Bazaar.

Dahal has been handed over to the Cyber Bureau in Bhotahity for further investigation and legal action.

According to police, Dahal had posted a message on Instagram threatening to “finish” Prime Minister Shah on September 8 and tagged the police in the post. He had also used abusive language against the police.

Police sources said Dahal is affiliated with the Ujyalo Nepal Party, led by Kulman Ghising.

Authorities are investigating the circumstances surrounding the alleged threat.

title.rendered: Finance Minister Wagle tasked with mobilising funds for Rasuwa flood recovery

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 26

Finance Minister Dr Swarnim Wagle has been tasked with coordinating the mobilisation of financial resources needed to rebuild infrastructure damaged by the Rasuwa floods. The decision was made at an emergency meeting of the Council of Ministers held today.

According to Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal, Minister Wagle has been assigned responsibility for coordinating the mobilisation of financial resources required for the immediate restoration and reconstruction of public structures and physical infrastructure damaged by the floods.

A massive flood in the Rasuwagadhi area this morning caused widespread damage.

After the floodwaters merged with the Bhotekoshi River, the Timure, Rasuwagadhi and Syafrubesi areas were affected. Reports indicate that the flood damaged settlements, markets, police offices, roads and infrastructure belonging to hydropower projects.

Foreign Minister Khanal provided the information while briefing Parliament on the incident.

The government has also decided to provide financial assistance to the families of those who died in the Rasuwa floods.

Foreign Minister Khanal said the Cabinet decided to “immediately provide financial assistance to the families of the deceased in accordance with prevailing law.”

The Cabinet also decided that the Ministry of Home Affairs would arrange food and accommodation for people who have lost their homes by relocating them to safe places.

It also decided to ensure the availability of drinking water and electricity and restore communication links in the affected areas.

More than 100 people have been rescued from areas affected by the devastating floods in Rasuwa, according to the Prime Minister’s Office.

The rescued people include 85 from Dhunche, 13 from Timure, five from Mailung, four from Betravati and three from Trishuli.

All of them were rescued by Nepal Army and private helicopters deployed to the flood-affected areas.

A sudden flood in the Bhote Koshi River in Rasuwa on Wednesday caused widespread destruction across Rasuwa and downstream districts including Nuwakot, Dhading and Chitwan.

Search, rescue and relief operations are continuing in the affected areas.

title.rendered: Rasuwa floods cause infrastructure damage estimated at Rs 200 billion

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 26

The floods that swept through Rasuwa and downstream areas have caused infrastructure damage estimated at around Rs 200 billion, according to Minister for Physical Infrastructure Sunil Lamsal.

Responding to questions about the damage caused by Wednesday morning’s flood, Lamsal said preliminary information suggested that infrastructure losses were approaching Rs 200 billion.

He said the Rasuwa flood had caused extensive damage to infrastructure, particularly roads and bridges, and that the government would prioritise their reconstruction and restoration.

“We have received information that infrastructure damage is around Rs 200 billion,” Lamsal said.

The flood entered Nepal from the Tibetan side through the Bhote Koshi River and caused widespread destruction across Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading and Chitwan, among other districts.

At least seven deaths have so far been confirmed, according to the information available to authorities, while rescue and search operations continue.

title.rendered: Govt to provide free treatment to Rasuwa flood victims

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 26

The government has decided to provide free medical treatment to people injured in the Rasuwa floods, following an emergency Cabinet meeting held on Wednesday.

Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal informed the House of Representatives that immediate free treatment would be provided to those injured in the disaster through the Ministry of Health and Food Hygiene, the Nepal Army and government hospitals.

“The Cabinet has decided to arrange immediate and free medical treatment for people injured in the incident through the Ministry of Health and Food Hygiene, the Nepal Army and government hospitals,” Khanal said.

The Cabinet also decided to arrange the immediate rescue and relocation to safe areas of people who have been injured or left stranded by the floods.

The Home Ministry and Defence Ministry have been tasked with coordinating the rescue operation, with both Nepal Army and private helicopters to be mobilised for the effort.

The massive flood that struck the Rasuwagadhi area on Wednesday morning has caused widespread damage.

After entering the Bhote Koshi River, floodwaters affected Timure, Rasuwagadhi and Syaphrubesi, with reports of damage to settlements, markets, police facilities, roads and hydropower infrastructure.

Khanal briefed the House on the government’s response to the disaster during Wednesday’s parliamentary meeting.

title.rendered: Trishuli Bazar in ruins after devastating flood

content.rendered:
Nuwakot, August 26

Trishuli Bazar in Nuwakot was bustling with its usual morning activity on Wednesday. Residents had begun their daily routines as normal.

Within minutes, however, a sudden and powerful flood swept through the area, dramatically transforming the town.

The floodwaters from the Bhote Koshi River, which entered Nepal through Rasuwa from the Tibetan side, moved downstream into Nuwakot, causing extensive destruction along the Trishuli River corridor.

Around 60 houses in and around Trishuli Bazaar were reportedly swept away, while the nearby Devighat area was also affected. Two motorable bridges over the Trishuli River were also washed away.

The flood also damaged the Trishuli and Devighat hydropower projects and affected infrastructure linked to a 25-MW solar power project.

The extent of the damage is still being assessed as rescue and relief operations continue across the flood-affected areas.

title.rendered: Flood damages at least 19 bridges, 40 km of roads along Trishuli

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 26

The devastating flood that swept through the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river system has damaged at least 19 bridges and 40 kilometres of roads, according to the Department of Roads.

Department of Roads Deputy Director General and spokesperson Shubharaj Neupane said the damage assessment was still preliminary and that several bridges along the Trishuli River had been affected by the flood.

At least 40 kilometres of roads have also been damaged or washed away, disrupting road connectivity across the affected areas.

Neupane said the department has deployed heavy equipment and machinery to the affected areas and has begun work to restore damaged roads and bridges.

The flood, which entered Nepal from the Tibetan side through the Bhote Koshi River in Rasuwa, has caused widespread damage downstream, including in Nuwakot and Dhading. Rescue and relief operations are continuing across the affected areas.

title.rendered: NEPSE falls 35.92 points as Rasuwa floods hit hydropower sector

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 26

Nepal’s stock market fell sharply on Wednesday, with the benchmark NEPSE index dropping 35.92 points to 2,558 points, as shares of hydropower companies were hit following the damage caused by floods in Rasuwa and surrounding areas.

Total turnover stood at Rs 4.77 billion, higher than the previous trading session. Of the companies traded, 23 gained, 252 declined and three remained unchanged.

The hydropower sub-index fell 2.84%, making it one of the worst-performing sectors after floods from the Tibetan side affected more than a dozen hydropower projects in Rasuwa and neighbouring areas.

The non-life insurance sub-index also dropped 3.90%, as investors reacted to the potential insurance liabilities arising from damage to hydropower infrastructure.

Other sectors also ended lower, including banking (-0.74%), development banks (-0.84%), finance (-1.10%), hotels and tourism (-0.54%), investment (-1.31%), life insurance (-1.52%), manufacturing and processing (-0.40%), microfinance (-0.91%), others (-1.44%) and trading (-0.04%).

Flood-hit hydropower companies among biggest losers

Shares of several hydropower companies affected by the floods recorded significant declines.

Rasuwagadhi Hydropower fell 15%, while Mailung Khola Hydropower dropped 14.99%, Trishuli Hydropower 12.95%, Upper Mailung Khola 11.56% and Sanjen Hydropower 11.18%.

Among the gainers, Sarbottam Paints rose 15%, while Upper Hewakhola gained 10.43% and Kalinchowk Hydropower increased 3.21%.

Chilime Hydropower, Sanima Middle Tamor, Sahas Urja, Solu Hydropower and Ridi Power were among the most actively traded companies.

The market decline came as authorities reported extensive damage to hydropower projects following the Rasuwa floods, with the Nepal Electricity Authority’s preliminary assessment putting the total capacity of affected operational and under-construction projects at 748 MW.

content.rendered:

Six bodies have been recovered in Dhading following the massive flood that entered Nepal through Rasuwa and moved downstream along the Trishuli River.

According to the District Police Office, Dhading, the bodies were recovered from different locations along the river by 3pm on Wednesday.

One woman’s body was found at Mahesh Dobhan in Galchhi Rural Municipality, while the bodies of two men were recovered near the Kolpu Khola bridge, also in Galchhi.

Another body was found along the Trishuli River in Siddhalek Rural Municipality-7.

Two women’s bodies were recovered from the Trishuli riverbank near Benighat Bazaar in Benighat Rorang Rural Municipality.

Dhading Police also said seven people have so far been rescued from the flood-affected areas.

The injured people have been taken to local hospitals for treatment.

title.rendered: Police constable recalls narrow escape as flood swept away colleagues

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 26

A sudden flood in Rasuwa has caused widespread devastation, resulting in significant loss of life and property in Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading and other areas.

All security agencies have been mobilised for search and rescue operations. Personnel trained in search and rescue, along with Nepal Army helicopters, private helicopters, drones and sniffer dogs, have been deployed to the affected areas.

Medical teams have also been sent to the flood-hit areas. Security agencies said the bodies of seven people who died in the floods have so far been recovered. Several injured people have also been rescued and are receiving treatment.

Security personnel have also suffered significant losses. Nepal Police Central Spokesperson and DIG Abinarayan Kafle said 32 police personnel are still missing. Nine personnel from the Armed Police Force are also out of contact.

A total of 41 security personnel remain unaccounted for.

Police Assistant Constable Santosh Rijal, who narrowly survived the flood, spoke to Onlinekhabar. He said a massive surge of water suddenly hit while he was making an announcement over a loudspeaker warning people that a flood was coming.

We are reproducing below, verbatim, what Assistant Constable Rijal told Onlinekhabar about the situation there:

“I am stationed in Betravati. We had gone out to make announcements warning people that a flood was coming. We were using a loudspeaker to urge residents living along the roadside and riverbanks to move to safer places.

“We had been deployed for the announcements under the command of Assistant Sub-Inspector Ram Kaji Paudel. Suddenly, a massive flood came. There was no time to even think. People who were sleeping, sitting at home or eating were swept away by the flood. We do not know exactly how many people were swept away.

“I was on my motorcycle. I abandoned the motorcycle and ran toward the forest to save my life. The ASI who had gone with us to make the announcements is out of contact. We still do not know what happened to him. I am currently staying in the forest. I have nowhere to go. I survived by just 10 seconds. At a time like this, simply being alive feels like a lot.

“We do not know how many children or students were swept away. I saw many people being swept away right before my eyes. Many of our police personnel are also out of contact. There must have been around 70 houses here. Now, none of those houses is still standing intact.”

According to the Nepali Army, 29 people have been airlifted to safety so far. The Army has deployed 6 helicopters alone for the rescue effort, and Army headquarters says 2 more helicopters are also en route.

title.rendered: Red Cross on standby for Rasuwa flood, blood stock remains sufficient

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 26

The Nepal Red Cross Society says it is on standby to manage blood and other medical supplies that may be needed to treat those injured or affected by the flood in Rasuwa.

Anticipating a possible emergency, the Red Cross is coordinating with hospitals and blood transfusion centers in various districts.

According to Pawan Kumar Gupta, director of the Nepal Red Cross Society’s blood bank, around 1,000 units of blood are currently in stock at the center in Kathmandu. He said blood supplies at transfusion centers in other districts across the country are also sufficient as needed.

Gupta said the Red Cross is coordinating with relevant hospitals and health institutions in view of the possibility that blood may be needed to treat those injured in the Rasuwa flood, and that it remains in constant contact with health workers and units involved in emergency treatment and trauma care in particular.

“Right now we have an adequate blood stock. Coordination with hospitals is ongoing in light of the Rasuwa incident,” Gupta said. “We are on standby to make blood available immediately if needed.”

He said transfusion centers in various districts also have the necessary stock, adding that Dhading and Chitwan also have sufficient supplies.

Since a flood could suddenly increase demand for blood if many people are injured in one area at once, the Red Cross has prepared to manage blood supplies as needed by coordinating between districts. If demand rises in any district, it says, available blood there will be used, and if necessary, blood will be brought in from other districts to meet the need.

Gupta said there is no immediate problem with the current blood stock, but since the number of injured could rise suddenly during a disaster, demand from hospitals and blood requirements are being continuously monitored.

Coordination between hospitals, health institutions, and Red Cross blood transfusion centers has been prioritized to prevent any blood shortage in treating those affected or injured by the Rasuwa flood. The Red Cross says it has kept its mechanism active to make blood available immediately if required.

Since demand for blood tends to rise during disasters and emergencies, the Red Cross has also urged people to continue donating blood regularly. It says that although current stocks are sufficient, since the disaster situation could persist for a while, blood donation and transfusion management should continue with future needs in mind as well.

Gupta made clear that the Red Cross is prepared to ensure no blood shortage arises in treating those injured by the Rasuwa flood, and stands ready to manage blood supplies immediately as needed.

He also said coordination is underway for collection with the Voluntary Blood Donors Society Nepal, the Blood Donors Association Nepal, various organizations involved in blood donation, and other donors.

According to him, the workers were carrying out work in a section of the tunnel located about 100 meters above the river level. They have not yet been rescued, and contact with them has also been lost.

“I tried to go there myself by helicopter, but no helicopter was available as all of them have been mobilised by the government,” he said. “Government agencies need to step up rescue efforts.”

He said around 60 workers had been working at the project. Complete information about all the workers is not yet available.

“We have received information that the employees working at the headworks are safe,” he said. “We are trying to find out the status of the others.”

title.rendered: Cause of Rasuwa flood remains unclear, experts suspect glacial lake outburst

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 26

The cause of the devastating flood in Rasuwa’s Bhote Koshi River remains unclear, with experts suggesting that a glacial lake outburst, avalanche or failure of a natural river blockage may have triggered the sudden surge.

The flood struck at around 9am on Wednesday, causing extensive damage in areas including Rasuwagadhi Customs Office, Syaphrubesi, Betrawati, Trishuli and Timure.

Authorities have yet to establish the exact cause of the Rasuwa flood, while no official information has been received from the Chinese side.

Geography professor Narendra Raj Khanal, who has studied floods and landslides, said an avalanche in Tibet could have triggered the flood.

“Only an initial assessment can be made at this point. We have not yet received official information from the Chinese side,” Khanal said. “The flood may have been caused by a slow avalanche.”

Information officer at the Department of Hydrology and Meteorology Dinkar Kayastha said a glacial lake outburst is among the preliminary possibilities being considered.

“The exact cause has not yet been established. Our preliminary assessment is that a glacial lake may have burst. We will issue a statement once the actual cause is established,” Kayastha said.

He also warned that the flood could reach Devghat in Chitwan within one to two hours, urging people in areas including Muglin and Narayangadh to remain on high alert.

Geologist Ranjan Kumar Dahal said the volume of water suggested that the Rasuwa flood was unlikely to have been caused by the blockage of a small stream.

“Looking at the flood, it appears that a lake has burst. But it is not possible to say which lake. It appears that an avalanche occurred and a lake also burst,” Dahal said.

Researcher and author Madhukar Upadhyay, who has studied the relationship between water and landslides, also said a glacial lake could be responsible.

“This is unimaginable destruction. This may have been caused by a glacial lake,” Upadhyay said.

Geologist Shrikamal Dwivedi suggested another possibility: melting permafrost in the Himalayan region.

He said prolonged light rainfall, even without heavy precipitation, could cause ice-bound soil and rocks on steep Himalayan slopes to melt and flow downhill.

“Even if there has not been heavy rainfall, continuous light rain could melt the soil and rocks held together by ice in the Himalayan slopes, known as permafrost, potentially triggering a glacial flood,” Dwivedi said.

The actual cause of the sudden Rasuwa flood, however, remains to be confirmed.

title.rendered: NOC sends 16,000-litre refuelling truck to Nuwakot to support helicopter rescue operations

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 26

The NOC’s aviation fuel depot in Sinamangal has dispatched aviation fuel to Nuwakot for helicopters deployed in rescue and relief operations in areas affected by the Rasuwa floods.

The 16,000-litre-capacity refuelling truck was sent to Nuwakot to make it easier for Nepal Army and private helicopters involved in rescue operations to refuel and eliminate the need to return to Kathmandu solely for fuel.

According to Pradeep Yadav, chief of the Aviation Fuel Depot in Sinamangal, the refuelling truck, which is normally used to refuel aircraft only inside airports, has been sent outside an airport for the first time in view of the emergency situation.

He said the decision was made in consultation with the Civil Aviation Authority of Nepal and the Nepal Army. If the refuelling truck cannot reach the Nepal Army barracks in Nuwakot, it will be stationed at the Army barracks in Gajuri, Dhading, he said.

“We are sending a 16,000-liter-capacity refueling truck to provide fuel to the Nepal Army and other helicopters involved in the rescue operations,” Yadav told Onlinekhabar. “Although the vehicle is not normally permitted to operate outside the airport, we have sent it under the security and supervision of two Nepal Army representatives and three representatives from the corporation due to the exceptional circumstances.”

Officials expect that allowing helicopters to refuel in Nuwakot will make rescue operations for people affected by floods and landslides faster and more effective.

The Nepal Oil Corporation’s move is expected to provide significant logistical support for rescue operations during the emergency.
