title.rendered: Ganga Dahal says she and family ready for any legal investigation

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 20

Ganga Dahal, daughter of Nepali Communist Party (NCP) coordinator Pushpa Kamal Dahal ‘Prachanda’, has said that she and her family are always ready to face any legal investigation by state authorities.

Dahal also urged the government to take serious note of what she described as recurring rumours being spread against her family.

“We are always ready for any legal investigation by any state agency under the Constitution and laws created by sacrificing the blood of thousands of martyrs,” she wrote on social media. “But why are such rumours spread from time to time? For what purpose are they being spread? I want to draw the government’s serious attention to this.”

Dahal said her family had survived situations involving the threat of death and therefore knew well what was right and wrong.

“We may face death, but we cannot deceive the people. That is our upbringing,” she wrote. “Is it a crime that I supported my father as his daughter, even at the expense of my personal life? I want to ask the leaders of this society and every parent this question.”

She also denied any financial wrongdoing or abuse of position by herself or her family, saying they would not engage in such activities in the future either.

“I want to remind everyone once again that we submitted our property details to the government some time ago,” Dahal wrote. “We will cooperate with any investigation conducted by the government, and if wrongdoing is proven, we will face the consequences.”

However, she said her family would not accept allegations made without evidence or wrongdoing.

“But accusations without reason and without any wrongdoing are unacceptable. I reject all such allegations,” she said.

title.rendered: Will the Nepal-India border task force meeting address key boundary disputes?

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 21

The 14th meeting of the Nepal-India Joint Working Group on Border Management is underway in Dehradun, India, with officials from both countries discussing a range of issues related to the management of the shared border.

The two-day meeting began on Thursday and will conclude on Friday.

Nepal’s delegation is led by Home Ministry Joint Secretary Anand Kafle, while India is represented by Pausumi Basu, Joint Secretary at the Ministry of Home Affairs.

The meeting is discussing the construction, restoration and maintenance of boundary pillars, management of the no-man’s land, GPS mapping of boundary pillars and collection of land ownership details of people living along the border.

Officials are also expected to discuss day-to-day problems faced by people crossing the Nepal-India border and ways to address them.

Nepal’s delegation includes Foreign Ministry Joint Secretary Gehendra Raj Bhandari, Department of Immigration Director General Ram Chandra Tiwari and security officials including Binod Ghimire and Krishna Khanal.

Will major border disputes be discussed?

The meeting comes amid renewed debate over Nepal-India boundary issues.

Prime Minister Balen Shah had drawn controversy in May after saying that Nepal, too, had encroached on Indian territory at several places.

Against this backdrop, diplomatic observers say the latest meeting could be significant, although the Joint Working Group primarily deals with border management rather than resolving major territorial disputes.

Former Foreign Minister Pradeep Gyawali has urged the two countries to ensure that the working group’s meetings do not become a mere routine exercise.

He said the mechanism should be used to make effective decisions on issues such as the use and control of land along the border.

Former Foreign Minister Upendra Yadav, however, believes the meeting will have limited significance unless the major boundary disputes over Lipulekh-Kalapani and Susta are addressed.

“Without resolving the fundamental border disputes, a meeting of the border management working group remains incomplete,” Yadav said.

Lipulekh-Kalapani and Susta remain unresolved

Nepal and India have prepared strip maps covering most sections of their shared boundary. However, the maps have not been formally signed because disagreements over Lipulekh-Kalapani and Susta remain unresolved.

Border experts have said that resolving the remaining disputes outside these two areas should not be particularly difficult.

The Joint Working Group was established to address practical issues related to border management, including boundary pillars, the no-man’s land and problems faced by people living along the border.

The group has been meeting regularly, except during the COVID-19 pandemic. Its 13th meeting was held in Pokhara last year.

The current meeting will also review the implementation of decisions taken during the previous meeting.

Calls for tighter regulation of open border

Former Foreign Minister Prakash Chandra Lohani has called for more effective regulation of the open Nepal-India border.

Lohani, who represented Nepal at a border security meeting nearly three decades ago, said both countries should consider requiring people crossing the border to carry identification documents.

“We had raised the issue of effective border regulation as early as 2052–53 BS,” Lohani said. “Even if passports are not made mandatory, arrangements should be made to require identification cards when people travel between the two countries.”

The outcome of the Dehradun meeting is therefore being watched to see whether it produces concrete decisions on longstanding border management issues or remains focused on routine technical matters.

title.rendered: Parliamentary committee directs govt to curb sewage discharge into Bagmati River

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 20

The House of Representatives’ Infrastructure Development Committee has directed the government to immediately control the discharge of sewage and wastewater into the Bagmati River and prepare an integrated plan for its conservation and revival.

The committee issued the directive during its meeting at Singha Durbar on Thursday.

Committee Chair Ashish Gajurel said the Ministry of Physical Infrastructure and Transport had also been directed to clearly demarcate the river’s jurisdiction and take an integrated approach to controlling encroachment, protecting the river corridor and managing flood risks.

The committee has called for the Bagmati beautification programme to go beyond physical infrastructure and develop the river corridor as a green, open, pedestrian-friendly and citizen-friendly public space.

According to the committee’s decision, priority should be given to making the Bagmati clean by preparing a plan to immediately control all sewage and wastewater discharge into the river.

The committee also directed the government to integrate the river’s environmental restoration with its religious, cultural, historical and tourism heritage and develop the Bagmati as a “heritage river corridor.”

It called for a unified institutional mechanism with clearly defined responsibilities, regular monitoring and public accountability to ensure the long-term success of the programme.

The Ministry of Physical Infrastructure and Transport has also been directed to allocate adequate funds for the clean Bagmati programme.

The committee said conservation, flood-risk management and development of the river corridor should be pursued through a coordinated approach rather than through isolated infrastructure projects.

title.rendered: Rabi Lamichhane to tour Madhesh to pave way for RSP’s pending provincial convention

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 20

Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) Chair Rabi Lamichhane is set to tour Madhesh districts to create an environment for holding the party’s long-delayed provincial convention.

The RSP held its central general convention without completing the provincial convention in Madhesh Province.

Among the eight districts in Madhesh, the party has elected new leadership only in Parsa. Conventions in the remaining districts have not been completed after disputes emerged during the process and the proceedings were suspended.

Most party structures under the district committees also remain without elected leadership.

While the RSP completed conventions in the other six provinces, it was unable to hold its provincial convention in Madhesh.

Lamichhane had said immediately after the central convention that he would personally visit Madhesh to facilitate the convention process. According to an RSP Madhesh Province lawmaker, Madhesh-based lawmakers met Lamichhane on Wednesday to discuss the issue.

During the meeting, Lamichhane informed them that he would begin visiting Madhesh districts after August 26.

“He informed us that he would travel from Chitwan through Thori in Parsa and visit the districts of Madhesh. The purpose of the visit is to facilitate the convention process,” the lawmaker who attended the meeting said.

The party’s Election Commission has already issued a circular directing local party bodies where conventions have not been held to restart the process.

Lamichhane’s planned tour is expected to focus on resolving internal disputes and creating the necessary environment to complete the pending organisational conventions in the province.

title.rendered: Nepali workers at risk after the UK revokes work permit licence

content.rendered:
London, August 20

After graduating with an MBA from the UK’s York St John University in 2021, Sadikshya Thapa worked full-time on a two-year Post-Study Work (PSW) visa.

After the scheme ended, she either had to return to Nepal or find sponsorship in the UK to remain on a work permit. Seeing little future in Nepal if she returned, she obtained a Skilled Worker visa on January 9, 2024, after receiving sponsorship from an Indian-owned restaurant, Bamboo House Limited.

At her employer’s request, Thapa paid more than Rs 900,000 (£4,500) herself to a solicitor when submitting her visa application.

Initially, her employment agreement stated that she would be paid an annual salary of £21,500 for a minimum of 37 hours of work per week. However, as she continued working, Sadikshya did not receive a written employment contract. She was made to work 42 hours per week, more than the hours stated on her visa. Regardless of how many hours she worked, she was paid only £400 per week.

For most of her employment, she did not receive payslips. She received payslips only for May, June and July 2024, which showed deductions labelled as ‘NEST pension contribution’.

When she later contacted NEST, she was informed that she had never been enrolled in its pension scheme.

From January 9, 2024, to March 28, 2026, over approximately 26 months, she did not receive any paid holiday. After experiencing severe financial and mental exploitation and a lack of a proper working environment, Sadikshya has now taken her case to a British employment tribunal.

“I have gone to court because I was exploited even in a place like the UK,” she told Onlinekhabar. “Even if I have to return to Nepal, I will continue fighting for my rights until the very end.”

She said being unemployed for the past four months had made her daily life difficult.

Many Nepali students have changed their immigration route after completing their studies, believing that a Skilled Worker visa is more secure than remaining on a student visa. Some have spent thousands of pounds on employers to obtain sponsorship. But their experiences have been similar to Sadikshya’s.

Most workers suffer at the hands of employers

With few exceptions, many workers who move onto the work permit route are forced to suffer financial and mental distress at the hands of their employers. Some receive neither holiday pay nor payslips and are not given leave. They may also find themselves in situations where they have to pay tax on their own wages.

There are many cases of people in Nepal being cheated out of millions of rupees by the lure of overseas employment. But recently, the number of Nepalis who have already come to the UK and obtained Skilled Worker visas who are being cheated or left in distress has been increasing.

A rule preventing people from switching to a work permit without completing their degree has now been implemented. The British government further tightened the rules from July 2025. Under the new system, mainly workers with a bachelor’s-level qualification who earn at least £41,700 per year are eligible.

Isha (name changed), who works as a manager at a restaurant operated by a Pakistani-origin businessman in Central London, spent nearly Rs 2.5 million when extending her visa twice. She had worked there for three and a half years.

Now, while waiting to become eligible for Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR) in the UK in another year and a half, she has suffered a major setback after the restaurant’s licence was suspended.

Isha is under stress after the UK Home Office began the process of cancelling the restaurant’s licence, preventing it from sponsoring workers, on the grounds that it had failed to comply with government rules, regulations and preconditions.

If a company’s licence is suspended or revoked, or if it does not renew the licence itself, workers must find another sponsor within 60 days or leave the UK.

“It is very difficult to find sponsorship elsewhere for a manager position because the annual salary threshold is now above £41,000,” she said sadly. “No company can pay that salary, and it is not easy to find such a job. I left my university studies midway and moved onto a work permit. Now I am left with nowhere to go.”

Almost impossible to bring workers from Nepal or other countries

Bishnu Kharel, director of Visa Quest UK, which has long provided services and advice on the work permit route, also operates two restaurants.

Immigration adviser Kharel said the government has recently begun tightening restrictions on Skilled Worker visas.

“During spot checks, many companies have been found to have lost or had their licences suspended after employers were found not to have complied with the requirements,” he said. “Many have lost their licences for not paying the agreed salary, for not even paying the minimum wage despite paying salaries, for not paying holiday pay, for not providing weekly days off, and for workers not appearing to be doing the job corresponding to the position stated on the Certificate of Sponsorship (CoS) when applying for the visa.”

Business owners also say the British government is currently tightening restrictions on Skilled Worker visas.

A businessman who operates several takeaway restaurants in London said that, because of government rules, it is now almost impossible to bring workers from Nepal or other countries.

“Our restaurants are simply not in a position to support workers while paying an annual salary of more than £41,000 and dealing with numerous compliance requirements and the associated stress,” the businessman said. “We gave many people work permits in London without taking a single penny from them, but various accusations, including exploitation, are made against Nepali businesspeople themselves. So we thought it was best to quietly run our businesses and keep to ourselves.”

Under the Home Office’s Skilled Worker visa scheme, employers officially registered with the Home Office and holding the relevant licence can sponsor and employ foreign workers who meet certain skill-level requirements.

Until July last year, people could qualify for sponsorship to bring workers from overseas if they were paid at least £38,700 per year and had qualifications at A-level or equivalent.

Following changes to the immigration rules, the salary threshold has increased, while people working in non-graduate occupations such as shop managers will no longer be eligible to apply.

The British government further tightened the rules from July 2025. Under the new system, mainly workers with a bachelor’s-level qualification who earn at least £41,700 per year are eligible.

There are more than 120,000 businesses in the UK holding licences to sponsor skilled workers. After the UK left the European Union (EU) through Brexit, free movement between the EU and the UK came to an end. Alongside this, the UK introduced the Skilled Worker visa scheme so employers could recruit foreign workers.

According to the British Home Office, 68,067 Skilled Worker visas were issued in the 12 months to March this year, including 29,745 main applicants and 38,322 dependants. This number is 30 per cent lower than the previous year.

Among those receiving Skilled Worker visas, the largest number were professionals working in the information technology sector, followed by those working in the financial sector. However, the number of visa approvals has fallen because workers in the hospitality sector are no longer eligible for this visa.

A Home Office spokesperson told the BBC: “We have raised the threshold for skilled worker requirements, and new Skilled Worker visas will no longer be available for more than 100 occupations.”

In addition, a higher standard for English-language proficiency was introduced in January this year.

title.rendered: CIAA chief Prem Kumar Rai says he discussed passport contract case with PM before filing case

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 21

Commission for Investigation of Abuse of Authority (CIAA) Chief Commissioner Prem Kumar Rai has told a parliamentary committee that he held discussions with Prime Minister Balen Shah before the passport contract case was filed.

Responding to questions from lawmakers at the House of Representatives’ State Affairs and Good Governance Committee, Rai said it was normal for the prime minister to call CIAA officials for discussions about an ongoing investigation.

“If there is a question about whether the prime minister called us or not, we can be called for discussion or to seek suggestions. We can also be called to ask what is happening in the matter and what you are doing. So, we went and held discussions,” Rai said.

Rai did not elaborate on the substance of the discussion but maintained that the CIAA had followed due process in filing the case.

He urged lawmakers to examine the prosecution documents to determine whether there were any shortcomings in the case, which has already been registered.

“Please look at the prosecution letter. You will clearly see that we did not file the case without grounds,” Rai said. “I do not want to go into this matter in detail.”

Lawmakers had questioned Rai about reports that CIAA officials were kept at the Prime Minister’s Office for around seven hours and allegedly pressured over the decision to prosecute in the passport procurement case.

The issue was raised during Thursday’s committee meeting, with lawmakers seeking clarification from the CIAA chief over the circumstances surrounding the meeting with the prime minister.

title.rendered: Foreign employment companies penalised for sending workers via India allowed to seek review

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 20

Foreign employment companies penalised for sending Nepali workers abroad through Indian airports have been given an opportunity to seek a review of the action taken against them following discussions between the Nepal Association of Foreign Employment Agencies and the Department of Foreign Employment.

The development follows an agreement between foreign employment companies and the Ministry of Youth and Employment, after which representatives of the association held discussions with department officials, including the director general, on Tuesday.

The talks covered the penalties imposed on agencies for sending workers through Indian airports instead of using Nepali airports, delays in the department’s routine services and difficulties faced by recruitment agencies in dealing with government procedures.

The Department of Foreign Employment had taken action against Foreign employment companies in three phases, penalising 598, 39 and 124 agencies respectively. The penalties ranged from warnings to fines of up to Rs 50,000.

Following the latest discussions, the 39 and 124 agencies penalised in the most recent rounds can now submit applications seeking a review of the action.

The department has asked the concerned agencies to provide reasons why action against them should not be taken and submit applications for review.

“Those affected in the latest cases involving 39 and 124 agencies have been asked to apply for a review. Businesses have started submitting applications explaining why action should not be taken against them,” said association president Dik Bahadur Khatri.

The review process gives the affected agencies an opportunity to present their explanations before the penalties are finally implemented.

Appeal deadline for 598 agencies has expired

However, the legal deadline for appealing against the action taken against the first batch of 598 agencies has already expired.

According to Khatri, the law provides 35 days to file an appeal, and that period has already elapsed. As a result, it may be difficult to pursue the matter through the regular appeal process.

The department has already sent letters to 83 of those 598 agencies regarding discrepancies, or “mismatches”, identified in their records.

Some foreign employment companies had objected to the action, arguing that they had already submitted the required details to the department. Following further examination, the department found similar issues involving 83 agencies and informed them that no further action was being taken against them on that particular matter.

Khatri said the latest cases involving 39 and 124 agencies also appear to be linked to discrepancies in earlier records.

As a result, foreign employment businesses argue that the latest penalties should not be examined in isolation and that the underlying records from previous rounds should also be reviewed.

According to the association, examination of the records of agencies penalised in the latest rounds has revealed links with information from earlier phases. This, they argue, warrants a fresh examination of the data and the basis on which the department imposed the penalties.

Dispute to be resolved alongside policy reforms

The latest meeting was held as part of an agreement reached between foreign employment companies and the Ministry of Youth and Employment on August 17.

Under the agreement, the ministry had set a two-month deadline to address the businesses’ demands, including issues related to service fees and policy reforms. The parties had also agreed to seek solutions to disputes over penalties through discussions with the Department of Foreign Employment.

Khatri said the latest discussions with the department were positive, but the actual outcome would depend on decisions on the review applications submitted by the affected agencies.

Manpower companies have now urged the government to resolve the disputes over penalties, including the issues involving the 83 agencies and the alleged mismatches, within the two-month timeframe agreed with the ministry.

They have also called for decisions on service fees and broader policy reforms to be taken within the same period.

title.rendered: Money laundering probe launched against contractor linked to ex-CAAN chief Pradeep Adhikari

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 20

The Department of Money Laundering Investigation has launched an investigation into contractor Nabin Raj Basnet, who was linked to former Civil Aviation Authority of Nepal (CAAN) Director General Pradeep Adhikari.

The development comes after the Commission for Investigation of Abuse of Authority (CIAA) filed a corruption and money laundering case against Adhikari at the Special Court.

Although Basnet’s name was linked to the case, the CIAA did not file a case against him. Sources at the anti-graft body said it had instead recommended that the Department of Money Laundering Investigation examine Basnet’s assets.

The department has now begun collecting documents and information related to Basnet’s assets.

“We have started the investigation. We have asked various agencies to provide documents related to his assets. A detailed investigation will be carried out after all the information is received,” a department source said.

The department is examining the assets of Basnet, his family members and business partners. According to officials, investigators have found substantial landholdings in different parts of the Kathmandu Valley.

Basnet, who is reportedly from a modest economic background, is now involved in several businesses. Companies linked to him and his family include Sandharbhik Nirman Sewa Pvt Ltd, Nil David International Unisex Salon, Kshamadevi Construction Solution Pvt Ltd, Dream Town Developers Pvt Ltd, Kshamadevi Interior and Kshamadevi International Pvt Ltd.

Officials are examining properties held in the names of family members, relatives and business partners to determine their sources.

Preliminary investigation has found that Basnet and partners of Dream Town Developers purchased and planned around 72 ropanis of land in Duwakot, Bhaktapur, according to an official involved in the investigation.

Investigators are also examining large landholdings in Sinamangal, Duwakot, Jorpati, Koteshwor, Thimi and Balkot that are registered in the names of different individuals.

“Land appears to have been registered in the names of his partners and relatives rather than in Basnet’s own name. If the source of the assets cannot be established, all those involved will come under investigation,” the official told Onlinekhabar.

The department said it has previously pursued major money laundering cases involving multiple individuals and is continuing to investigate cases involving substantial assets.

Basnet had also been investigated previously in connection with an incident involving former CAAN chief Adhikari and others. Kathmandu District Police had investigated allegations that Adhikari and others threatened senior officials, including the CIAA chief.

Basnet’s connection to that incident had emerged during the investigation, but no case was filed against him at the time as authorities said further investigation was required.

The authorities had stated that if evidence later established the involvement of individuals not included in the initial case, a separate investigation report would be submitted under Section 35 of the Criminal Code.

Basnet had also secured a contract around three years ago for construction work on the taxiway and apron at Gautam Buddha International Airport in Bhairahawa. The contract was awarded to Ashish-Kshamadevi-Buddha Himalaya JV, with Basnet associated with Kshamadevi at the time.

title.rendered: Kiran Thapa appointed Bagmati chief minister with support from three parties

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 20

Kiran Thapa has been appointed chief minister of Bagmati Province with the support of the CPN-UML, Nepali Communist Party (NCP) and Rastriya Prajatantra Party (RPP).

Bagmati Province Chief Dipak Prasad Devkota appointed Thapa chief minister on Thursday under Article 168(2) of the Constitution.

Thapa had staked his claim to form the provincial government on Wednesday with the support of 63 provincial lawmakers from the three parties.

Devkota had invited a member of the provincial assembly who could command a majority with the support of two or more parties to stake a claim for the chief minister’s post by 4 pm on Thursday.

However, the RPP’s support for the new government has triggered an internal dispute within the party.

The RPP has expelled its parliamentary party leader in Bagmati, Uddhav Thapa, from the party. The party’s central leadership had rejected the decision to support the new government, arguing that the provincial parliamentary party had taken the decision without central approval.

The RPP central office had sent a letter to Province Chief Devkota on Wednesday clarifying that the party had not decided to support any party in the province.

Despite the dispute, the Province Chief’s Office issued a statement on Thursday announcing Thapa’s appointment and the schedule for his swearing-in.

Thapa is the seventh chief minister of Bagmati Province.

During the first term of the provincial assembly, Dor Mani Paudel of the CPN-UML became chief minister in 2017, followed by Asta Laxmi Shakya in 2021. After the UML split, Rajendra Prasad Pandey of the CPN (Unified Socialist) became chief minister in the same year.

During the second term, Shalikram Jammarkattel of the CPN (Maoist Centre) became chief minister in 2022, followed by Bahadur Singh Lama of the Nepali Congress in 2024 and Indra Bahadur Baniya of the Nepali Congress in 2025.

title.rendered: Basudev flash flood claims 2 girls, 1 still missing

content.rendered:
Hetauda, August 20

It was almost dusk last Tuesday. Four girls were returning home after school from Nirmal Secondary School in Bastipur. The Basudev Khahare stream in Hetauda Sub-Metropolitan City-19, which lies between their school and homes, was familiar to them. However, the stream had swollen unusually that evening.

A sudden flash flood swept all four girls away in different directions as they attempted to cross the stream. Two girls died, one remains missing, and one managed to survive.

According to 13-year-old Seema Blon of Dadagaun, Hetauda-19, who survived the incident, the four girls were crossing the stream while holding hands. Eight-year-old Roshani Syangtan was the first to be swept away, followed by 11-year-old Sumitra Blon and then Seema and the other girl.

After the current dragged Seema downstream, her hand caught a bush on the bank, allowing her to pull herself out of the water. She sustained minor injuries and was taken to Hetauda Hospital for treatment.

Residents had already begun searching for the other girls when Seema emerged from the stream. Police teams from the Area Police Office, Nawalpur, and the District Police Office, Makwanpur, were mobilised after receiving information about the incident. A team of 20 police personnel led by SP Shyam Bahadur Khatri was deployed for the search.

Another team of 11 police personnel led by Inspector Bijayraj Timalsina from the Bagmati Province Disaster Management Battalion and a 17-member Armed Police Force team led by DSP Nibankumar Khadka from APF No. 14 Battalion also joined the search. The Nepal Army and residents were also involved.

During the search, eight-year-old Roshani, daughter of Deep Syangtan of Bastipur, Hetauda-19, was found trapped in the roots of a tree about 600 meters downstream from the incident site. She was pronounced dead by doctors after being taken to hospital.

The bodies of 11-year-old Sumitra, daughter of Tikaram Blon, and 12-year-old Binita, daughter of Rajkumar Blon, could not be found overnight. Darkness, rising water levels and stones and debris carried by the stream made the search difficult.

Nepal Police and Armed Police Force teams resumed the search downstream early Wednesday morning. Binita was found dead about four kilometres downstream from the point where she was swept away. Sumitra remains missing.

DSP Madhav Prasad Kafle, spokesperson for the District Police Office, Makwanpur, said the search for Sumitra was continuing. According to Narnath Subedi, ward chairperson of Hetauda-19, security personnel and residents are searching for her in the lower reaches of the Basudev stream.

Of the four girls returning home from school, two have died, one remains missing, and one survived. The Basudev flash flood has taken daughters from two families and left another family waiting in hope of finding their daughter.

The incident is not the first water-related fatality recorded in Makwanpur in the current fiscal year. On the second day of the fiscal year, around 14-year-old Yukesh Rai drowned in a water-filled pit near the Karra River in Rohini Colony, Hetauda-6.

About two weeks later, a sudden flash flood in Chiruwa Khola in Naya Damaar, Bakaiya Rural Municipality-4, swept away two women. Forty-one-year-old Tara Blon and 50-year-old Sunmaya Waiba were caught in the flood while crossing the stream. Local residents rescued both women in an injured condition. Tara, who was brought to a hospital in Hetauda after receiving first aid, died during treatment on Shrawan 19. Sunmaya recovered and returned home.

The incidents at Karra, Chiruwa Khola and Basudev Khahare were different in nature. The death at Karra occurred when a person drowned while swimming, while the incidents at Chiruwa and Basudev involved people being swept away by sudden flash floods while crossing streams. These incidents highlight the risks posed by rivers, streams, gullies and water-filled pits in the district during the monsoon.

According to the District Police Office, Makwanpur, four people have died from drowning or being swept away by water in the current fiscal year. In fiscal year 2082/83 BS, Makwanpur recorded six such incidents, resulting in four deaths, one injury and one person reported missing. One of those who died was a girl.

title.rendered: Nepali Congress dissident faction to move court seeking halt to general convention process

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 20

The dissident faction of the Nepali Congress has decided to move court seeking a halt to the party’s 15th General Convention process.

A meeting of senior leaders from the faction held at the residence of Dr Shashank Koirala in Maharajgunj on Thursday decided to file a petition seeking an immediate suspension of the convention process.

Min Bishwakarma, coordinator of the faction’s publicity committee, confirmed the decision.

“The meeting decided to file a petition in court as soon as possible, seeking a halt to the general convention. The petition will be registered by Friday,” Bishwakarma said.

The dissident faction argues that the party should not proceed with the convention process as a dispute over the party’s official status is set to be reheard by the court.

The party, however, has already moved ahead with preparations for the convention.

According to the latest decision of the Central Election Committee, the ward-level conventions are scheduled to be held on September 9.

The Nepali Congress has retained its earlier decision to hold its 15th General Convention in Kathmandu from October 2 to 5, while revising the schedule for conventions at lower levels.

title.rendered: Lamichhane warns 2/3 majority alone not enough for constitutional amendment

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 20

Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) chair Rabi Lamichhane has said a two-thirds majority in the House of Representatives alone is not sufficient to amend Nepal’s Constitution.

Speaking at the House State Affairs and Good Governance Committee meeting on Thursday, Lamichhane urged RSP lawmakers to exercise caution when raising the issue of constitutional amendment.

“Some colleagues have said that we will amend the Constitution. Securing a two-thirds majority in the House of Representatives is not, by itself, enough for a constitutional amendment,” Lamichhane said.

He said lawmakers must consider the sensitivity of the issue and pay attention to the constitutional and legal provisions governing amendments.

Lamichhane said he welcomed the position that the RSP would support the government, provided it was consistent with the facts, law and Constitution.

“The spirit is right. But we have to keep the facts, law and Constitution in mind,” he said.

He stressed that political parties should work within the existing constitutional framework and focus on fulfilling the mandate given by the people as fully as possible.

Lamichhane also cautioned lawmakers against making sweeping allegations against constitutional bodies and their officials.

“We cannot simply say that the courts belong to one party and this institution belongs to another,” he said, arguing that officials of constitutional bodies are appointed under the provisions of the Constitution to perform responsibilities assigned to them.

He said excessive allegations against institutions and their leaders could undermine their dignity and credibility.

Lamichhane said he was not defending individuals but was concerned about protecting the integrity of institutions.

“My realisation is that if we keep weakening institutions, it will ultimately weaken democracy,” he said.

He warned that attempts to undermine democratic institutions out of personal grievances could gradually erode their strength and eventually reduce public trust in them to zero.

“That will ultimately take democracy and the system to a point of collapse,” he said.

Lamichhane said he did not want a society in which no one respects or trusts anyone else.

He argued that any constitutional amendment should seek to strengthen the democratic system rather than weaken it.

“If possible, an amendment should add one or two bricks to the system; if not, we should at least find a way to prevent its erosion while resolving the problems,” Lamichhane said.

content.rendered:
Canberra, August 20

Australia’s unemployment rate rose to 4.5 percent in July. According to government data released Thursday, the increase came even though economists had forecast the rate would hold steady at 4.4 percent.

According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS), the number of employed people fell by 15,800 between June and July, while the number of unemployed rose by 4,200. July’s unemployment rate is among the highest since November 2021.

According to ABS head of labour statistics Sean Crick, male employment fell by 11,000 and female employment by 5,000 in July. He said that while the number of women working part-time fell by 22,000, the number of women working full-time rose by 17,000.

Total hours worked fell by 0.6 percent over the period, dropping to 1.99 billion hours. The ABS also reported that the participation rate among the working-age population, those employed or looking for work, fell from 67 percent in June to 66.9 percent in July.

–RSS/Xinhua

title.rendered: Foreign aid sources shrinking, Nepal turning to private capital: Finance Minister

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 20

Finance Minister Dr Swarnim Wagle has said foreign aid to Nepal has been declining, with sources of grants and concessional loans becoming increasingly limited.

Speaking at a meeting of the Public Accounts Committee on Thursday, Wagle said Nepal now needs to mobilise private capital as an alternative, as traditional sources of foreign assistance continue to shrink.

According to Wagle, Nepal has relied on foreign aid and loans since its first budget to finance expenditures that could not be covered by domestic revenue. However, as the economy and the size of the national budget have grown, the share of foreign grants has declined.

“Concessional resources are narrowing. Almost all of Nepal’s major infrastructure projects were built using these loans,” Wagle said. “Traditional sources of foreign aid are now drying up. So, we are moving towards new sources of private capital.”

Wagle said the current budget has set a target of borrowing around Rs 212 billion in foreign loans, while foreign grants have been estimated at around Rs 62 billion. However, although grants of Rs 48 billion to Rs 52 billion have been projected in recent budgets, actual receipts have generally remained around Rs 10 billion to Rs 15 billion.

He said highly concessional loans, which carry interest rates of around 1% to 1.5%, with no repayment required for the first eight years and repayment periods extending up to 40 years, are gradually becoming unavailable.

Wagle said foreign assistance should be analysed separately, including aid received through NGOs and international NGOs, bilateral grants and multilateral concessional loans.

He noted that assistance through INGOs has been declining and now represents a relatively small share compared with the size of Nepal’s budget and economy.

According to Wagle, concessional loans from multilateral development partners remain an important source of development financing. However, he warned that financing conditions are becoming increasingly difficult, with rising interest rates, shorter grace periods and shorter maturity periods, while competition for limited concessional resources is also increasing.

“We are heading into an extremely challenging phase,” he said.

title.rendered: Toddler missing for two days found safe in Nawalparasi forest

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 20

A two-and-a-half-year-old boy who had been missing for two days in a community forest east of Nawalparasi has been rescued safely. Shiwan Tamang, two and a half, went missing from Gaindakot Municipality-14, Bhagar, in eastern Nawalparasi, and was found safe in a community forest two days later.

At 7 am on August 18, Shiwan’s grandmother, Hem Kumari Ale, had gone to the Shankhadevi Community Forest near their home to pick mushrooms. When she returned home, Shiwan was not there.

After residents and neighbours searched the forest area without finding him, they filed a report at the Area Police Office.

Teams from the Area Police Office Gaindakot, Area Police Office Rajahar, and a temporary police post at Beldiya were mobilised alongside residents to search for Shiwan.

During the search, Shiwan was found at 10 am on Thursday near the head of the Bhagar stream, within the Shankhadevi Community Forest in Gaindakot Municipality-14.

Police said the boy, rescued safely, was handed over to relatives after completing the necessary procedures.

title.rendered: Mastercard, MOCO launch QR payment solution for international visitors in Nepal

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 20

International visitors to Nepal can now use their existing Mastercard credit and debit cards to make digital payments at merchants accepting NepalPay and Fonepay QR codes nationwide.

Mastercard on Wednesday announced the launch of its Pay Local solution in Nepal in partnership with MOCO, a card-based digital wallet and unified QR payment platform.

Under the new service, international travellers can link eligible Mastercard cards to the MOCO Travel App and make payments directly through the app without having to carry cash, exchange currency or load money into prepaid accounts.

The MOCO Travel App is available on both the Apple App Store and Google Play Store.

The service can be used at hotels, restaurants, retail outlets, local markets and other tourism-related businesses accepting NepalPay and Fonepay QR payments.

“International travellers increasingly expect the simplicity, security and convenience of their everyday payment experiences to travel with them,” said Sandun Hapugoda, country manager for Sri Lanka, Maldives, Bangladesh, Bhutan and Nepal at Mastercard.

“With Mastercard Pay Local available on MOCO, visitors can use the cards they already know and trust across the country’s extensive QR payment ecosystem,” he said.

Mastercard said the service will also allow local businesses to serve international customers through their existing QR infrastructure, potentially helping them benefit from Nepal’s growing tourism sector.

The launch expands Mastercard’s Pay Local presence in Asia, following similar deployments in China, Indonesia, Malaysia, Cambodia and Sri Lanka.

Pranaya Rajbhandari, chief executive officer of FOCUSONE Payment Solutions, said the partnership would make it easier for inbound tourists to access Nepal’s QR payment ecosystem.

“Through our travel app, inbound tourists can seamlessly access Nepal’s QR payment ecosystem, making it easier to explore the country while supporting local merchants,” Rajbhandari said.

title.rendered: NEPSE rises 7 points after four-day losing streak

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 20

Nepal’s stock market rose on Thursday after declining for four consecutive trading days.

The Nepal Stock Exchange (NEPSE) index gained 7.17 points to close at 2,629 points. The market had fallen by 0.26 points on Wednesday.

The index dropped to an intraday low of 2,608 points at around 12:23 pm before recovering steadily through the rest of the trading session.

Turnover also increased. A total of Rs 4.40 billion worth of shares changed hands on Thursday, compared with Rs 3.29 billion on Wednesday.

Shares of 132 companies gained while 132 declined. Prices of 13 companies remained unchanged.

Most sectoral indices recorded movements of less than 1%.

The hydropower index posted the biggest gain, rising 0.99%. Banking gained 0.28%, investment 0.05%, life insurance 0.01%, manufacturing and processing 0.76%, and the ‘Others’ group 0.09%.

Development banks declined 0.37%, finance companies 0.19%, hotels and tourism 0.05%, microfinance 0.06%, non-life insurance 0.48% and trading 0.21%.

title.rendered: Mobile app launched to track public transport in Kathmandu Valley

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 20

The KTM Public Transport mobile application has been launched to help passengers track public vehicles operating in Kathmandu Valley and check how long a vehicle will take to reach their location.

Sunita Dangol, acting mayor of Kathmandu Metropolitan City and chairperson of the Federal Capital Urban Area Public Transport Council, launched the app at the council’s third meeting on Wednesday.

The application currently provides information on around 1,200 GPS-equipped public vehicles, with plans to expand the system to cover more vehicles.

Dangol said public transport in the Valley should be made simpler, more accessible and convenient. She stressed the need to expand night-time services and operate buses from early morning to accommodate students travelling to schools and colleges.

“Public transport is not an issue that can be confined to a single municipality. Since it connects different municipalities, it is a shared issue,” she said, calling for greater coordination among local governments.

The council has also approved programs to determine bus stops and pick-and-drop points, introduce night bus services, install GPS-based public transport information systems at major bus stops and bus parks, and prepare a legal framework for cashless fares.

The council also plans campaigns to encourage passengers to obtain tickets and studies aimed at improving public transport services.

The council has 35 members and a nine-member steering committee to streamline its decision-making process.

title.rendered: Parliamentary committee directs govt to reform foreign aid management

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 20

The Public Accounts Committee of the House of Representatives has directed the government to introduce policy and institutional reforms to ensure foreign aid is mobilised in line with the principle of results-oriented spending.

A meeting of the committee held at Singha Durbar on Thursday directed the government to ensure that foreign aid in the coming days is aligned with national priorities, the budget system, public funds, transparency, auditing and results-based spending.

The committee also directed the government to bring all forms of foreign aid— whether cash, in-kind or technical — into the national budget system and government treasury as far as possible and subject them to mandatory auditing.

Committee Chair Bharat Bahadur Khadka said the Ministry of Finance had been instructed to include and allocate foreign-funded resources in the annual budget only after the availability of the assistance had been confirmed.

The ministry was also directed to ensure timely reimbursement of expenses made through foreign aid to minimise the additional financial burden on the government’s domestic resources caused by delays.

The committee called for an integrated record of foreign aid commitments, actual receipts, expenditure, utilisation and reimbursements, with mandatory updates in the relevant government systems.

It also directed the government to strengthen management, monitoring and implementation capacity so that projects funded through foreign aid are completed within their stipulated time and cost.

Speaking at the meeting, Finance Minister Dr Swarnim Wagle said the ministry was closely monitoring the global economic situation, the effectiveness of foreign aid and new financial strategies Nepal should adopt.

Wagle said donor countries were increasingly imposing stricter conditions on aid or seeking to spend the funds through their own mechanisms to prevent misuse of taxpayers’ money.

Traditional sources of foreign aid, he said, were no longer sufficient or effective, prompting Nepal to explore alternative sources of financing.

The finance minister said alternative financing sources had already been given policy priority in the national budget and that the government was working to manage the transitional period while adapting to the changing global economic order.

title.rendered: Seriously injured Nepali in Poland awaits rescue

content.rendered:
Khotang, August 20

The family of a Nepali youth seriously injured in a road accident in Poland has accused the government of failing to take adequate steps to bring him back to Nepal.

Amitkumar Chaudhary of Itahari Sub-Metropolitan City-16, Sunsari, was seriously injured in a road accident in Poland. His family said the Nepal government has shown little concern about his rescue and repatriation.

According to his family, Chaudhary went to Poland three years ago for foreign employment. He was seriously injured in a road accident on Baisakh 5 and is currently receiving treatment at the Regional Hospital in Sosnowiec City, Poland, according to Parsuram Dhimal, who is in Poland.

Chaudhary’s wife, Usha Chaudhary, appealed to the Non-Resident Nepali Association (NRNA) Poland for assistance on Ashadh 19. She said she had repeatedly requested help from the Foreign Employment Board, Ministry of Labour and Ministry of Foreign Affairs, but the government had not responded adequately.

Usha said the family’s financial situation does not allow them to cover the costs of repatriation, including airfare, which forced her to seek help from the NRNA.

Lawmaker Ashok Kumar Chaudhary had also raised the issue in Parliament, but the family said the government has yet to respond.

Meanwhile, NRNA Poland has started collecting donations to bring Chaudhary back to Nepal through the “Bring Amitkumar Chaudhary Home” campaign.

title.rendered: Landslide continues in Ratapani, 6 families displaced

A landslide has been continuously occurring in the Ratapani settlement of Surnaya Rural Municipality-8 in Baitadi, putting the entire settlement at risk. Six families have already been displaced, while 19 other houses remain at risk.

Resident Tej Bohara said the landslide has been occurring continuously for the past week.

“The landslide has been occurring continuously. Twenty-five families are living in fear,” he said. “So far, six families have been displaced. The displaced families are taking shelter with their neighbours.”

The landslide has damaged maize crops planted across around 25 to 30 ropanis of land. It has also disrupted the movement of students and residents.

“Landslides occur almost every day, and it is frightening even to walk around. The fear increases whenever it rains,” said resident Ramsingh Bohara.

Surnaya Rural Municipality Chairperson Ammar Bahadur Kunwar said the Ratapani settlement, which is at high risk from landslides, needs to be relocated.

“The landslide has been troubling this area for a long time, and the situation has worsened recently,” he said. “There is no alternative to relocating the settlement. We are coordinating with the relevant authorities.”

title.rendered: RSP lawmaker questions CIAA chief Prem Kumar Rai’s moral grounds to remain in office

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 20

Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) lawmaker Yagyamani Neupane has questioned the moral grounds of Commission for Investigation of Abuse of Authority (CIAA) Chief Commissioner Prem Kumar Rai to continue in office, citing his alleged links to several controversial cases and court rulings.

Neupane raised the questions during a meeting of the parliamentary committee attended by Rai and other CIAA officials.

Referring to the Supreme Court’s ruling on the wide-body aircraft procurement case, Neupane said the court had mentioned that the procurement process for two wide-body aircraft had moved forward following a decision of the Nepal Airlines Corporation board chaired by Rai, who was then secretary at the Ministry of Culture, Tourism and Civil Aviation.

Neupane questioned why Rai was not made a defendant in the case despite his name being mentioned in connection with the procurement process.

He argued that prosecuting some officials involved in the same process while not prosecuting others amounted to selective prosecution.

“Selective prosecution is contrary to the principle of equal justice, the right to equality and the principle of natural justice,” Neupane said.

He also raised questions about Rai’s alleged involvement in the Nepal Oil Corporation land acquisition case, saying that the parliamentary Public Accounts Committee had specifically mentioned Rai’s name. He also referred to issues surrounding Gautam Buddha International Airport in Bhairahawa.

Neupane then brought up the fake Bhutanese refugee scam, saying he had obtained court documents in his capacity as a lawyer in the case.

Reading from the statement of accused Sanu Bhandari, Neupane alleged that Bhandari had claimed that then-secretary Prem Kumar Rai’s vehicle was used to deliver Rs 10 million in cash and that Rai later called him to his office.

According to the statement read out by Neupane, Bhandari claimed Rai told him that his work would be done and asked him to leave.

Neupane said these issues raised serious questions about Rai’s ethical grounds for continuing as CIAA chief.

“On this basis, Chief Commissioner, do you have the moral grounds to remain in office? Does the law allow you to continue in that position? This is my second question. I want an answer,” Neupane said.

title.rendered: Protesters surround Simara Police Office over Garima’s murder

content.rendered:
Furious residents have shut down rural roads within Jitpursimara Sub-Metropolitan City in Bara to protest the murder of three-year-old Garima Chaudhary following her rape.

Private and community schools within Jitpursimara Sub-Metropolitan City held mourning assemblies and closed on Thursday.

Calling the brutal incident against the three-year-old girl a shock to the entire education sector, private and community schools issued a statement demanding the strictest possible action against those responsible.

Protesters, saying police failed to act in time and that this led to the girl’s murder, continued their agitation today, which began on Wednesday.

Protesters have been burning tyres and demonstrating on rural roads within the sub-metropolitan city since early Thursday morning. Traffic on the Birgunj-Pathalaiya road section, closed since Wednesday afternoon, has still not resumed.

Locals accuse the Area Police Office of serious negligence in the search for Garima. They allege that although her father filed a report at the Simara Area Police Office in time after she went missing, police failed to show urgency in the search.

Locals are now protesting, demanding action against DSP Dilip Chhetri, in-charge of the Simara Area Police Office.

Surrounding the Area Police Office in Simara, protesters put forward their demand for action against DSP Chhetri.

Protesters, burning tyres, have completely halted traffic on the Simara-Dumarwana, Piluwa-Wadaharwa, Simara-Jitpur and Pathalaiya-Simara road sections within Jitpursimara Sub-Metropolitan City.

The Bara District Administration has said it remains positive about addressing the protesters’ demands and is attempting dialogue.

Chief District Officer Dharmendra Mishra said preparations were underway for decisive talks later today to address the protesters’ demands.

“We have already arrested the accused. As for the allegations of police negligence raised by locals, we are verifying that ourselves,” CDO Mishra said.

title.rendered: Govt planning to allow private sector to collect biometric data of Nepalis abroad

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 20

The government is preparing to allow private-sector entities to collect biometric data from Nepali citizens living abroad as part of the passport application process.

The provision has been proposed in the Passport (First Amendment) Bill, 2026, registered in the House of Representatives by Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal on July 30.

Under the proposed amendment, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs would be able to arrange for private companies or other institutions to collect passport applications along with biometric data from Nepalis abroad.

Currently, biometric collection is handled exclusively through government agencies and Nepali diplomatic missions. Nepali citizens applying for passports abroad must generally appear in person at the relevant embassy or consulate to provide their biometric data.

Concerns over sensitive data

The proposed provision has raised concerns among lawmakers over the security and potential misuse of sensitive personal data.

Rastriya Swatantra Party lawmaker Rima Bishwakarma questioned whether the bill provides adequate safeguards against the misuse of biometric data.

She said the bill lacks clear standards for preventing the misuse of sensitive personal data and stressed the need for explicit legal provisions on data security, use, protection and accountability.

Nepali Congress whip Nishkal Rai also raised concerns about who would control citizens’ data if private companies were allowed to collect it.

He questioned what would happen in cases of data misuse, leaks, subcontractor access, transfers to foreign jurisdictions, incorrect identity matching or failure to destroy data when required.

Rai argued that the bill should establish a clear chain of accountability rather than leaving major decisions concerning citizens’ sensitive information to the executive.

Government cites difficulties faced by Nepalis abroad

Foreign Minister Khanal defended the proposed provision, saying it is intended to make passport services more accessible to Nepalis living far from diplomatic missions.

He said Nepal has embassies in only limited locations while Nepalis are increasingly dispersed across different countries. Requiring citizens to travel long distances simply to provide biometric data can impose significant costs and inconvenience.

Khanal cited Australia as an example, noting that Nepal’s embassy is in Canberra while a large Nepali population lives in Sydney. Travelling from Sydney to Canberra for passport-related services can cost hundreds of dollars in airfare alone, in addition to accommodation expenses.

He said similar challenges exist in Europe, where Nepal does not have diplomatic missions in many countries.

“That’s why we have introduced the concept of third-party provision to see whether the service can be made easier,” Khanal said, adding that the ministry is studying possible arrangements with established institutions that already handle similar services internationally.

Bill moves forward

The bill underwent a preliminary discussion in the House of Representatives on August 18. Parliament subsequently approved a proposal to consider the bill, opening a 72-hour window for lawmakers to submit amendments.

The provision allowing private-sector collection of biometric data is expected to receive further scrutiny during clause-by-clause discussions.

The key issue will be whether the government can expand access to passport services without compromising the security and control of citizens’ biometric data.

title.rendered: St. Xavier’s College stages Bichitra Baje

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 20

The Department of Major Arts at St. Xavier’s College, Kathmandu, has begun its three-day theatre run of Bichitra Baje. It is a Nepali adaptation of Gabriel García Márquez’s acclaimed short story A Very Old Man with Enormous Wings.​

The first show took place on Thursday at Miller Hall, Loyola Campus, Thapathali.

There will be two more shows on August 21 at 8:30 a.m. and 12:00 p.m., and the final two shows on August 22 at 11:30 a.m. and 3:00 p.m.

Written by Kritika Koirala and Raunak Karki, two students in the Department of Major Arts, Bichitra Baje sets the story in a Nepali setting. It follows a village that encounters a mysterious old man with wings. As the villagers react to his arrival with curiosity, fear, faith, and exploitation, the play explores kindness, compassion, and how people treat those who are different from them. The story also follows Punam, a young girl who responds to the old man with care and respect.

The production is a student-led initiative, with students taking responsibility for different aspects of the play under their teachers’ guidance and mentorship. From acting and writing to stage preparation and props, students have been actively involved in bringing the production to life. The handmade props, in particular, reflect their creative effort and hands-on involvement. Working together throughout the production has also helped them strengthen their teamwork, coordination, and ability to work as a group.​

This play is part of the students’ academic engagement with drama. It aims to give them practical experience in theatre, while also creating a space for students to develop their confidence, creativity and teamwork.

A special feature of this year’s play is its focus on accessibility. The department has set up live audio descriptions for visually impaired audience members. A volunteer will describe key visual parts of the performance, such as movements, expressions, costumes, and actions, using a live Google Meet session. Earphones and internet access will be provided to help with this service.​

Fr. Dr Augustine Thomas, S.J., Principal of St. Xavier’s College, said, “Bichitra Baje is a remarkable example of how our students can transform a powerful literary work into a meaningful theatrical experience. The play invites us to look beyond appearances and differences and rediscover the value of human dignity. I am proud of our students for using the stage to make us reflect on what it means to be truly human.”

Shishir Kumar Bhusal, Head of the Department of Major Arts, said, “It is so heartwarming to witness the play performed by our students here at St. Xavier’s College. The play, Bichitra Baje, stages why human literacy, empathy, emotional intelligence, and interpersonal communication are significant to discuss in today’s society.”

title.rendered: 4 countries agree to exchange pre-arrival customs data

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 20

Nepal and three other countries have signed an agreement to exchange pre-arrival information on goods at customs.

The Department of Customs said the memorandum of understanding was signed among member countries of the South Asia Subregional Economic Cooperation (SASEC) to facilitate trade and strengthen customs controls.

The agreement was signed by the customs administrations of Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh and the Maldives during the 14th SASEC Subgroup Meeting held in the Maldives. On behalf of Nepal, Director General of the Department of Customs Yamlal Bhusal signed the agreement.

According to the department, the main objective of the agreement is to facilitate the exchange of pre-arrival information on goods among member countries. This will allow customs authorities to analyse available information and manage risks before goods arrive at customs offices.

The department said the arrangement will help strengthen customs controls and facilitate faster and more efficient clearance of goods. It is also expected to reduce the time and cost involved in trade procedures and make foreign trade more convenient, transparent and predictable.

Nepal and India had previously signed a similar memorandum of understanding. The agreement was signed between the Department of Customs and India’s Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs in New Delhi in the first week of Magh, 2082 BS.

Both countries expect the arrangement to strengthen cooperation between their customs administrations and facilitate risk analysis by exchanging data on goods before their arrival, making it easier to monitor and regulate shipments identified as high-risk.

The system is also expected to provide greater facilitation to compliant businesses and make customs clearance faster and more efficient. Pre-arrival data exchange among major trading partners is an established international practice aimed at facilitating trade through risk management.

The RSP had also instructed its lawmakers to maintain decorum in their presentations.

title.rendered: DICL to extract 96 million tonnes iron ore

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 20

Dhaubadi Iron Company Limited has prepared a plan for mining iron ore at its mining site located in Hupsekot Rural Municipality-5, Dhaubadi, Nawalparasi. The company has submitted a report to the Department of Mines and Geology with a plan to extract 96 million tonnes of iron ore from the mine spread over about 41 square kilometres.

The mining area has been divided into two parts: the Dhaubadi Pokhari block and the Durlung block. The Dhaubadi Pokhari block covers 25 square kilometres, while the Durlung block spans 16 square kilometres. After this plan is approved, the company has said it will carry out further exploration and mining operations related to the iron deposits. Dhaubadi Iron Company Limited was established in 2076 BS with the aim of commercially producing iron.

It is an undertaking of the Government of Nepal. The company’s director, Shailesh Kumar Thapa, informed that drilling work of 1,500 meters was completed at 12 different locations to test underground iron ore samples. The company has stated that the environmental impact assessment work is currently underway and the work to prepare the Detailed Project Report (DPR) will also be started soon.

Director Thapa said that once the mine is operational, the iron products produced are expected to replace about 25 per cent of the country’s overall import demand. He believes that mining operations will create a large number of jobs and contribute to the national economy. The company has stated that the necessary infrastructure and road upgrades to reach the mine are underway.

Dolpa administration distributes border passes to residents for China crossings

content.rendered:
Dolpa, August 20

The District Administration Office, Dolpa, has begun distributing border passes to residents of three local units to facilitate travel and trade across the Nepal-China border.

The passes are being issued in coordination with local governments for access to the Marim La and Kato border crossings. More than 350 residents have received passes for the Kato crossing, according to the administration.

Officials have been visiting villages in Upper Dolpa to distribute the passes, aiming to make regular cross-border movement and trade easier for residents living near the Chinese border.

According to Administration Section officer Datta Lama, who has been deployed by the administration office, officials have been distributing the passes across Upper Dolpa for the past 15 days.

Despite the difficult terrain, officials have been travelling to remote settlements to provide the service locally rather than requiring residents to travel to the district headquarters.

50 passes distributed in Dho

So far, 50 border passes have been distributed in Dho of Dolpo Buddha Rural Municipality.

Lama said the process has been largely completed in Dho, although some residents of wards 1, 2 and 3 are yet to receive their passes. The administration is preparing to issue passes to those who complete the required procedures.

Officials have yet to reach wards 7, 8 and 9 of Shey Phoksundo Rural Municipality to distribute the passes because of the difficult geography and poor road access.

Around 200 passes have been distributed in other areas of the rural municipality so far, Lama said.

The administration said it is preparing to reach the remaining settlements and provide passes to eligible residents.

The administration said border passes have already been distributed to all eligible residents of Chharka Tangsong Rural Municipality.

Residents of the three Upper Dolpa local units have longstanding social and commercial ties with Tibet. Many rely on the border crossings to purchase daily necessities and conduct trade.

Because most settlements in Upper Dolpa have limited road and transport access, residents rely heavily on Tibet for essential goods such as rice, flour, salt and cooking oil.

The Marim La crossing, in particular, serves as an important trade and supply route for communities in Upper Dolpa. Residents travel to Tibet to purchase goods and return to their villages through the border crossing.

The border passes are therefore considered important for both local trade and daily movement.

Officials said distributing the passes directly in villages will save residents the time and expense of travelling to the district headquarters, particularly those living in remote settlements.

The administration has said it will continue coordinating with local governments to distribute passes to residents who have yet to receive them.

Nepali Congress lawmaker Arjun Narsingh KC has proposed forming a special task force to trace money held in foreign banks by high-ranking Nepali individuals.

Recalling that Bangladesh formed a special task force after the Gen Z movement to investigate how much money its high-ranking officials held in banks around the world, KC said Bangladesh had also written to banks worldwide as part of the investigation.

He said Nepal should undertake a similar initiative.

“Can you (the Rastriya Swatantra Party government), in coordination with the Nepal Rastra Bank and the Commission for Investigation of Abuse of Authority, establish a special commission to investigate and control corruption taking place outside the country?” lawmaker KC asked. “I don’t think there is enough courage for this, but I have still proposed that such an investigation be carried out.”

He also urged the government to pay attention to corruption taking place abroad.

“Forgive me, but corruption is currently taking place on the largest scale outside the country,” he said. “I don’t want to get into who is involved at this point. But there are reports that money is being held in Singapore, Cambodia, Swiss banks and elsewhere around the world.”

title.rendered: Egg prices rise for fifth time since Shrawan

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 20

Egg prices have increased again with the start of Bhadra. The Nepal Layers Poultry Farmers Association has set new farm-gate support prices for eggs, effective from Thursday.

Based on Chitwan as the reference market, the new support prices have increased for all grades of eggs.

Under the new price list, an XL egg now costs Rs 590 per crate. The price of a large egg has been set at Rs 575 per crate, while a medium egg costs Rs 535 per crate. The price of small eggs has been maintained at Rs 3,200 per box.

The association has increased the price by Rs 15 per crate in less than a week. Previously, effective from August 15, the association had set the prices of XL, large and medium eggs at Rs 575, Rs 560 and Rs 520 per crate, respectively.

Egg prices have been steadily rising in recent weeks. The association had already raised the support price four times during Shrawan alone. At the beginning of Shrawan, the price of XL eggs was set at Rs 525 per crate, which had risen to Rs 575 by the end of the month.

With the beginning of Bhadra, another Rs 15 has been added, bringing the price of XL eggs to Rs 590 per crate.

Poultry businesses attribute the continued rise in egg prices mainly to declining production.

Association Chairperson Binod Pokharel said poultry farmers have been forced to raise prices because bird flu outbreaks led to the culling of large numbers of chickens, while chicken deaths have caused a significant decline in egg production, making it difficult to meet demand.

title.rendered: CIAA says Rs 700 million commission allegation in security press deal under investigation

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 20

The Commission for Investigation of Abuse of Authority (CIAA) has said a complaint alleging that Rs 700 million was negotiated as commission in the procurement of a security printing press remains under detailed investigation.

The CIAA disclosed the status of the case during a meeting of the House of Representatives’ State Affairs and Good Governance Committee on Thursday. Acting CIAA Secretary Padma Mainali provided the information while briefing lawmakers on the commission’s activities.

The case involves former Communications Minister Gokul Baskota, who was accused of negotiating a commission in connection with the proposed procurement of a security printing press.

The CIAA began investigating the matter after a complaint was filed following the release of an audio recording in February 2020. The recording purportedly captured a conversation between Baskota and Vijay Prakash Mishra, the Nepal representative of a Swiss company involved in the security printing press project, regarding the procurement cost and alleged commission.

The audio sparked widespread controversy, and Baskota subsequently resigned as communications minister.

The complaint was then registered with the CIAA, which launched an investigation into the allegations.

In 2023, then-CIAA Chief Commissioner Prem Kumar Rai had also told the Public Accounts Committee that the commission was investigating the alleged Rs 700 million commission case.

The CIAA reiterated on Thursday that the complaint concerning the alleged commission negotiation in the security press procurement remains under detailed investigation.

title.rendered: CIAA calls for law requiring proof of source of funds for large share investments

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 20

The Commission for Investigation of Abuse of Authority (CIAA) has recommended that the government introduce a legal provision requiring investors to verify the source of funds for share investments above a specified threshold.

The anti-graft body made the recommendation through its annual report for the fiscal year 2024/25, warning that investments in shares could potentially be used for money laundering.

“Since there is a possibility of money laundering through investments in shares, arrangements should be made to verify the source of assets for amounts above a certain threshold,” the CIAA said in its report.

The commission said the recommendation is new and was not included in its suggestions made in the previous fiscal year.

The CIAA has also called for measures to prevent conflicts of interest among companies issuing shares, credit rating agencies, underwriters and officials responsible for approving public offerings.

It has further urged authorities to control collusion and unauthorized access to systems operated by the Nepal Stock Exchange (NEPSE) that could be used to manipulate the share market.

The CIAA’s 35th annual report for fiscal year 2024/25 was presented to the House of Representatives on July 9. Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs Minister Sobita Gautam presented the report on behalf of Prime Minister Balen Shah.

Meanwhile, the House Committee on State Affairs and Good Governance is scheduled to discuss the CIAA’s activities and issues raised in its annual report with the commission’s officials. The meeting is scheduled for 11 am today at the committee hall in Singha Durbar.

Other recommendations to Finance Ministry

The CIAA has made several other recommendations to the Ministry of Finance, including expanding the coverage of the Central Billing Monitoring System (CBMS) so that the Inland Revenue Department can directly monitor taxpayers’ transactions.

It has also recommended signing memorandums of understanding with countries that have Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements (DTAAs) with Nepal to facilitate the use of e-invoicing data.

To curb the use of fake invoices, the commission has suggested developing and implementing a central billing software system.

The CIAA has also recommended developing an Integrated Non-Tax System (INTS) software to automate records of non-tax revenue.

It has further called for strict implementation of a system requiring all payments received by civil servants through government systems to be mandatorily entered into the tax system.
