title.rendered: 6 trending passions gaining popularity among Gen Z

content.rendered:
Today’s younger generation has very different lifestyles, interests and forms of entertainment compared with previous generations. Although this generation has grown up with digital technology, smartphones and social media and spends a significant amount of time on screens, it is increasingly drawn to passions and activities that offer a break from screens while promoting mental peace, creativity, self-expression and social connections.

Social media, in particular, has played an important role in giving old hobbies a new and popular identity. Activities once associated with grandparents, such as knitting, crochet, baking and birdwatching, have now become “cool” and trending passions among young people. Likewise, gaming, digital art and music production bring technology and creativity together.

These passions are not merely ways to pass the time. Some can help reduce stress, improve concentration, develop new skills, expand social networks and even become sources of income in the future.

1. Birdwatching

Birdwatching, the activity of observing birds and identifying their species, is no longer limited to older generations. Young people are increasingly viewing it as an interesting way to connect with nature, practice photography, and learn new things.

Mobile apps and digital technology have made birdwatching easier. Various apps allow users to identify birds by their calls, record the location and time of sightings, and maintain records of the birds they have observed. Searching for different bird species has become an exciting experience for many young people, similar to a “real-life Pokémon hunt.” The excitement of photographing rare birds and keeping records of sightings has made the activity even more entertaining.

Young people often share photos and videos of birds they have captured on social media. This has also helped create online communities among people with similar interests. Another important aspect of birdwatching is that it can increase interest in nature conservation. Learning about different bird species and their habitats can encourage young people to become more interested in environmental protection.

2. Digital art and music production

Art and music have always been popular among young people. However, advances in digital technology have significantly changed how art is created and music is produced.

In the past, producing music required expensive studios and extensive equipment. Today, beats, music and digital art can be created with nothing more than a computer, tablet or smartphone. Young people are increasingly interested in digital illustration, graphic design, animation, photography, video editing and producing their own music. These activities give them opportunities to showcase their talents.

One of the biggest advantages of digital art and music production is that they can eventually be turned into careers in freelancing, content creation, design, music production and digital marketing. Social media has also provided a major platform for young creators. By posting their work online, they can reach audiences not only in their own countries but around the world.

3. Knitting, crochet and crafting

Once dismissed as “grandmothers’ work,” knitting and crochet are becoming popular again among young people. Making their own clothes, bags, hats, toys, home décor and accessories by hand is increasingly common.

Trends such as “granny-core,” inspired by the lifestyle, clothing, handicrafts and domestic skills of older generations, have made crochet and knitting even more popular among young people. Spending time crocheting with friends, learning handicrafts or organising “craft nights” has also become a fun social activity.

The popularity of crafting is also linked to the concept of sustainable fashion. Making things oneself instead of buying new products, reusing old clothes and choosing durable materials can help reduce waste. Crafting can also help develop patience, concentration, manual skills and creative thinking.

4. Home baking

Making cakes, cookies, bread and other baked goods at home is also becoming increasingly popular among young people. The process of making sourdough bread, in particular, has gained considerable attention on social media.

Young people share photos and videos documenting everything from their first attempts at making bread to their progress as they become better bakers. Sharing recipes, ingredient measurements and baking tips has turned the hobby into a popular form of online content.

Young people are not limited to traditional recipes. Fusion baking, which combines different flavours, as well as healthier baking using less sugar and ingredients such as fruits, nuts and whole grains, is also gaining popularity. Home baking can develop creativity, patience and cooking skills while potentially providing a foundation for starting a small business.

5. Jigsaw puzzles and gaming

Gaming was once viewed mainly as a form of entertainment or a way to pass the time. Today, however, the gaming world is much broader. Strategy, puzzle, competitive and cooperative games offer young people both challenges and entertainment. Jigsaw puzzles are also making a comeback among the younger generation. Activities such as “puzzle and chill,” popular on social media, are encouraging people to sit together in groups and solve puzzles.

Although digital gaming is screen-based, activities such as jigsaw puzzles provide an opportunity to spend some time away from digital devices. Solving puzzles encourages concentration, problem-solving and patience.

Online gaming can bring people from different parts of the world together in a single community. Playing with friends, livestreaming and participating in gaming communities are creating new forms of social interaction. However, time management and balance are important when gaming. Spending long periods continuously in front of a screen can affect daily life, sleep, studies or work, so entertainment should be kept in balance.

6. Desire to step outside the digital world

Young people who spend significant amounts of time in the digital world are also becoming interested in activities that bring them closer to nature. Hiking, camping, nature walks, gardening and outdoor photography are some examples. Spending some time in nature after being constantly engaged with mobile phones, social media and online activities can provide young people with a digital break. Hiking or camping with friends can be entertaining while also strengthening social bonds.

Young people often share photos and videos from their hikes, trips and camping experiences on social media. This helps spread information about new places while also connecting people with similar interests.

Why are young people’s passions changing?

Social media and digital technology are major factors behind the changes in Gen Z’s interests. A hobby no longer needs television or magazines to become popular. Once a video of an activity goes viral on TikTok, Instagram, YouTube or another platform, the number of young people following the trend can increase rapidly.

At the same time, an interest in self-expression, creativity and personal identity has encouraged young people to explore new passions. The younger generation no longer sees hobbies simply as activities to pursue during free time. For many, they are also ways to learn new skills, connect with like-minded people and explore future income opportunities.

The growing popularity of these passions among Gen Z reflects an important shift. Young people are not trying to escape technology; rather, they are seeking balance in their lives alongside technology. Birdwatching connects them with nature, crafting encourages creativity, baking develops practical skills, digital art provides opportunities to showcase talent, puzzles and gaming offer both entertainment and challenges, while hiking and camping strengthen their connection with the natural world.

These passions, therefore, are not merely trends. When pursued in the right way, they can contribute to skill development, mental relaxation, social connections, confidence and new career opportunities. By combining traditional hobbies with modern technology and new ideas, Gen Z is reshaping the way people approach leisure and entertainment.

title.rendered: Travel time through Banke National Park reduced under revised time-card system

content.rendered:
Kohalpur, August 19

Authorities have reduced the time allotted to vehicles travelling through the Banke National Park section of the East-West Mahendra Highway under the existing time-card system.

A coordination meeting chaired by Kohalpur Municipality Mayor Purna Prasad Acharya on Tuesday decided to shorten the travel time between the Obhari and Khairi checkpoints while maintaining traffic flow through the protected area.

The meeting was attended by Banke National Park Senior Conservation Officer Birendra Prasad Kandel, Ranadhwaj Battalion commander Khim Bahadur Dangi, Kohalpur Municipality Ward 9 chair Opendranath Yogi and Ward 12 chair Birendra Shah, among others.

Under the Banke National Park Regulations, 2014, vehicles travelling at a speed of 40 kilometres per hour were allowed between 24 and 28 minutes to cover the 14.2-kilometre stretch.

The revised arrangement reduces the allotted time to between 21 and 24 minutes.

Ward 12 chair Shah said a scientific assessment showed that the distance could safely be covered within 21 to 24 minutes, leading to the decision to implement the new time limit.

He said the change would save travellers at least seven minutes.

The meeting also decided to install information boards and road signs at various locations along the highway to promote tourism, encourage coexistence between people and wildlife, and help reduce road accidents.

Kohalpur Municipality and Banke National Park will coordinate on the installation of the signs.

Authorities also agreed to promote Banke National Park as a tourism destination for the district.

In coordination with Nepalgunj Sub-Metropolitan City and other relevant agencies, large hoarding boards and information signs will be placed at Jhudwa border point, Ranjha Chowk, Nepalgunj Airport and Kohalpur Chowk.

The meeting also discussed linking park conservation with tourism promotion and local development, with participants agreeing to move forward through greater coordination among local governments and park authorities.

title.rendered: Rabi Lamichhane warns RSP lawmakers, ministers against indiscipline, urges coordination

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 19

Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) Chair Rabi Lamichhane has issued a stern warning to the party’s lawmakers and ministers, urging them to maintain parliamentary conduct, improve coordination and focus on results rather than publicity.

Lamichhane held a joint meeting with RSP lawmakers and ministers on Wednesday after concerns emerged over indiscipline among lawmakers and growing disagreements between lawmakers and ministers.

RSP parliamentary party leader and Prime Minister Balendra Shah was absent from the meeting, leaving Lamichhane to address the lawmakers and ministers on behalf of the party.

According to a leader who attended the meeting, Lamichhane told the ministers to change their working style while assuring that there would be no immediate change in the ministerial team.

Tensions have reportedly grown within the party as some lawmakers have publicly questioned the work of RSP ministers. Lamichhane instructed lawmakers to copy him when submitting questions to ministers.

“Write your questions to the ministers with a copy to me. I will also study them,” Lamichhane said. “The lawmakers have questions from the people, and lawmakers have questions for ministers. Let us strengthen coordination among the lawmakers, the party and the government.”

He also reminded the party that although the government is powerful, all opposition parties have come together against it.

‘Do not create a spectacle’

Lamichhane also raised concerns about RSP lawmakers’ conduct and attendance in Parliament.

With some lawmakers reportedly speaking in an undignified manner and skipping parliamentary meetings, he urged them to strictly follow parliamentary rules.

“You have to be regular in Parliament. You cannot make the parliamentary rules yourself, pass them and then refuse to follow them,” he said. “Do not create a spectacle through undignified activities. Both lawmakers and ministers must maintain parliamentary decorum in their conduct and activities.”

Lamichhane also warned against treating politics as a five-year project.

He said building a political party and establishing its political identity takes time, and that the existing structure should be strengthened rather than used for personal interests.

“If you think you found a position on the street without any investment, there is nothing I can say,” he said. “If you have come into politics only for five years, I will bid you farewell with garlands.”

Lawmakers, ministers told to update activities on RSP app

Lamichhane also instructed RSP lawmakers and ministers to make their activities more transparent.

He asked them to keep the party informed about their parliamentary interventions, travels, meetings and other activities and regularly update them on the ‘RSP Pulse’ app.

He also urged party members to abandon ego and improve internal communication.

“We must set aside our egos and work through coordination and dialogue,” he said. “The government can be effective only when lawmakers and ministers cooperate and coordinate. Communicate clearly with one another.”

Lamichhane also expressed dissatisfaction with what he described as a tendency to focus on publicity rather than actual work.

“Pay attention to how you present yourself in Parliament and how you behave according to your role. The people are looking for results. Focus on results rather than publicity,” he said.

He urged lawmakers to study parliamentary procedures and understand what they can and cannot do in their roles.

“Pay attention to learning and study,” he said, urging lawmakers to analyse how they should conduct themselves in Parliament and interact with the government and the public.

Lamichhane said the next meeting would be held with parliamentary party leader and Prime Minister Balendra Shah present.

RSP forms task force to amend parliamentary party statute

The meeting also formed a task force to make timely amendments to the RSP Federal Parliamentary Party statute.

The task force is headed by Kabindra Burlakoti, with Prakash Chandra Pariyar, Krantishikha Dhital and Ganesh Karki as members.

Speaking to journalists after the meeting, Lamichhane said the discussion was necessary because the RSP has a large number of lawmakers and individual remarks can sometimes lead to controversy.

“There are many of us. When many people speak, something said by one or two colleagues can become controversial. We will manage that,” he said.

He said the meeting was also held after questions were raised by members of the public and within the party about issues concerning the party’s parliamentary representation and ministers.

title.rendered: 45 pythons rescued in Chitwan last year

content.rendered:
Chitwan, August 19

The Division Forest Office here rescued as many as 69 wildlife animals, birds and reptiles in the last fiscal year. Among the animals, birds and reptiles rescued in a year, pythons counted the most, 45. The wildlife were rescued from various places and released near their habitats. Office chief Bishnu Prasad Acharya informed that 45 pythons which entered nearby human settlements and panicked people were taken under control and managed to safety by releasing to the forest.

Other animals found stranded and managed by the Office were crocodile, monkey, leopard, tortoise, stag, spotted deer and barking deer. Even birds like peacock and owl were rescued by the authority. The Office also found 42 wild animals dead last year. Among these, the highest number were spotted deer, 32, followed by barking deer, nine.

title.rendered: Cabinet takes 11 key decisions: Pay hike, Japan grant and new appointments

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 19

 The government has made public the key decisions of the Cabinet meeting held on Wednesday afternoon.

Government spokesperson and Education Minister Sasmita Pokhrel announced the decisions.

Among the key decisions, the government has increased the monthly remuneration grant for early childhood development facilitators, school employees and school support staff by Rs 5,000.

The Cabinet has also decided to bring the salaries of teachers working under teaching assistance grants at the lower secondary and secondary levels in line with those of third-grade government teachers at the respective levels.

The major Cabinet decisions are:

  1. Approved the Software Development and Operation Committee Formation Order, 2026.
  2. Accepted a grant of around Rs 2.73 billion from the Government of Japan for an air traffic control improvement project at Tribhuvan International Airport.
  3. Approved a delegation led by a joint secretary of the Ministry of Home Affairs to participate in the 14th meeting of the Joint Working Group on Border Management, scheduled to be held in India on August 20 and 21.
  4. Approved the establishment of a sub-centre of the Asian Disaster Preparedness Center in Nepal.
  5. Approved a Nepali delegation led by the foreign minister to participate in the 81st United Nations General Assembly in New York.
  6. Increased the federal government’s monthly remuneration grant for early childhood development facilitators, school employees and school support staff by Rs 5,000.
  7. Decided to bring the salaries of teachers working under teaching assistance grants at Grades 9–10 and Grades 6–8 in line with those of third-grade secondary and lower-secondary teachers, respectively.
  8. Approved negotiations for a bilateral air services agreement between Nepal and Saudi Arabia.
  9. Approved the submission to the Federal Parliament of a bill to amend the Payment and Settlement Act.
  10. Approved the submission to the Federal Parliament of a bill to amend the Citizen Investment Trust Act.
  11. Promoted Joint Secretary Kamal Prasad Bhattarai to the gazetted special class (secretary) and appointed him as chief secretary of the Bagmati Province Office of the Chief Minister and Council of Ministers.

title.rendered: Public institution employees to receive increased salaries and allowances

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 19

Employees working at public enterprises, authorities, boards, corporations and committees will also receive the recently increased salaries and allowances.

The Ministry of Finance has informed all such institutions about the decision through an official letter.

The government has increased employees’ basic salaries, grade amounts and incentive allowances effective from July 17 (Shrawan 1).

According to the ministry, a ministerial-level decision on August 18 has made arrangements for employees of all public enterprises, boards, corporations and committees to receive the revised salary, grade and incentive allowances.

The ministry has, however, instructed the institutions not to increase any additional allowances or facilities that would create an extra financial burden without prior approval from the Ministry of Finance.

It has also set conditions for employees already receiving performance-based or incentive allowances.

If the existing incentive allowance is higher than the amount prescribed by the government, institutions will be required to limit the allowance to the amount exceeding or falling within the government-prescribed level, according to the ministry.

The ministry has further directed institutions to gradually move towards a system where incentive allowances are provided based on performance indicators.

title.rendered: Govt decides to increase pay of early childhood facilitators, school staff

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 19

title.rendered: Ex-Gurkha soldiers urge Indian Army chief to help resume Agnipath recruitment from Nepal

content.rendered:
Pokhara, August 19

Nepali ex-servicemen who served in the Indian Army have urged Indian Army Chief General Dhiraj Seth to initiate efforts to resume recruitment of Nepali youths under India’s Agnipath scheme.

The request was made during General Seth’s interaction with former Indian soldiers and their families at the Indian Pension Camp in Rambazar, Pokhara, on Wednesday.

Captain Gaj Bahadur Thapa, co-chair of the Indian Ex-Servicemen Welfare Association Nepal and its Gandaki president, urged General Seth to raise the issue with the Nepal government.

“We have been raising our voice for recruitment. The friendship between Nepal and India will continue. You also need to raise this issue,” Thapa told Seth.

Thapa also raised concerns over pension problems faced by families of former Indian soldiers due to discrepancies in official documents. He said around 8,000 to 10,000 wives of former soldiers in Nepal were still unable to receive pensions because of documentation issues.

He urged the Indian Army chief to simplify the verification process, including by using photographs and biometric identification.

Agnipath recruitment halted since 2022

Recruitment of Nepali youths into the Indian Army under the traditional Gorkha recruitment system has remained suspended since India introduced the Agnipath scheme in 2022.

Under the scheme, recruits, known as Agniveers, serve for four years, after which only 25 percent are eligible for permanent retention. The remaining 75 percent leave without a pension, receiving a one-time financial package.

The Nepal government has not allowed recruitment under the scheme, maintaining its reservations over the terms of Agnipath.

Former soldiers, however, have been campaigning for recruitment to resume, arguing that it would provide employment and military experience to Nepali youths while also contributing to remittance earnings.

“Many unemployed youths would be able to serve even for a short period, earn money and gain experience that could be useful in other countries as well,” Thapa said. “But with recruitment halted, many young people are going to the Gulf countries for work.”

Indian former soldiers recently held demonstrations in Pokhara demanding the resumption of recruitment under the Agnipath scheme.

Indian Army pledges continued support

Addressing the former soldiers and their families, General Seth said the Indian Army would continue to do everything possible for their welfare, healthcare and other facilities.

He described former soldiers as “living representatives” of India-Nepal relations and praised the contribution of Gorkha soldiers to the Indian Army.

“The relationship between the Indian Army and Gorkha soldiers is a proud history,” Seth said, praising their courage and dedication in wars and military operations.

Seth said efforts would be made to equip the Ex-Servicemen Contributory Health Scheme (ECHS) polyclinic in Pokhara with additional modern medical equipment.

He also said the demand for a bus service between Sunauli and Gorakhpur was being considered. Such a service would make it easier for former soldiers to access ECHS and other healthcare facilities in India, he said.

A new ECHS polyclinic has also been opened in Kohalpur to serve former Indian soldiers and their families in western Nepal.

More than 60,000 former Indian soldiers and their family members receive pensions through the Pokhara pension camp, while the number across Nepal is estimated at around 120,000.

Former soldiers honoured

During the programme, former Gorkha soldiers, war widows and injured veterans were presented with medals, certificates of honour and mobility scooters.

Dilibahadur Thapa was awarded the Kirti Chakra, India’s second-highest peacetime gallantry award, for his bravery during Operation Rakshak in Jammu and Kashmir.

Kesh Bahadur Chhetri received the Shaurya Chakra, India’s third-highest peacetime gallantry award, for his contribution during the same operation.

Seven soldiers were awarded the Sena Medal for courage and dedication during various military operations.

Thakur Prasad Poudel was awarded the Vishisht Seva Medal for distinguished service in the Indian Army.

Nine retired senior soldiers were also presented with the Yoddha Seva Samman, while 10 wives and mothers of soldiers who died during various wars and military operations were honoured as Veer Naris.

title.rendered: CIB freezes bank accounts of share trader Dipendra Agrawal, family members

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 19

The Central Investigation Bureau (CIB) has frozen the bank accounts of share trader Dipendra Agrawal, his family members and some of his business associates as part of an ongoing investigation into alleged manipulation of share prices and fraudulent trading.

The CIB has been investigating Agrawal over allegations of artificially increasing share prices and conducting false transactions to influence the market.

CIB spokesperson Anupam Shamsher Rana said the accounts of Agrawal, family members involved in his transactions and other individuals linked to him had been frozen as part of the investigation.

“Bank accounts of family members and individuals linked to Dipendra Agrawal’s transactions have been frozen as part of the ongoing investigation,” Rana said. “The bureau is investigating allegations including fraud and fraudulent share transactions.”

The Securities Board of Nepal (SEBON) had previously investigated Agrawal and forwarded the case to the CIB for further investigation.

Agrawal was arrested by the CIB in December and spent 10 days in custody before being released on a personal guarantee.

According to the investigation, Agrawal allegedly purchased shares at relatively low prices and subsequently used misleading publicity to push up their prices before selling them.

The CIB has also found that Agrawal allegedly conducted transactions between himself, family members and related entities without changing the actual ownership of the securities.

He is also accused of operating trading accounts belonging to other individuals and transferring funds between different accounts.

Agrawal had reached the CIB after learning that his bank accounts had been frozen. He was later released after the bureau asked him to cooperate with the investigation.

According to a CIB source, the bureau has also begun looking into possible money laundering after its investigation identified Agrawal’s net worth at around Rs 55 billion.

Dispute over Bhote Koshi heli resort

Agrawal has also recently become embroiled in a dispute over the Bhote Koshi Heli Resort in Sindhupalchok.

The resort is currently closed and the bank is preparing for its third auction. Employees of the resort have also filed complaints with the Department of Labour, alleging that they have not received their salaries.

Agrawal is said to have control over the resort, although a dispute has emerged over its management and company records.

A resort investor alleged that Agrawal had created and updated a purportedly fake board of directors at the Office of the Company Registrar after the bank began the process of auctioning the resort.

The investor alleged that Agrawal took the step to avoid being blacklisted as the bank moved to auction the property.

title.rendered: Fact check: Viral video shows Gurkha veterans in India, not Nepal

content.rendered:
A video showing former Gurkha Rifles soldiers and their families singing India’s national anthem and saluting the Indian flag has been falsely claimed to be from Pokhara, Nepal. Nepal Check found that the video was filmed in Sukhiapokhri, a town in India’s Darjeeling district.

On August 17, 2026, the X account @gorockgo_100, which regularly posts content about the Indian Army, shared the nearly two-minute video. Its caption claimed: “This is at Pokhara Nepal by veterans of Gurkha Rifles. Veterans with families are singing the national anthem of India, despite being citizens of a sovereign country.”

A screenshot of the viral video on Instagram

The post praised the participants’ “respect” for the Indian flag and ended with “Jai Hind.” The video was subsequently shared on Instagram and LinkedIn with the same claim.

Indian news outlets also amplified the claim. Navbharat Times claimed the video showed Gurkha veterans singing India’s national anthem and unfurling the Indian flag.

Fact check

Nepal Check extracted screenshots from the viral video and conducted reverse-image and keyword searches. We could not locate its original video. However, we found another recording of the same event on a Facebook page by Rinzing Namgyal Bhutia.

Bhutia’s video was filmed from a different angle and showed the gathering in greater detail. A frame-by-frame comparison revealed several people appearing in both videos. Their clothing, positions within the gathering and physical features matched. The positions of the participants and other surroundings were also consistent across the two videos.

Screenshot comparison between video on Bhutia’s Facebook account and the viral clip (right). Woman wearing blue shawl.

According to the video posted on Bhutia’s Facebook, the event took place in Sukhiapokhri (also written as Sukhia Pokhari) in Darjeeling district of West Bengal, India. The town lies along the border with Nepal.

The participants were therefore not Nepali citizens singing the anthem of another country, as the viral caption claimed. They were Gurkha Rifles veterans and family members attending an event in India.

Context

The video circulated as Indian Army chief General Dhiraj Seth visited Nepal from August 17 to 19. On August 17, President Ramchandra Paudel conferred on Seth the honorary rank of General of the Nepal Army in Kathmandu.

Nepal and India have a longstanding tradition of granting honorary general ranks to each other’s army chiefs. This also comes amid uncertainty over the recruitment of Nepali citizens into the Indian Army. Under the 1947 tripartite agreement involving Nepal, India and Britain, Nepali Gurkhas have historically served in the Indian and British armies.

Recruitment into the Indian Army has remained stalled since India introduced the Agnipath scheme in 2022. Under the scheme, most recruits serve for four years, while only 25 per cent are retained for longer service. Nepal has not approved the recruitment of its citizens under these changed conditions, citing concerns about their employment and benefits after discharge.

That dispute, however, is unrelated to the provenance of this video.

Conclusion

Our comparison of the viral footage with another video of the same gathering shows that the event occurred in Sukhiapokhri, Darjeeling, India not in Pokhara, Nepal. The claim that Nepali citizens were shown singing India’s national anthem is false.

title.rendered: Rabi Lamichhane says there is no problem in his relationship with PM Balen Shah

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 19

Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) Chair Rabi Lamichhane has said there is no problem in his relationship with Prime Minister Balendra Shah.

Speaking to journalists on Wednesday, Lamichhane said reports about tensions between the two had, in fact, brought them closer.

“There is no problem between us, and there is no confusion,” he said.

Lamichhane was responding to a question about a recent social media post by Prime Minister Shah in which Shah said he felt “alone.”

Defending the prime minister’s remarks, Lamichhane said Shah was also a poet and an artist, and that his words should not necessarily be interpreted politically.

“The prime minister wrote that. He is also a poet and an artist. Can’t I feel alone even in a crowd this large? If we start looking for political meanings in every word, it doesn’t necessarily have a political meaning,” Lamichhane said.

He said there was no reason for concern over the relationship between the two leaders.

title.rendered: NCP and UML reach agreement on ministry sharing in Karnali

content.rendered:
Surkhet, August 19

The ruling coalition partners in Karnali, the Nepal Communist Party (NCP) and CPN-UML, have reached an agreement on sharing the provincial government’s portfolios. The six-point agreement between the two parties’ provincial parliamentary parties for the power-sharing arrangement was reached on Wednesday.

Under the agreement, apart from the Chief Minister and Council of Ministers office, the NCP will get three ministries, and UML will also get three ministries.

The NCP will hold the Office of the Chief Minister and Council of Ministers, the Ministry of Physical Infrastructure Development, the Ministry of Land Management, Agriculture and Cooperatives, and the Ministry of Industry, Tourism, Forest and Environment.

Meanwhile, UML has agreed to take the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Planning, the Ministry of Social Development, and the Ministry of Water Resources and Energy Development.

The two parties have agreed that any new policies, programs, nominations, and appointments will only move forward once mutual agreement is reached between them. The agreement document also states that the provincial government will be run in a manner that ensures good governance, frugality, and transparency.

They have also agreed to continue implementing earlier decisions made for administrative structural reforms and to carry forward the remaining work in that area.

title.rendered: Inspector Suraj Khatri named outstanding police officer

content.rendered:
Kathmandu

Police Inspector Suraj Khatri has been named the Outstanding Police Officer for the month of Shrawan.

Khatri, who is serving at the Kathmandu Valley Crime Investigation Office, received the award for his significant contribution to crime investigation. SSP Santosh Khadka, chief of the Crime Investigation Office, presented the award to him.

Khatri, who works under Pillar No. 4 of the office, has investigated serious crimes including gang-related activities, kidnapping and murder. He is regarded as an accomplished crime investigator.

His team recently successfully investigated a case in which a young man was abducted from Kalanki, taken to Nagarjun and held hostage.

The victim was allegedly beaten with a plastic pipe and tortured while being held captive, with the abductors demanding a ransom of Rs 1.8 million. The victim was rescued, and seven people allegedly involved in the kidnapping were arrested.

For the first time in the history of the Crime Investigation Office, the office itself has filed a case in connection with the kidnapping. Previously, the office had authority to investigate cases but did not have the authority to prosecute them.

title.rendered: NEPSE virtually unchanged as turnover drops to Rs 3.29 billion

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 19

Nepal’s share market remained virtually unchanged on Wednesday, with the Nepal Stock Exchange (NEPSE) index declining by just 0.26 points to close at 2,622 points.

The index had dropped 19.34 points on Tuesday.

Trading turnover also declined significantly. Shares worth Rs 3.29 billion were traded on Wednesday, down from Rs 5.07 billion the Tuesday.

A total of 110 companies recorded gains, while 150 declined and 18 remained unchanged.

All sectoral indices fluctuated by less than 1%.

The banking sector rose 0.06%, hydropower 0.09%, non-life insurance 0.14%, others 0.12% and trading 0.76%.

Development banks declined 0.02%, finance 0.22%, hotels and tourism 0.38%, investment 0.28%, life insurance 0.31%, manufacturing and processing 0.04% and microfinance 0.33%.

As usual, hydropower companies recorded the highest turnover among sectoral groups, with transactions worth Rs 1.84 billion.

Commercial banks recorded turnover of Rs 370 million, while manufacturing and processing companies saw transactions worth Rs 350 million.

Recently listed companies Sarbottam Paints and Mount Everest Power gained 15% each.

Bhagwati Hydropower rose 3%, while Gurans Laghubitta gained 2.41%.

Manakamana Engineering Hydropower fell 8.45%, Rizline Energy declined 3.38% and Green Development Bank dropped 3.07%.

In terms of turnover, Sahas Urja, Solu Hydropower, Reliance Spinning Mills, Manakamana Engineering Hydropower and Khanikhola Hydropower were the most actively traded companies.

Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) has formed a taskforce to amend the statute governing its parliamentary party.

According to RSP parliamentary party Deputy Leader Ganesh Parajuli, the taskforce has been formed under the leadership of the party’s chief whip.

“The statute amendment taskforce has been formed under the leadership of the chief whip to amend the parliamentary party statute as necessary,” Parajuli said.

The taskforce has been given seven days to propose necessary amendments to the RSP parliamentary party statute and prepare related procedures.

The proposed amendments will focus on parliamentary conduct and the responsibilities of lawmakers, including maintaining the dignity of the House, fulfilling responsibilities towards the public, strengthening the voice of the opposition and making the lawmaking process more effective.

The decision comes after RSP Chair Rabi Lamichhane held discussions with the party’s lawmakers and ministers on parliamentary conduct and style on Wednesday.

Parajuli provided details about the taskforce following the meeting.

The RSP has recently been focusing on making its lawmakers more accountable for their attendance and conduct in Parliament, including through a system requiring lawmakers who are absent or arrive late to explain their reasons.

title.rendered: Man who helped search for missing child arrested for her murder

content.rendered:
Simara, August 19

Police have arrested two individuals, including a man who pretended to assist officers during the initial search, in connection with the rape and murder of a three-year-old girl in Jitpur Simara Sub-Metropolitan City-1, Bara.

The victim a resident of the Dashdhure squatter settlement and a playgroup student at local Saraswati Basic School, went missing on Sunday morning.

Her body was recovered on Tuesday evening, wrapped in clothes inside an abandoned house roughly 200 meters from her home, after local residents alerted authorities to a foul smell emanating from the building.

Police arrested Suman Thapa, a resident of Jitpur Simara-2, directly from the crime scene after a police tracker dog signaled his involvement.

Thapa, who works as a helper on a public Magic van running along the Birgunj–Pathlaiya route, has confessed to raping and murdering the child.

Police Inspector Prakash Thapa of the Area Police Office, Simara, confirmed that Thapa actively walked around the scene alongside investigators, calling for the perpetrator’s immediate arrest before being identified.

Authorities also detained Progress Chaudhary, the driver of the van (Na 1 Ja 7758) where Thapa worked, for further investigation. Because the driver’s house is situated near the victim’s residence, the young girl frequently visited the area.

Investigators stated that Thapa lured the child from the driver’s house on Sunday morning. In his statement to the police, Thapa disclosed that after raping the child until she lost consciousness, he hanged her with a rope, left the area to bathe, and returned later that afternoon to bundle the body in fabric.

The tragedy has left the victim’s family completely devastated, with her mother remaining in a state of semi-consciousness since Tuesday evening. Meanwhile, outrage has erupted across the local community.

On Wednesday afternoon, aggrieved locals demonstrated in front of the Area Police Office in Simara, demanding the maximum punishment for the offender. The protest led to a traffic blockade along the busy Birgunj–Pathlaiya highway section that lasted for over two hours.

title.rendered: TU MBS paper leak: Seven charged, three released on bail

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 19

Seven people have been charged in connection with the leak of a question paper for the first semester of Tribhuvan University’s Master of Business Studies (MBS) programme.

The charges were filed based on investigation reports prepared by the Cyber Bureau of Nepal Police and the Central Investigation Bureau (CIB).

Those charged are Sandip Singh, 33, who teaches finance at KMC College in Bagbazar and Himalaya College in Koteshwor; Atul Kumar Mishra, 25, of Rajdevi Municipality-4, Rautahat; Abdul Sani Hakimi, 31, of Bara; Rishikesh Prasad Yadav, 30, of Bara; Khushbu Giri, 25, of Parsa; Devnath Mahato, 25, of Parsa; and Ranju Kumari Giri, 27, of Parsa.

Of the seven accused, Singh, Mishra and Hakimi, who were arrested during the investigation, have been released on bail.

CIB SSP Anupam Shamsher Rana said the three were released after depositing bail as ordered by the Kathmandu District Court.

A bench of Kathmandu District Court Judge Navaraj Dulal had ordered their release on bail of Rs 2,000 each. They were released on Tuesday accordingly.

The remaining four accused have not yet been arrested and have been charged as absconding defendants.

Police said their investigation has so far found no evidence of involvement by anyone else in the question paper leak.

The question paper for the MBS first-semester Business Research Methods (BRM) examination was leaked on July 24. The paper was reportedly circulated through a WhatsApp group before the examination began.

The CIB had treated the incident as a serious matter and conducted an investigation into the leak. However, the three arrested suspects have been released on bail of just Rs 2,000 each.

“I planted timur because its thorny branches can also serve as a natural fence. It is also a cash crop,” Hari Bansha said.

He had previously pledged to plant a total of 200 saplings at the site.

The producers of Mahajatra had earlier said that the film was shot as part of a carbon-neutral initiative. Since some carbon emissions were generated during filming, Hari Bansha committed to planting trees as part of the initiative.

title.rendered: Govt steps up preparations to cut electricity tariffs

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 19

The government has intensified preparations to reduce electricity tariffs for consumers and industries.

A committee was formed on July 29 on the proposal of Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha to review existing electricity tariffs.

The committee, coordinated by Nepal Electricity Authority board member Anshu Kiran Shahi, is scheduled to meet at the ministry at 4 pm on Wednesday to discuss ways to reduce electricity prices.

Representatives from the Ministry of Energy, Federation of Nepalese Chambers of Commerce and Industry, energy experts, consumer representatives and financial experts are members of the committee.

Shahi said the tariff is being reviewed in view of the surplus electricity generated during the monsoon season, much of which is currently going to waste.

He said the authority is considering introducing a seasonal tariff to provide electricity to consumers and industries at cheaper rates during the rainy season and increase domestic consumption.

According to Shahi, the authority has been incurring monthly losses when electricity generated during the monsoon cannot be consumed or exported.

“We are meeting at the ministry today to discuss how much the tariff can be reduced under the seasonal tariff,” Shahi said. “We are also discussing how industries can pass on the benefit of cheaper monsoon electricity to consumers through lower prices of their products.”

He said industries are also being considered for discounted electricity rates during the rainy season.

The committee is expected to make a decision on the proposed tariff revision soon.

Kathmandu, August 19

Reconstruction of the historic Bhadrakali Temple complex in Kathmandu is progressing rapidly, with the project being carried out in the traditional Newa architectural style.

The temple complex was damaged by the 2015 earthquake, and reconstruction began in 2024. According to Kathmandu Metropolitan City, work is underway on the main temple as well as surrounding patis, sattals and other structures.

The reconstruction has been entrusted to Tulsi-Ambuja JV for Rs 348.071 million, with the project targeted for completion within three years. The Department of Archaeology is documenting the complex’s old structures, craftsmanship and architectural features during the reconstruction.

According to civil engineer Rabindra Rijal of the metropolitan city’s Heritage and Tourism Department, the reconstructed structures will feature intricately carved doors, windows and pillars, while traditional jhingati tiles will be used for the roofs. The total area of the buildings will be around 39,000 square feet.

Acting Mayor Sunita Dangol said the project was not merely an infrastructure development initiative but an important effort to preserve Kathmandu’s cultural, historical and religious heritage.

A Temple Reconstruction Facilitation Committee has also been formed to coordinate and facilitate the project. The completed complex is expected to strengthen the preservation of Kathmandu’s traditional Newa architecture and heritage.

title.rendered: Manang bridge remains incomplete 10 years after contract signed

content.rendered:
Manang, August 19

A motorable bridge over the Marsyangdi River linking Manang Ngisyang Rural Municipality-3 and Ngawal-4 in Manang remains incomplete even 10 years after a construction contract was signed, forcing locals to travel at risk.

The Infrastructure Development Office, Manang, said the contractor has already received around 70 per cent of the contract payment, but construction has progressed very slowly. Office Chief Hari Thapa said the contractor had failed to accelerate the work despite receiving the required payments and repeated extensions to the project deadline.

The contract was signed to complete the bridge by the end of Asar 2073 BS at an estimated cost of around Rs 40 million. Locals say the delay has made travel to the rural municipality office difficult. “The office can be reached within four to five minutes once the bridge is built. At present, it takes much longer because there is no bridge,” said resident Mukhiya Lama.

Chairperson of Manang Ngisyang Rural Municipality-3 Krishna Bahadur Lama said both the contractor and concerned authorities had shown little interest in completing the project. Locals have demanded that the contract be terminated if the contractor fails to resume work and that a new company be hired.

During a recent monitoring visit, Manang lawmaker and former minister Tek Bahadur Gurung instructed the contractor to resume construction immediately and urged the concerned office to release payments only after assessing the actual progress. Former lawmaker Palden Chhompang Gurung said the delay had caused difficulties for both locals and tourists visiting Manang.

title.rendered: Indian Army chief pledges continued support for ex-servicemen in Nepal

content.rendered:
Pokhara, August 19

Indian Army Chief General Dhiraj Seth has pledged that the Indian Army will continue to provide support for the welfare, healthcare and other facilities of former Indian soldiers living in Nepal.

Addressing former Indian soldiers and their families at a pension camp in Pokhara on Wednesday, Seth described ex-servicemen as “living representatives” of India-Nepal relations.

Paying tribute to the contributions of Gorkha soldiers who served in the Indian Army, Seth said their welfare remained the responsibility of the Indian Army.

“We will do everything possible with full sincerity and dedication for your welfare and facilities,” he said. “You should never feel that you are alone. The Indian Army will always stand with you.”

More health facilities planned

Seth said efforts would be made to provide additional medical equipment to the Ex-Servicemen Contributory Health Scheme (ECHS) polyclinic in Pokhara.

He said the Indian Army would also work to further equip the polyclinic with modern medical facilities.

Seth said the demand from former soldiers for a bus service from Sunauli to Gorakhpur was also being considered seriously.

He said efforts were underway to provide the service, which would make it easier for former soldiers to access ECHS and other healthcare facilities.

The ECHS scheme has been operating in Nepal since 2014, providing healthcare services to former Indian soldiers and their families at hospitals in Nepal and India.

Seth said efforts were also underway to expand the number of hospitals enlisted under the scheme.

He also highlighted the recently established ECHS polyclinic in Kohalpur, which is intended to serve former soldiers and their families in western Nepal.

“I dedicate this new polyclinic, on behalf of the Indian Army, to all former soldiers and their families in Nepal,” he said.

Seth said various district soldier boards were providing vocational training to families of former soldiers in areas including computer skills, beauty care and fashion designing.

Following an agreement with Meghavi Skills University in Sikkim, certificates issued after completing the training will be recognised nationally and internationally, he said.

‘India-Nepal ties go beyond being neighbours’

Seth said India-Nepal relations were centuries old and went beyond the relationship between two neighbouring countries.

The relationship, he said, was rooted in shared culture, traditions, religious beliefs and history.

He described the special relationship between the Indian and Nepali armies as an important part of those historic ties.

Praising the bravery, courage, loyalty and sacrifice of Gorkha soldiers, Seth said they had displayed exceptional courage in every war and challenge faced by the Indian Army.

Five priorities for Indian Army

Seth also outlined the five priorities he has set for the Indian Army since taking charge as army chief.

They are vigilance and preparedness, innovation and transformation, jointness, self-reliance and warriors.

Seth said he considered everyone serving in the Indian Army—from its youngest soldier to its most senior former serviceman—as a “warrior”.

“From the junior-most soldier to the most senior former soldier sitting before me, everyone is a warrior in my vocabulary,” he said. “The Indian Army is proud of all these warriors.”

He reiterated the Indian Army’s commitment to continuing its support for the welfare and facilities of former Indian soldiers in Nepal.

Seth concluded his address by thanking the former soldiers and their families, ending with the slogan, “Jai Hind, Jai Nepal, Jai Bhupu.”

title.rendered: RSP meeting delays House of Representatives session

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 19

The meeting of the House of Representatives has been delayed as a meeting of the Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) parliamentary party continued beyond its scheduled time on Wednesday.

RSP Chair Rabi Lamichhane is holding discussions with the party’s lawmakers and ministers on parliamentary decorum and conduct at the party’s parliamentary office in Singha Durbar.

Prime Minister Balendra Shah, who is also the RSP parliamentary party leader, did not attend the meeting.

The House of Representatives session was scheduled to begin at 1 pm but had not started as the RSP meeting was still underway.

Wednesday’s House agenda includes a proposal by Finance Minister Dr Swarnim Wagle to consider the Employees Provident Fund (10th Amendment) Bill, 2026.

Similarly, Youth, Labour and Employment Minister Ramji Yadav is scheduled to present a proposal seeking consideration of the Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Bill, 2026.

RSP had ordered lawmakers to arrive on time

The delay is notable because the RSP parliamentary party had itself instructed its lawmakers several days ago to attend parliamentary meetings on time.

The party has introduced a Google Form through which lawmakers who fail to attend a House meeting on time must provide the reason for their absence and upload supporting evidence.

The form must also be filled out by lawmakers who arrive more than 30 minutes late to a scheduled parliamentary meeting.

RSP leaders say the system is intended to make lawmakers more accountable for their attendance and conduct in Parliament.

The party plans to maintain records not only of lawmakers who remain absent but also of those who attend a session and leave before it concludes.

The initiative is aimed at treating parliamentary attendance as a matter of responsibility and accountability rather than merely a matter of marking attendance.

Move comes after House meeting was adjourned for lack of quorum

The RSP’s new monitoring system was introduced against the backdrop of a recent House meeting being adjourned after failing to meet the required quorum.

The House meeting on August 11 was suspended after the required quorum was not met, delaying the process of advancing government legislation.

The RSP has 182 lawmakers in the House, making it the largest party in the governing side. The ruling side carries the primary responsibility for ensuring the smooth functioning of parliamentary business.

However, during the August 11 meeting, even the required quorum of 69 lawmakers was not reached when a proposal to consider a mining-related bill was put to a vote.

Against this backdrop, the RSP parliamentary party decided to introduce a Google Form to track lawmakers’ attendance and activities more closely.

Ironically, the party’s own meeting on Wednesday has now delayed the start of the House session.

Under the party’s own directive, RSP lawmakers who arrive late to Wednesday’s House meeting will have to fill out the form and explain the reason for their delay.

title.rendered: Tokha-Chhahare road section to remain closed at night amid landslide risk

content.rendered:
Nuwakot, August 19

The Nuwakot District Administration Office has decided to close the Tokha-Chhahare road section at night following an increase in landslides and mudslides triggered by rainfall.

According to Nuwakot Chief District Officer Shambhu Prasad Regmi, the road will remain closed to traffic from 10 pm to 5 am every day due to the heightened risk of landslides, mudslides and falling rocks.

The road is a major route connecting Dhading and the Rasuwagadhi border point with China through Nuwakot.

The administration said traffic would be restricted during the night to ensure the safety of passengers and motorists. Only essential and emergency vehicles will be allowed to operate during the closure.

The Ghattekhola section of the Tokha-Chhahare road in Shivapuri Rural Municipality-8 has been identified as particularly vulnerable to landslides, mudslides and rockfalls.

The restriction came into effect on the night of August 17 and will remain in place until further notice.

Regmi said security personnel would be deployed at high-risk locations to monitor the situation and facilitate emergency movement.

Ambulances and other essential emergency vehicles will be allowed to operate during the restricted hours.

For disaster-related information and assistance, the public can contact the District Police Office at 100, the Armed Police Force at 1114, and the District Emergency Operations Centre at 1234.

title.rendered: National Information Day being observed today

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 19

National Information Day is being observed today by organising various programmes. The Day is marked to commemorate the introduction of the RTI Act, 2064. Various organisations are holding programmes to observe the Day that celebrates the value of information. The RTI Act was passed by the parliament on Saun 5, 2064BS and came into force on Bhadra 3, 2064BS. Article 27 of the Constitution has provided the right to information to every citizen to seek and receive information of his or public concern.

Public agencies are obliged to share information in line with the RTI Act and the constitutional provision. Even the practice of proactive disclosure by public agencies is advocated by the RTI Act. RTI is regarded as an anti-corruption tool, so an imperative for good governance. Good governance advocates and researchers argue that the use of RTI not only helps curb financial irregularities at public agencies but also builds transparency and accountability. The National Information Commission is the agency the government set up to advance the use of RTI across the country through youth training.

The Commission stated in a message that RTI is instrumental in empowering citizens and building pillars of sustainable development and a pro-people system. Since the introduction of the RTI Act, numerous civil society organisations in the federal capital, Kathmandu, and outside have trained cohorts of youths, launched RTI campaigns, filed RTI requests and even exposed irregularities. Lately, RTI is linked to sustainable development goals (SDGs).

Speaking to journalists after landing at Kathmandu airport on Tuesday evening, he said he was very excited to perform.

“This is my first time visiting Nepal. I like Nepal. I like Nepali customs and culture,” he said. “I’m very excited to perform for the Nepali audience.”

Expressing his fondness for Nepali music, he said he also listens to Nepali songs. He also said he would be willing to sing if any Nepali musician offered him a song. He will stay in Nepal for three days, during which he will visit religious and tourist sites in Kathmandu.

title.rendered: France to expel two Iranian diplomats

content.rendered:
Kathmandu

France has decided to expel two Iranian diplomats from the country. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot announced on social media platform X on Tuesday that the two Iranian diplomats currently in France will be expelled in the coming days.

The decision comes in response to an incident in July in which Iranian security officials detained, questioned and threatened two employees of the French Embassy in Tehran. France described the incident as a violation of diplomatic immunity and an “extremely serious and premeditated” act.

Earlier, Iran had also decided not to allow the two French Embassy employees to return to Iran. Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei accused them of engaging in activities supporting Iranian civil society in violation of the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations.

The French Foreign Ministry rejected the allegations, calling the charges against its employees “completely false.” According to France, the employees were involved in programs supporting Iranian civil society, including students, artists and scientists.

On July 20, Foreign Minister Barrot said Iranian security forces had held the two French employees for several hours and questioned them, with one of them allegedly subjected to physical abuse. At the time, he warned that Iran would face consequences for the incident.

The expulsion decision comes amid growing tensions between France and Iran and is expected to further strain relations between the two countries.

title.rendered: Why is the Bar Association unhappy with the Chief Justice?

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 19

The Nepal Bar Association has sent a written notice of attention to Chief Justice Dr Manoj Sharma, raising concerns over the way judges are being selected for the Supreme Court’s Constitutional Bench and how cases are being transferred to it.

The umbrella organisation of Nepal’s legal practitioners has urged the Chief Justice to ensure consistency and transparency in the formation of the Constitutional Bench.

The Bar has proposed two options for selecting the four judges who sit on the bench alongside the Chief Justice.

It has suggested that the judges should either be selected according to seniority or, if that is not possible, through a lottery system from the roster of judges designated for the Constitutional Bench.

The Bar’s intervention follows a Supreme Court administrative decision to send around six writ petitions related to the Property Investigation Commission to the Constitutional Bench.

The association objected after the decision to place the petitions before the Constitutional Bench was made public.

Bar Association President Bijay Mishra had warned on Sunday that lawyers could be forced to refrain from pleading in the cases if the Supreme Court administration did not reconsider its decision. No hearing date has yet been fixed for the petitions.

What is the Bar’s concern?

Article 137 of the Constitution provides for a Constitutional Bench headed by the Chief Justice. Four other judges are selected by the Chief Justice on the recommendation of the Judicial Council.

According to the Bar, judges for the Constitutional Bench have generally been selected according to seniority since the Constitution was promulgated in 2015.

Although this practice was disrupted for some time during the tenure of former Chief Justice Cholendra Shumsher Rana, it was later restored. Former Chief Justice Prakash Man Singh Raut also deviated from the seniority-based practice for a period last year.

The Bar argues that selecting judges according to the nature of individual cases can raise questions about the credibility of the bench and its decisions.

In its letter, the association expressed particular concern over reports that cases pending before other benches were being transferred to the Constitutional Bench through administrative decisions without the consent of the parties or discussion with the concerned bench.

It described the practice as contrary to established norms and judicial traditions.

What does the Bar want?

The Bar has urged the Supreme Court to immediately convene a full court meeting and discuss the issue seriously. It wants the court to establish a clear policy of selecting Constitutional Bench judges based on seniority.

If seniority-based selection is not possible, the Bar wants judges to be selected through a lottery system.

The association argues that a consistent selection process is necessary to maintain the credibility of the Constitutional Bench and public confidence in the judiciary.

Bar also seeks revival of coordination committee

The Nepal Bar Association has also called for the Supreme Court’s Bar-Bench Coordination Committee to be reactivated.

The committee includes the Chief Justice, judges designated by the Chief Justice and representatives of the Nepal Bar Association. It is intended to facilitate coordination between lawyers and the judiciary and help address problems within the justice system.

The Bar said the committee has not met for a long time and has effectively become inactive.

It has therefore urged the Chief Justice to reactivate the committee and resume regular coordination between the judiciary and the legal profession.

title.rendered: 17 new films get production permits, meet the filmmakers

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 19

Seventeen films received production permits from the Film Development Board in Shrawan. Both new and veteran filmmakers have obtained these permits.

Saurabh Chaudhary has received a permit for the feature film “Samrajya.” Saugat Malla, Dayahang Rai, and Nazir Hussain are already signed on for lead roles in this film.

Director Deepak Lama has taken a production permit for a film titled “Feri Bhetaula.” Shraddha Prasai is set to direct “Dear Kabya,” featuring Upasana Singh Thakuri.

Director Rishi Lamichhane will be making the film “Ujeli,” starring Sabin Shrestha and singer Yash Kumar, among others.

Akash Adhikari will produce and direct “Kohinoor 2,” the sequel to the hit film “Kohinoor.” Uttam KC will produce the film “Champa.”

title.rendered: Nepali Congress dissident faction to move Supreme Court seeking halt to 15th general convention process

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 19

The dissident faction of the Nepali Congress is preparing to move the Supreme Court seeking an immediate halt to the process for the party’s 15th General Convention.

The faction decided to approach the court after the party revised and published the general convention schedule while a dispute over the party’s legitimacy remains sub judice.

Min Bishwakarma, coordinator of the faction’s publicity and promotion committee, said they were preparing to seek a court order to suspend the convention process for the time being.

“It is not appropriate for one side to unilaterally move forward on a matter that is already under consideration by the court,” Bishwakarma told Onlinekhabar. “But the process has been moved forward. Our side will file a petition in court.”

According to Bishwakarma, the faction’s Law and Statute Committee, led by party leader Ramesh Lekhak, will take the matter to the Supreme Court.

“It is the responsibility of the Law and Statute Committee. They will carry out that task,” he said.

The faction has not yet fixed a date for filing the petition.

“The new schedule was announced only yesterday,” Bishwakarma said. “The Law and Statute Committee will probably approach the court within a day or two.”

Faction had earlier urged party to halt convention preparations

Earlier, Dr Shashank Koirala, coordinator of the main organising committee of the faction’s national gathering, had written to the Election Commission and the Nepali Congress on August 11, urging them not to proceed with activities related to the general convention.

The letter called for an immediate suspension of all organisational, technical and policy-related schedules concerning the party’s 15th General Convention or a special general convention.

It also urged the party to keep all long-term policy, political, organisational and financial decisions on hold until the Supreme Court delivers its final verdict on the dispute.

The faction further asked the party to maintain all organisational structures in their existing form until the final decision of the Supreme Court and to fully respect the court’s authority and legal process.

Koirala’s letter warned that the concerned parties would be responsible for any contempt of court or legal complications arising from proceeding with the convention process.

Supreme Court allows review of Nepali Congress legitimacy dispute

The Supreme Court on August 6 granted permission to review the case concerning the Nepali Congress’ legitimacy dispute.

Following the review permission, the dispute surrounding the party’s special general convention will now be heard afresh from the beginning.

The dissident faction argues that the party should not proceed with its convention process while the dispute remains pending before the Supreme Court.

title.rendered: Dr Dhundiraj Paudel appointed Nepal Medical Council chairperson

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 19

Senior otolaryngologist Dr Dhundiraj Paudel has been appointed chairperson of the Nepal Medical Council.

Health and Food Safety Minister Nisha Mehta appointed Dr Paudel to the post on Wednesday.

Dr Paudel previously served as chairperson of the Bharatpur Hospital Development Committee.

During his tenure, he had proposed developing Bharatpur Hospital as a teaching hospital and an institution capable of providing medical education.

He had also advocated for developing Bharatpur Hospital into an institution modeled on the National Academy of Medical Sciences, with its own legal foundation and without having to depend on other institutions.

Dr Paudel has also been vocal on issues related to health service improvement, management of government hospitals and medical education.

He has consistently emphasized strengthening the capacity of government hospitals and making medical education and healthcare delivery more effective.

As chairperson of the Nepal Medical Council, Dr Paudel will now be responsible for key areas including regulation of the medical profession, professional conduct of doctors and matters related to medical education.

title.rendered: Nepal earns Rs 29.32 billion from electricity exports to India and Bangladesh

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 18

Nepal earned Rs 29.32 billion from electricity exports to India and Bangladesh in the fiscal year 2025/26, Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha informed Parliament.

Minister Shrestha provided the information in response to a question from Nepali Congress Chief Whip Basana Thapa regarding the country’s existing energy system and problems faced in electricity service delivery.

Shrestha said the ministry has been taking various measures to ensure a continuous and reliable electricity supply for domestic consumers.

The government has started expanding smart metering and substation automation systems in Kathmandu Valley and major cities.

Construction of new substations and the expansion and upgrading of transmission and distribution lines have also been accelerated to meet growing electricity demand in urban areas.

In industrial areas, infrastructure including dedicated feeders is being constructed and upgraded to reduce voltage fluctuations and ensure reliable power supply.

The minister said efforts would continue to strengthen the electricity distribution system and improve its reliability and quality.

Nepal Electricity Authority has also been carrying out maintenance and rehabilitation work according to a planned schedule, he said.

According to Shrestha, the authority provides advance notice of scheduled power cuts through mass media, social media and its official communication channels.

He said the authority has also started making its system for immediately informing consumers about unexpected power outages more effective.

Shrestha said the Ministry of Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation has been operating a 24-hour hotline at 1151 to address public complaints, while Nepal Electricity Authority operates a separate 1150 hotline and a ‘No Light’ service.

He informed Parliament that 31,496 complaints had been addressed through the ministry’s hotline since the formation of the new government.

The ministry coordinates with the concerned offices and officials to facilitate the resolution of complaints received through the hotline, according to Shrestha.

title.rendered: Transformer theft surges in Madhesh, disrupting irrigation and water supply

content.rendered:
Janakpurdham, August 19

Transformer thefts are increasing across Madhesh Province, disrupting irrigation, drinking water projects and electricity services while putting additional financial pressure on the Nepal Electricity Authority (NEA).

A 100 kVA transformer installed for irrigation in Aurahi Municipality-1, Mahottari, was stolen on the night of August 12. The theft has left local farmers struggling to irrigate their paddy fields amid inadequate rainfall.

Similar incidents have been reported in Dhanusha. A transformer installed for a drinking water project in Kshireshwarnath Municipality-9 was recently stolen while the project was preparing to begin operations. In Mithila Municipality-2, Naktajhij, thieves removed another drinking water transformer from its pole and stole its oil and coils. Despite being welded to prevent theft, the transformer was stolen after the welding was cut. The incident disrupted water supply for four days.

According to the Madhesh Province Police Office, 33 transformers were stolen in fiscal year 2082/83 BS. Mahottari recorded the highest number with 11 thefts, followed by Saptari with seven, Dhanusha and Bara with four each, Sarlahi with three, Siraha with two and Rautahat with one.

A total of 101 transformers were stolen across Madhesh between fiscal years 2078/79 BS and 2082/83 BS.

NEA officials say transformers installed in open fields for irrigation and drinking water projects are particularly vulnerable. Although the authority has started welding transformers to deter thieves, criminals have been cutting through the welds.

Police and NEA officials have called for stronger surveillance and greater community involvement to prevent further thefts.

title.rendered: 3 months on, CAN leaves six job applications in limbo amid questions over team manager post

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 19

The Cricket Association of Nepal (CAN) has yet to conclude the recruitment process for six positions it opened applications for three months ago, raising questions among applicants over the fate of the vacancies.

CAN had opened applications on April 24 for the positions of national men’s cricket team manager, women’s cricket development officer, front desk officer, inventory officer, procurement officer and junior officer (finance).

The deadline for applications was May 10. However, CAN has not publicly announced any progress since the vacancies were published on its official website and Facebook page.

Applicants say they have received no information about the recruitment process.

“I applied, but I haven’t heard anything so far. I also need to find out what happened,” one applicant said.

Even CAN’s central members appear to be unaware of the progress.

“I know the vacancies were announced. I don’t know what happened after that,” a CAN central member said.

CAN President Chatur Bahadur Chand said a selection committee had been formed under General Manager Utsav Dhungana to oversee the recruitment process.

However, CAN Treasurer Padam Khadka has claimed that the team manager position is not currently necessary, raising further questions over whether the recruitment process will move forward.

Manager vacancy changed after controversy

CAN had initially set a specific qualification for applicants seeking the national men’s team manager position.

Under the original criteria, candidates were required to have represented Nepal at the international level for at least three years or to have played top-level domestic cricket for at least five years.

The criteria drew strong criticism, with concerns that it had been designed to favour a particular individual.

CAN subsequently revised the criteria on the same day following the controversy.

Despite opening applications for the position, CAN officials now say the team does not currently require a permanent manager.

Khadka said the manager position would not be filled immediately and that the issue would be taken up at CAN’s upcoming Annual General Meeting.

“There’s no need for a manager right now. What would a manager do? The Nepal A team is going to Australia while the senior team is going to Malaysia. What would one manager do?” Khadka said.

He added that CAN would seek approval from its upcoming AGM before proceeding with the position.

Nepal has repeatedly travelled without a team manager

The uncertainty comes at a time when Nepal’s national team has repeatedly faced management problems due to the absence of a permanent team manager.

Nepal recently returned from the Netherlands after playing an ICC World Cup League 2 series without a win.

CAN had assigned Shridhar KC, secretary of the Karnali Province Cricket Association and president of the Surkhet District Cricket Association, as team manager for the Netherlands series.

However, delays in his appointment and visa processing prevented him from travelling with the team, leaving Nepal without a manager during the series.

Nepal had also travelled without a team manager during the League 2 series held at home last April.

At the time, CAN central member Diwakar Ghale had criticised the practice of creating the manager position primarily for overseas travel.

“We still haven’t properly understood the importance of a manager,” Ghale had written on social media, arguing that the position should also be used effectively during domestic series.

Nepal had faced a similar situation during a League 2 series in the UAE, where technical analyst Raman Shiwakoti took on the manager’s responsibilities in the absence of a designated team manager.

CAN officials continue to send provincial and district officials

CAN’s failure to appoint a permanent manager has meant that officials and members from district and provincial cricket associations are regularly being sent with the national team.

KC, who was previously unable to travel to the Netherlands because of visa-related issues, has now travelled to Australia as manager of Nepal A for the Top End T20 Series.

A CAN member alleged that the manager position had increasingly been used to send individuals preferred by the CAN leadership on overseas tours.

“CAN leadership has been using the manager position as a vote bank by sending people of its choice abroad,” the member said. “They are afraid that this practice could stop if the recruitment process moves forward.”

Foreign coaches have also reportedly advised CAN to appoint one permanent team manager rather than changing managers from one tournament to another.

CAN had opened the vacancy with the intention of appointing a permanent manager, but the recruitment process has remained stalled amid internal disagreements.

‘Opening a vacancy does not guarantee recruitment’

CAN Treasurer Khadka said opening vacancies does not mean all the advertised positions will necessarily be filled.

He said only positions considered essential would ultimately be recruited.

“We are not saying we will recruit for all these vacancies. We will recruit only for positions that are absolutely necessary. Just because we open vacancies does not guarantee that we will hire everyone and create a jumbo team that becomes a financial burden on CAN,” Khadka said.

Khadka said additional staff would be recruited only after CAN moves to a new office and assesses its actual requirements.

“We opened vacancies for the staff we need. We don’t have sufficient office space at Mulpani. Once we move to an office outside, we will add staff as needed. Simply adding employees creates a financial burden on CAN,” he said.

The uncertainty over the six vacancies, particularly the national team’s manager position, has left applicants waiting while the national cricket team continues to operate without a permanent management structure.
