title.rendered: After months of criticism, Speaker DP Aryal takes a tougher line with government

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 18

Speaker DP Aryal has stepped up pressure on the government, directing Prime Minister Balendra Shah to appear in Parliament and answer lawmakers’ questions.

Aryal’s latest move comes after months of criticism from opposition parties that he had failed to make the government accountable to Parliament and had appeared too accommodating toward the ruling side.

On Monday, Aryal issued three important rulings.

First, he directed Prime Minister Shah to attend the House and answer lawmakers’ questions under the provisions of the House of Representatives Regulations.

Second, he instructed the concerned minister to respond within three days to questions raised in Parliament regarding the Jajarkot earthquake-affected areas.

Third, he gave the concerned minister three days to inform Parliament about efforts to bring back the body of Santosh Rai of Dhading from Cambodia.

The ruling on the prime minister’s appearance is particularly significant. Opposition parties had been obstructing Parliament for 78 days, demanding that Shah answer questions over his remarks concerning Nepal-India border issues.

The dispute began after Shah, while addressing Parliament on May 31, said Nepal had also encroached on Indian territory in several places. Opposition lawmakers demanded evidence and sought clarification from the prime minister.

However, Shah did not return to Parliament to address the issue, while the opposition continued its protest throughout the Nepali months of Jestha, Ashadh and Shrawan.

The Speaker had repeatedly faced criticism for failing to bring the prime minister to Parliament despite assuring opposition lawmakers that he would do so.

Speaker DP Aryal, who was elected to Parliament from the Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP), was also accused of becoming a “helpless shadow” of the powerful government.

But his approach appears to have changed as Parliament entered its fifth month.

Aryal on Monday ruled that the prime minister must appear in the House and answer lawmakers’ questions under Rules 56, 57, 58, 59 and 60 of the House of Representatives Regulations, 2083.

He has also fixed August 26 for a direct question-and-answer session with the prime minister.

Government told to answer questions raised in ‘zero hour’

Speaker DP Aryal also sought to address another longstanding complaint of lawmakers: that issues raised during the zero hour were being ignored by the government.

On August 7, Nepali Communist Party lawmaker Gopal Sharma had raised concerns about the situation in the Jajarkot and Salyan areas affected by the earthquake. He had given the government nine days to provide answers but said no response had been received.

Sharma later demanded that the Speaker set a deadline for the government to respond, warning that he would otherwise be forced to protest in the House.

RSP lawmaker Ashika Tamang also raised the issue of bringing the body of Dhading resident Santosh Rai back from Cambodia.

Tamang said she had raised the issue 37 days earlier but had received no response.

“I thought that once an issue was raised in the House, it would be implemented. But how long should a lawmaker keep going from ministers’ offices to secretaries’ offices with the same issue?” she asked.

She said she would continue standing in the House until the government responded.

Instead of asking the lawmakers to wait, Aryal directly instructed the government to provide answers within three days.

“Regarding the issues raised by lawmakers Gopal Sharma and Ashika Tamang, I direct the government to provide answers within three days,” he said.

Speaker DP Aryal also appeared willing to enforce parliamentary rules against members of the ruling party.

When RSP lawmaker Sulav Kharel sought time to speak under the emergency session, he began discussing local and provincial elections and praised his party for starting a candidate club.

Aryal stopped him, saying the issue did not qualify as an emergency matter and asked him to sit down.

Under the House regulations, emergency time is meant for serious developments occurring between two parliamentary meetings that require the government’s immediate attention.

But questions over the Speaker remain

Speaker DP Aryal’s tougher stance comes after he himself faced criticism over his handling of the prime minister’s controversial remarks.

On August 4, Shram Sanskriti Party chair Harka Sampang had questioned why the Speaker had not issued a ruling on Shah’s statement that Nepal had encroached on Indian territory.

Aryal had, meanwhile, made several attempts to persuade Shah to appear in Parliament.

On May 21, he visited the Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers to meet Shah.

On July 14, Shah and RSP chair Rabi Lamichhane met Aryal at the Speaker’s office for around five minutes.

Aryal again met Shah on July 29 and urged him to address contemporary issues in Parliament. According to Aryal, Shah responded that he would “consider” the proposal.

On August 11, Aryal again visited the prime minister’s office and reminded Shah of his earlier commitment to consider appearing in Parliament.

After those informal efforts failed, Aryal issued a formal ruling from the parliamentary rostrum on Monday.

Some had also questioned why the Speaker repeatedly went to the prime minister’s office when the executive and legislature have separate constitutional roles.

Speaker DP Aryal has defended the visits, saying that going to meet someone does not make a person smaller.

He also held discussions with opposition leaders, including RSP chair Lamichhane.

A leader close to Aryal said the Speaker had become increasingly concerned about the way Parliament was functioning.

“Even when the RSP alone had 182 lawmakers, there were times when there were not enough members to meet the quorum to advance government bills,” the leader said. “These incidents made the Speaker realise that Parliament could not continue functioning this way.”

Former Parliament Secretariat secretary Som Bahadur Thapa welcomed Aryal’s latest moves.

“The Speaker’s role is to make Parliament organised, dignified and effective and to make the government accountable to the House,” Thapa said. “There had been questions about shortcomings in this role. The Speaker has now issued rulings. Even if it came late, it is a positive step.”

Thapa described Aryal’s change in approach as a sign that he had learned from his experience of running Parliament for four months.

Will the prime minister appear?

The key question now is whether Prime Minister Shah will comply with the Speaker DP Aryal’s ruling.

There is already a precedent of ministers answering questions on behalf of the prime minister.

On May 14, Finance Minister Dr Swarnim Wagle answered questions raised in Parliament regarding the government’s policies and programmes on behalf of the prime minister.

Opposition parties criticised the move as disrespectful to Parliament, while RSP lawmaker Bipin Acharya defended it as a departure from established practice.

A similar arrangement was followed during discussions on the budget, when Wagle answered questions concerning the Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers.

Shah’s last appearance in the House was on July 14. He stayed for around 20 minutes before leaving, after which Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs Minister Sobita Gautam presented government proposals on his behalf.

The emerging practice has raised a broader question: can the prime minister remain absent from Parliament while ministers perform his parliamentary duties?

The Speaker’s latest ruling may now put that question to the test.

The prime minister has also been criticised for not maintaining the parliamentary practice of being present when opposition leaders address the House. Congress parliamentary party leader Bhishma Raj Angdembe has argued that the prime minister’s presence during an opposition leader’s address is an established parliamentary practice internationally.

title.rendered: I lived through the first Taliban girls’ school ban — watching it happen again is heartbreaking

content.rendered:
In August 2021, the Taliban recaptured Kabul and, within weeks, barred girls from attending school beyond Grade 6. The ban has not lifted.

Afghanistan remains the only country in the world that formally bars girls and women from secondary and higher education. In the years since, Afghan women have also been banned from working across most sectors that once employed them, from the civil service to national and international aid organizations.

About 2.2 million adolescent girls have been barred from secondary school for nearly 1,800 days. A 2026 UNICEF analysis projects Afghanistan will lose up to 20,000 women teachers and 5,400 health-care workers by 2030, with the restrictions already costing the country an estimated $84 million US a year.

Since September 2025, Taliban forces have also barred Afghan women, including United Nations staff, from entering UN offices. In January 2026, women civil servants lost even the reduced pay they had received since 2021 for staying home.

I watched a version of this happen once before, as a young girl in 1996, the last time the Taliban took Kabul.

What strikes me most about this second ban isn’t that it happened again. It’s that the world’s failure this time isn’t due to a lack of awareness. Everyone knows what’s happening to Afghan girls. The failure is that knowing has not carried any real cost for the Taliban.

What Afghan women have built

Within days of the takeover, Afghan women were in the streets of Kabul chanting “Bread, Work, Freedom,” a demand they have kept making since, at real personal risk. The defining rallying cry calls for basic human rights — education and employment in the face of systemic erasure from public life.

Groups of Afghan women have organized protests throughout that time, even as participants have described arrests, torture and killings in response — reactions so severe they’ve forced much of their resistance work underground.

As recently as February 2026, girls were back on the streets of Kabul, still demanding education. But where protest has become too dangerous, Afghan women have built something quieter instead: informal networks of underground schools, run out of homes, that teach girls who would otherwise have no access to a classroom at all.

None of this resistance is happening because it’s easy or safe. It’s happening because no one else has done it for them, and it has to be done.

Alongside protest and underground schooling, Afghan women’s organizations have also taken on documentation. As of June 2026, researchers at Georgetown University’s Institute for Women, Peace and Security counted 264 Taliban decrees affecting human rights since 2021, 166 of which specifically target women and girls.

International response falls short

The main channel for international engagement with the Taliban is the UN-led Doha process. There have been multiple rounds of talks with Taliban representatives since 2023 in pursuit of Afghanistan’s eventual reintegration into the international community — normalized diplomatic relations, formal recognition of the Taliban government and the country’s return to standard participation in international institutions and trade.

At the Taliban’s insistence, women and Afghan civil society groups have been excluded from the main talks, meeting separately and on the sidelines instead. Sima Samar, former chairperson of the Afghan Independent Human Rights Commission, has argued that by accepting the Taliban’s terms for participation, the UN risks indirectly legitimizing the very policies it says it opposes.

That risk is disputed within the UN itself. Georgette Gagnon, the UN’s Deputy Special Representative and Officer-in-Charge of the UN Assistance Mission in Afghanistan, argued the opposite case at that same session: that continued, principled but pragmatic engagement remains necessary even when progress is incremental.

That disagreement, playing out at the UN’s own podium, captures the trap Afghan women have been describing for years — statements of concern are issued regularly and they cost the Taliban nothing.

Global efforts

In September 2024, Australia, Canada, Germany and the Netherlands formally invoked Afghanistan’s obligations under CEDAW, the UN convention against discrimination against women that Afghanistan ratified in 2003. It is a genuinely significant initiative because it’s the first time any states have attempted to hold another accountable at the world’s highest court for gender discrimination.

But two years on, the case has still not reached the International Court of Justice (ICJ). Civil society’s own statement marking the initiative’s first anniversary has described it as an effort that may eventually culminate in an ICJ case, not one that has achieved it.

When the Netherlands and Canada pursued a similar case against Syria over torture, they moved through each stage without delay. Once negotiations stalled in 2022, they promptly requested arbitration. When Syria failed to engage within the required six-month window, they filed at the ICJ in 2023 and secured a binding order.

After invoking the same mechanism against Afghanistan, no equivalent milestone has been reached. Negotiations, if they have failed, have not visibly given way to a request for arbitration, and the case remains where it started.

Afghan women, and the states that made this commitment on their behalf, deserve the same procedural urgency that carried the Syria case through to a resolution.

The scale of what this inaction has allowed is well-documented.

Personal reflections

I recognize all of this because I lived a version of it once already.

In 1996, I was a young girl a few weeks from final exams when the Taliban took over Kabul. That night, with no electricity, we gathered around a radio and heard we were promoted to the next grade, but that schools were closing to girls until further notice.

At first, I didn’t understand what that meant. As a young student, I was excited about the cancellation of final exams, so I ran to tell my grandmother. Partway down a dark corridor, what it actually meant caught up with me: there would be no school next year. I sat down and cried.

But I was fortunate.

My parents moved my sister and me to Pakistan so we could keep studying, a decision many Afghan families could not afford. We could not either. It was my aunts and uncles living overseas who supported our studies.

Friends of mine were not able to finish school and, as far as I know, were married off instead. I went on to become the first woman to serve as a director, then deputy minister, then acting minister of mines and petroleum in the Afghan cabinet.

Those conditions changed for my generation. Nothing guarantees they will for this one — awareness alone will not accomplish that.

Afghan women have spent the last five years proving they have not accepted this ban as permanent. It is worth asking why the rest of the world has settled for so much less than that.

title.rendered: After release, Kishor Shrestha says pressure won’t stop him from writing

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 17

Journalist Kishor Shrestha, who was released following a court order, has said pressure and intimidation will not stop him from reporting what he sees.

The Supreme Court had ordered his release on Monday.

Speaking after his release, Shrestha said he was not even allowed to meet his legal counsel while in custody. He expressed concern that such actions could be the beginning of similar treatment of other journalists.

Shrestha said he had faced pressure from the authorities in the past for reporting on issues he had witnessed, but he had never backed down.

“They did not even allow me to meet my lawyer. But I have not lost, and I will not lose. Until I die, I will continue to write what I see,” Shrestha said.

He said some people had been unhappy since he brought the report prepared by former Supreme Court justice Gauri Bahadur Karki into the public domain.

Shrestha also warned the government against taking the law into its own hands and using state agencies to exert pressure.

“I have faced such excesses from the state in the past as well,” he said, reiterating that he would continue his work despite the pressure.

title.rendered: Task force formed to study Birgunj Sugar Factory operations

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 17

A task force has been formed to study the possibility of reviving the Birgunj Sugar Factory, which has been closed for years.

According to the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies, Minister Gauri Kumari Yadav’s secretariat says the task force was formed based on a Cabinet decision. It has been tasked with studying the factory’s current condition and preparing the feasibility assessment and necessary action plan for restarting operations.

The task force will study the closed factory’s current status, past decisions made about it, previous studies and reports on reviving it, and the steps that should now be taken.

The task force has been given 15 days to complete its study and submit a report. The team is coordinated by CDE Srikant Yadav from the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies, with members including a section officer from the ministry and an officer representative from the Department of Industry.

The study will examine the current condition of the factory’s buildings, structures, and machinery, and assess how usable they are. The task force will also determine whether the factory can be restarted using the existing structures and machinery or whether new technology and infrastructure would be needed.

Alongside this, the task force will study the status of land and other assets owned by the Birgunj Sugar Factory. It has been tasked with identifying problems related to these assets and preparing the necessary legal and administrative options to resolve them.

title.rendered: Mukti & Revival, Shiva Pariyar, Samikshya Adhikari to resonate across the USA

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 17

Singer Shiva Pariyar and singer Samikshya Adhikari are set to perform across the USA. Joining them on tour will be Mukti & Revival.

These are two separate programs being organised by Three E Entertainment, USA, aimed at bringing entertainment and a cultural atmosphere to Nepali communities in America.

Through the “Dashain-Tihar Dhamaka USA Tour 2026,” singers Adhikari and Pariyar will perform roughly 20 shows. Their schedule kicks off on September 25 in Austin and September 26 in Dallas.

The tour then continues to Columbus on October 2, Akron on October 3, Harrisburg on October 9, Lancaster on October 10, Ashburn on October 11, Milwaukee on October 17, and Chicago on October 18.

Further dates are set for Charlotte on October 24, Earle on October 25, Nebraska on October 30, New York on October 31, and Bradford and Hartford on November 1. Florida is planned for November 7, with a few additional dates possibly to be added.

Mukti & Revival is also preparing performances across various American cities to celebrate 30 years of its musical journey in the Nepal Blues tradition. The band’s special tour is titled Musical Revival, Sadhana Bhandari 30th Anniversary Tour.

Under the slogan “The Legacy, The Blues, The Revival,” the tour will give special focus to marking Sadhana Bhandari’s 30th anniversary. According to the band’s schedule, shows are planned in Dallas on September 12, Houston on September 18, St. Louis on September 19, and New Hampshire on September 26.

title.rendered: Scott Kuggeleijn to play NPL 3 with Sudurpaschim Royals

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 17

New Zealand fast bowler Scott Kuggeleijn will return to the Sudurpaschim Royals for the third edition of the Nepal Premier League (NPL).

The Royals announced Kuggeleijn’s re-signing through a statement on Monday, making him their second overseas signing for the upcoming season.

Kuggeleijn was among the leading wicket-takers in the inaugural edition of the NPL, taking 17 wickets in nine matches. He finished joint-top of the wicket-taking charts.

In the second edition, he claimed 10 wickets in nine matches for the Royals.

The third edition of the NPL is scheduled to begin on October 26. Sudurpaschim had earlier signed England all-rounder Saif Zaib as their first overseas player for the upcoming season.

Royals Chief Executive Officer Prakash Khadka said the franchise was delighted to welcome Kuggeleijn back.

“We expect him to make the same contribution he made in the first and second editions. We believe he will play an important role in helping us win our first title,” Khadka said.

Sudurpaschim have retained captain Dipendra Singh Airee, along with Binod Bhandari, Aarif Sheikh, Ishan Pandey, Abinash Bohara, Hemant Dhami and Hikmat Mahara for the third edition.

The franchise signed Deepak Bohara, Milan Bohara, Tek Rawat, Anil Kharel, Sachin Bhatta and Aayush Chand through the auction.

title.rendered: Budget spending falls, revenue collection rises in first month

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 17

Overall budget spending declined in the first month of the current government’s fiscal year 2026/27.

According to the Office of the Comptroller General, the government spent Rs 41.89 billion by the end of Shrawan, lower than the same period last fiscal year, when spending stood at Rs 46.30 billion. This year’s Shrawan spending amounts to 1.68% of the annual target, compared to 2.36% progress during the same month last year.

Last year’s first-month spending figure was inflated largely by financial arrangement expenses, which totalled Rs 27.10 billion in that Saun. This year, such spending came to Rs 19.15 billion, funds typically used to repay the principal on public debt.

The government is implementing a total budget of Rs 2,124.34 billion this year. Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle has maintained that no revision to spending will be needed when the mid-year review of this budget takes place.

Capital spending sees modest growth

First-month capital expenditure showed a slight increase compared to the same period last year. Of the total capital budget of Rs 421.10 billion, the government managed to spend just Rs 1.33 billion in Saun, only 0.31% of the target.

Last year’s Shrawan capital spending was even lower, at Rs 726.3 million, or just 0.18% of the target. Looking at the pattern, capital spending continues to lag in the opening months of the fiscal year, even though this is when development work should ideally be picking up pace.

The budget being presented on 15 Jestha is meant to allow 45 days of preparatory work before implementation begins on 1 Shrawan. In practice, however, preparatory work for the new budget doesn’t gain momentum until after Saun begins, meaning spending consistently falls short of targets.

Current expenditure in the first month came to Rs 21.40 billion, or 1.68% of this year’s Rs 1,270 billion target.

Revenue collection rises

Revenue collection in Shrawan rose somewhat compared to last year, reaching Rs 92.22 billion this year against Rs 84.46 billion in the same month last year. This represents 5.84% of the year’s target, compared to 5.71% achieved last year.

The government has set a revenue collection target of Rs 1,480 billion for this year. The first month also saw Rs 24.03 million in grants received. Total government income for Saun came to Rs 93.43 billion, or 5.69% of the annual target.

title.rendered: PM Balen Shah to face MPs’ questions in Parliament on August 26

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 17

Prime Minister Balen Shah will face lawmakers’ questions during a direct question-and-answer session in the House of Representatives on August 26.

Speaker Dol Prasad Aryal has scheduled the session in accordance with Rule 56 of the House of Representatives Regulations.

Rule 56 requires the Speaker to allocate the first hour of a meeting during the first week of every month for questions directly related to the prime minister or matters under the prime minister’s jurisdiction.

The rule also states that if the House cannot meet on the scheduled day for any reason, the session should be held during the first hour of the immediately following meeting.

The provision has not been implemented regularly, prompting questions over the delay in holding direct question-and-answer sessions with the prime minister. The Speaker has now fixed a date for the programme.

Under Rule 57, the question-and-answer session may be broadcast live through government and other media outlets.

Lawmakers wishing to question the prime minister must submit written information about the subject of their questions to the Speaker at least three days before the meeting, as stipulated by Rule 58.

The Speaker will determine whether submitted questions are admissible, while other procedures for the session will be determined by the Speaker under Rule 59.

Rule 60 states that no discussion will be held in the House regarding answers provided by the prime minister under the direct question-and-answer provision.

title.rendered: Barsaman Pun draws government’s attention to 22 disaster deaths in Rolpa

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, 17 August

Nepali Communist Party lawmaker Barsaman Pun has drawn the government’s attention to the deaths of 22 people in floods, landslides and lightning strikes in his home district Rolpa over the past two weeks.

Speaking at the House of Representatives meeting on Monday, Pun said several parts of Rolpa had suffered significant loss of life and property due to natural disasters during the latter half of Shrawan.

According to Pun, 13 people were killed in a massive landslide in the Uwa area of Thawang Rural Municipality on August 12. The following day, four people died in a landslide in Seram of Sunachhari Rural Municipality.

Similarly, one person died in a landslide at Dhaireni in Lungri Rural Municipality on August 15, he said.

Pun said two more people died in a landslide in Seram the following week, while another person was killed in Pachhawang of Paribartan Rural Municipality.

He also informed the House that one person died after being struck by lightning in Lungri Rural Municipality-1.

Paying tribute to those who lost their lives in the disasters, Pun wished those injured a speedy recovery. He also informed the House that he had already met Prime Minister Balendra Shah (Balen) and drawn his attention to the situation.

Pun called on the government to strengthen mechanisms for disaster preparedness, search and rescue and relief. He said state agencies should be made more effective in conducting search and rescue operations in affected areas and relief materials should be delivered immediately.

He also urged the government to immediately reopen the Sulichaur-Uwa-Thawang road, which has been obstructed by landslides.

According to Pun, drinking water infrastructure, roads and bridges have also been damaged and need to be reconstructed.

He called on the government to immediately send a geological study team to identify long-term risks in areas of Rolpa that are repeatedly affected by landslides.

“I have also met the Honourable Prime Minister and drawn his attention to the issue. The government should focus on preparedness. Search and rescue mechanisms should be made more effective, and relief materials should reach the affected areas immediately,” he said.

“I specifically urge the government to immediately reopen the Sulichaur-Uwa-Thawang road. Drinking water systems, roads and bridges have been damaged. They should be restored soon, and a geological study team should be sent without delay for long-term assessment,” Pun added.

He also urged the government to make necessary arrangements for the resettlement of affected communities and reconstruction of damaged infrastructure.

title.rendered: Landless squatters demand probe into death of man at Bhaktapur holding centre

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 17

Family members and landless squatters have demanded an independent investigation into the death of 57-year-old Hira Hazara Paswan, who was found hanging at a holding centre in Bode, Bhaktapur, on August 13.

Paswan had been staying at the holding centre after his house in the Thapathali squatter settlement was demolished by the government in April.

Following the demolition, his family was moved to a holding centre in Kirtipur. They were later shifted to Bode after the Kirtipur facility was flooded, damaging the belongings they had managed to save from the demolition.

The United National Landless Squatters’ Front has said Paswan’s death should be investigated, alleging that he had been subjected to prolonged mental pressure following his displacement.

“His house was demolished by a bulldozer, the belongings that remained were swept away by floods, and he received nothing from the state except continuous mental pressure and despair,” the front said in a statement issued on Monday.

Paswan is survived by his wife, son, daughter-in-law, two granddaughters and a grandson.

The organisation also alleged that the family was subjected to further pressure after his death instead of receiving support and sympathy from the state.

“The government forcibly conducted the post-mortem and pressured the family to take the body to Bara overnight for cremation instead of providing comfort and support,” the statement said.

It further alleged that police mistreated people who were attempting to communicate with the grieving family.

The front’s acting chairperson Lil Bahadur Tamang and general secretary Arjun Kunwar have described Paswan’s death as a structural killing and called for an investigation by the National Human Rights Commission or another independent body.

Family members have also called for an investigation into the circumstances surrounding his death.

“How did Hiralal Paswan reach a situation where he had to take his own life? Was he subjected to administrative, social or psychological pressure? What were the conditions at the holding centre?” they asked.

They also demanded an investigation into whether any illegal or inhumane treatment was carried out by authorities during the displacement or relocation process.

The landless squatters say the government had claimed that all necessary preparations had been completed before demolishing their settlements. However, they allege that the authorities lacked adequate preparations from the holding centres through the verification process.

They also claim that some displaced people were being sent, based on their citizenship documents, to addresses they had abandoned decades ago, further deepening their frustration and uncertainty.

The front has demanded that Paswan be declared a martyr of the landless movement, along with compensation for the loss of physical structures and proper rehabilitation of affected families.

It has also called for an immediate halt to what it termed “bulldozer terror” against landless and squatter communities and demanded protection of their rights under the Land Act 2021.

According to the front, Paswan is the ninth landless person to have died since the government began demolishing squatter settlements with bulldozers in April.

The organisation said those who have died include Indra Bahadur Rai, Rabin Tamang, Kamala Balampaki, Hira Pun, Bhesh Bahadur Darji, Ratan Devi Malahani, Ujjwal Tamang, Parbati BK and Paswan.

title.rendered: Shashank Koirala willing to accept Gagan Thapa as NC president if senior leaders are accommodated

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 17

Nepali Congress leader Dr Shashank Koirala has said he is ready to accept Gagan Thapa as the party president if senior leaders are also accommodated in the party structure.

Speaking to journalists outside the contact office of the establishment-opposition faction in Chundevi, Koirala urged Thapa to include senior leaders and other factions rather than excluding them.

“Senior leaders should be included; they should not be left out. Gagan Thapa, you can remain as president. But please accommodate the other colleagues as well,” Koirala said.

Asked specifically whether he was ready to accept Thapa as party president, Koirala replied, “We are ready to accept Gagan Thapa as the president.”

Koirala said he was making efforts to resolve the differences between the two factions and bring the party leadership together. He said he had been working to reduce the distance between former president Sher Bahadur Deuba and Thapa and had held several rounds of talks with Thapa.

According to Koirala, there had also been attempts to draw him into one side of the dispute, but he had refused to go alone.

Koirala also said the ongoing dispute within the party was essentially a struggle over positions and urged both sides to be clear about what they wanted.

“Both sides should be able to say clearly what they want. What else is there to want? It is the position. If they did not want positions, why would there be such a big fight?” he said.

Koirala said he would continue efforts to bridge the differences between the two sides and seek a compromise within the party.

title.rendered: Arjun Kulung Rai and Manju Sunuwar win Backyard Ultra 2026

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, 17 August

Arjun Kulung Rai and Manju Sunuwar won the men’s and women’s titles respectively at Backyard Ultra 2026, organised by Ultra Trails Nepal.

Competing for Xtep, Rai completed 33 laps to finish first in the men’s category and set a new course record. The previous record was 32 laps, held by Hemanta Rana.

Manju also set a new course record in the women’s category by completing 14 laps. The previous record was 12 laps.

Both winners received a cash prize of Rs 30,000 each. Cash prizes were also awarded to competitors finishing from second to 10th place.

Participants had to complete one 6.7-kilometre lap within one hour. Competitors who failed to complete a lap within the one-hour limit were eliminated from the race.

Race director Diwakar Budha said competitions of this kind could contribute to promoting tourism in Nepal.

According to the organisers, 65 competitors from Nepal, France, the United States, Denmark, Norway, Switzerland and other countries participated in the event.

The race started from Matchegaun in Chandragiri Municipality, passed through various parts of the area and finished at the same location.

The organisers said the 2026 Backyard Ultra World Championship will be held in Pokhara on October 17.

title.rendered: Home Minister’s hasty order leaves police administration confused

content.rendered:
Gorkha, August 17

Home Minister Sudan Gurung has directed police to immediately remove a fence installed to protect land owned by the Nepal Police in Manakamana, Gorkha, leaving local representatives and the police administration confused.

The Home Minister issued the directive on Sunday while meeting voters in Manakamana. After hearing complaints from locals, he instructed the police to remove the fence surrounding the land belonging to the Area Police Office.

However, local representatives and residents say the land belongs to the police and that the fence was installed last year to protect it from encroachment and facilitate construction of a new police office.

They have questioned why the fence should be removed when it has been installed on police-owned property.

The land, located near the ward office in Shahid Lakhan Rural Municipality-2, is registered under plot number 799 in the name of the Nepal Police. Police had fenced the property last year with plans to construct a new building for the Area Police Office.

The Home Minister’s directive has now left the police administration uncertain about how to proceed.

Ramesh Thapa Magar, chairperson of Shahid Lakhan Rural Municipality, said Home Minister Gurung may have been given incorrect information by people pursuing their own interests.

“The Home Minister’s responsibility is to properly manage the Nepal Police. The Manakamana police office is currently operating on trust land. The police should have protected their own land and proceeded with construction of the police office,” Magar said.

“But someone appears to have briefed the Home Minister incorrectly.”

Magar said preparations were also underway to upgrade the Area Police Office to a ‘Category A’ facility, making a permanent building necessary.

Shakun Thapa, ward chairperson of Shahid Lakhan-2, also said there was no reason to remove the fence.

“That is the police office’s land. I don’t see any reason to demolish a fence installed on its own land,” she said.

Thapa said a court case had previously been filed over the land, following which the Survey Office had separated the areas belonging to the ward office, police office and public land.

“The Home Minister may not have known about this. Some people may have tried to influence him for their own interests,” she said.

Local resident Dinesh Joshi also confirmed that the fenced land belongs to the Nepal Police.

“The police office has not occupied anyone else’s land. It has fenced its own land,” he said.

Locals say some people had previously been using the property for their own purposes, including storing construction materials and parking vehicles. The dispute intensified after police fenced the land, preventing such use.

According to locals, some residents of Pujari village have been putting pressure on authorities to remove the fence.

Gorkha District Police Chief SP Anil Kumar Khadka said the fence was installed to protect the police office’s own property.

“We fenced our own police office land to protect it. Now the Home Minister has instructed us to remove it,” Khadka said. “We will coordinate with police headquarters and proceed according to the instructions from higher authorities.”

Gorkha Chief District Officer Tulsi Bahadur Shrestha declined to comment on the matter.

This is not the first time Home Minister Gurung has faced criticism over directives issued during his visits to his home district. He had previously faced criticism over his directive concerning the management of Bahrakilo Bazaar, which has been established through encroachment on forest land.

title.rendered: New govt formation process begins in Bagmati Province after Baniya’s resignation

content.rendered:
Hetauda, 17 August

The process of forming a new government in Bagmati Province has begun following a change in the power equation.

The process will move forward after Nepali Congress leader Indra Bahadur Baniya resigned as chief minister on Monday, submitting his resignation to Province Province Chief Deepak Prasad Devkota.

Province Province Chief Devkota will now invite parties represented in the provincial assembly to stake a claim to form a new government in accordance with the constitutional provisions.

Leaders say the new government is likely to be formed based on an earlier agreement between the Nepali Communist Party and CPN-UML to run coalition governments in the provinces.

Under the two-party power-sharing arrangement, the CPN-UML has been agreed to lead the Bagmati Province government.

The 104-member provincial assembly requires a majority of 53 lawmakers to form a government. The Nepali Communist Party and CPN-UML have 51 lawmakers combined, meaning they need the support of another party to secure a majority.

The Nepali Congress has 36 seats, the Nepali Communist Party 26, CPN-UML 25, Rastriya Prajatantra Party 12, Nepal Workers’ and Peasants’ Party three and Hamro Nepali Party two.

Rastriya Prajatantra Party’s support appears crucial for the Nepali Communist Party and CPN-UML to secure a majority.

There could be legal complications if the two parties rely only on the support of Hamro Nepali Party to claim a majority and subsequently secure a vote of confidence.

Article 186 of the Constitution provides that decisions in the provincial assembly are made by a majority of members present and voting. The provision does not give the presiding officer the right to vote, except in the event of a tie.

According to Provincial Assembly spokesperson and Deputy Secretary of Law Prakash Chapagain, the presiding officer can cast a deciding vote only when votes are equally divided.

CPN-UML lawmaker Apsara Chapagain is the deputy speaker. The post of speaker has remained vacant since August last year, and she has been presiding over the assembly.

A Supreme Court ruling in the case of government formation in Koshi Province suggests that involving the presiding officer in government formation could create legal complications.

In its ruling on July 27, 2023, on a writ petition challenging the formation of the Koshi provincial government, the Supreme Court held that the speaker could not support a particular party or candidate to facilitate government formation.

The court had declared the speaker’s support unconstitutional and overturned the appointment of then-Chief Minister Uddhav Thapa.

Based on that precedent, questions could arise over whether an alliance between the Nepali Communist Party, CPN-UML and Hamro Nepali Party alone would be sufficient to form the government.

One option would be for Deputy Speaker Chapagain to resign from the post and participate in the government formation process only as a provincial assembly member.

If she resigns, the assembly would have to select its senior-most member to preside over the meetings. The senior-most member is Nepali Communist Party lawmaker Ram Prasad Dhungana.

However, even if Dhungana presides over the assembly, he would not be able to vote on a confidence motion unless the votes were equally divided.

Therefore, support from Rastriya Prajatantra Party would make both the government formation and confidence vote processes more secure for the Nepali Communist Party and CPN-UML.

CPN-UML lawmaker and former minister Kiran Thapa Magar said discussions were underway with other parties to secure the required majority to form the new government.

RPP Bagmati parliamentary party leader Uddhav Thapa told Onlinekhabar that the party would make a decision at an appropriate time, recalling the decision of its executive committee.

He indicated that the RPP was likely to participate in the government, saying failure to support the new government could create a constitutional crisis in Bagmati Province .

Who will be the seventh chief minister?

Bagmati Province is expected to get its seventh chief minister within a few days.

Under the power-sharing agreement, the CPN-UML will lead the provincial government. However, the party has yet to finalise its candidate amid an internal dispute.

The future chief minister will be decided after the CPN-UML resolves a no-confidence motion filed against its current parliamentary party leader, Jagannath Thapaliya.

A no-confidence motion was registered on August 12 with the signatures of 16 lawmakers, seeking to replace Thapaliya with Kiran Thapa Magar of Bhaktapur as the parliamentary party leader.

According to Thapa Magar, a meeting of the CPN-UML parliamentary party has been scheduled for 11 am on Tuesday in Hetauda.

The meeting will decide on the no-confidence motion. If the motion against Thapaliya is passed by a majority, Thapa Magar will become the parliamentary party leader.

Thapa Magar has claimed that he has the support of a majority of lawmakers.

title.rendered: Special Court sets Rs 1.5 million bail for Madan Dahal

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, 17 August

The Special Court has ordered the release of former Nepal Insurance Authority chairman and joint secretary Madan Dahal on bail of Rs 1.5 million in a money laundering case.

Dahal appeared before the Special Court and recorded his statement before a bench comprising Justices Narayan Prasad Poudel, Hemanta Rawal and Bidur Koirala ordered his release on bail.

Dahal had been accused of playing a role in the alleged misuse of around Rs 4.27 billion from the funds of Himalayan Life Insurance Company.

The Department of Money Laundering Investigation had accused Dahal of approving repeated investments of a similar nature in the same company and failing to regulate the concentration of investments in the same shares despite the high level of risk.

The department had determined a loss amount of Rs 3.5 billion and sought recovery of half of that amount from Dahal.

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, 17 August

Nepali Congress leader Dr Shashank Koirala has said he is ready to mediate between party president Gagan Thapa and former president Sher Bahadur Deuba to reduce tensions between the two leaders.

Speaking at a tea reception organised by the party’s establishment-opposition faction in Kathmandu on Monday, Koirala said he was willing to facilitate positive dialogue between Thapa and Deuba.

He said that although disputes and disagreements currently exist within the party, there was ultimately no alternative to bringing the party’s top leaders and factions together.

Koirala expressed confidence that the two sides would eventually reach an agreement.

Recalling the periods of BP Koirala and Pradeep Giri, he said political debates in the past were based on ideas and principles.

He expressed concern that contemporary politics had seen a decline in the quality of political language, with personal attacks and abusive remarks increasingly replacing substantive debate.

title.rendered: Nepali Congress’ US sister organisation holds convention after 12 years

content.rendered:
August 17, Kathmandu

The Nepali Congress’s sister organisation, the Janasamparka Samiti in the United States, has elected a new leadership after holding its convention for the first time in 12 years. The organisation elected a new committee under the leadership of Munindra Nembang at its third convention. Nembang was elected president with 266 votes, defeating five other candidates for the post.

Binod Bhatt and Hari P Sharma were elected senior vice-presidents. Nima Bomjan, Sanjiv Shrestha and Shri Thapa were elected vice-presidents. Sushil Khatri was elected youth vice-president, while Narayan Khanal and Gautam Dahal were elected general secretaries. Arjun Bam and Anita Pariyar were elected joint general secretaries, and Narayan P Pokharel was elected treasurer.

Nepali Congress General Secretary Gururaj Ghimire and Joint General Secretary Prakash Rasaili ‘Snehi’ travelled to the United States to attend the convention of the Janasamparka Samiti.

A consumer who purchased goods worth Rs 350 from Ganesh Electronics and Mobile Centre has won the Rs 1 million taxpayer bumper incentive prize under the government’s taxpayer incentive programme.

The Inland Revenue Department announced the second fortnightly prize for Shrawan at an event organised at the Ministry of Finance. Finance Minister Dr Swarnim Wagle and Finance Secretary Dr Ghanshyam Upadhyaya announced the winner.

The prize was awarded among consumers who carried out transactions in accordance with tax regulations between August 1 and 16.

According to the department, the number of consumers participating in the incentive programme surged during its first month.

A total of 357,149 cash transaction bills were uploaded for the prize draw between August 1 and 16.

In comparison, only 7,077 transaction bills had been uploaded by consumers during the first 15 days of Shrawan.

title.rendered: ‘Dimagi Naxal Party’ goes viral after Modi’s remarks, gains 170,000 followers

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 17

A new Instagram account named ‘Dimagi Naxal Party’ has suddenly gained popularity, amassing more than 170,000 followers within just a few days of its launch. The page is currently unavailable on Instagram. Before it was taken down, the page had claimed that it had been subjected to multiple cyberattacks.

The account, @dimaginaxalparty, described itself as the official page of the ‘Dimagi Naxal Party’. Its slogan was “Think, Research, Resist.” Its bio listed the founder as ‘A Dimagi Indian’ and the co-founder as ‘56 Inch Ka’. The account also directed users to the X account @DNJP_India.

As of Monday, the page had 65 posts and followed 35 accounts. The account was created in August. It is not known who operated it. The account followed several prominent figures, including comedian Kunal Kamra, YouTuber Dhruv Rathee, actor Prakash Raj, filmmaker Anurag Kashyap, actress Sonakshi Sinha, comedian Shyam Rangeela, activist Sonam Wangchuk and journalist Ravish Kumar. It also followed an organisation called CJP.

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi used the term ‘Dimagi Naxal’ in his Independence Day address. The account appeared a few days after his remarks. Speaking from the Red Fort, Modi said armed Naxalism had been eliminated from the forests but that ‘Dimagi Naxals’ still existed.

He said people with Maoist ideology were occupying positions in government institutions and influencing policies. He urged people to identify and isolate such individuals. His remarks sparked a political debate between BJP and opposition leaders. Former Home Minister P Chidambaram wrote on X, “I am proud to be a Dimagi Naxal.” He described the term as a new label similar to ‘Urban Naxal’ and the ‘Tukde Tukde Gang’.

Union Minister Kiren Rijiju clarified that Prime Minister Modi had not referred to opposition leaders as ‘Dimagi Naxals’. He said the term was being used for people who support Maoists, reject the Constitution and seek to divide the country.

Earlier, another social media account called ‘Kakroach Janata Party’ had also gone viral. The new account emerged after that. The Kakroach Janata Party has announced a ‘School Thik Karo’ campaign aimed at improving the condition of government schools.

title.rendered: ‘Government seeking long-lasting solutions to educational problems through dialogue’

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 17

Minister for Education and Sports, Sasmit Pokharel, has said that a lasting policy solution to educational problems would be sought based on dialogue and the stakeholders’ suggestions. Minister Pokharel posted on social media today that since taking office as the Minister of Education, he has been adopting a ‘listening and learning’ approach to seriously understand issues in the education sector.

He said that during the first 100 days, some rules and guidelines necessary for reform and good governance were worked out, and now the ministry’s priority is focused on the new Education Act, the Technical Education Act, and contemporary reforms in higher education. Minister Pokharel stated that in this context, a team led by the ministry’s chief advisor and the head of the School Education Division is reaching all seven provinces through the ‘Education Dialogue’ programme, collecting issues, suggestions, and expectations from stakeholders related to the education sector.

The ministry has stated that through dialogue, work is being carried out to directly hear the concerns of local authorities, teachers, education staff, parents, schools, and students. Issues and concerns of early childhood development (ECD) facilitators, teachers, school management, school staff, parents, and students have also been prioritised in the dialogue. Minister Pokharel said that the suggestions received about the role of local bodies, challenges in school management, and various policy issues in the education sector will be used as a basis for future reforms in the education sector.

Stakeholders who cannot physically attend the dialogue can send their suggestions, problems, and expectations through the ‘Education Dialogue: Suggestions, Problems, and Expectations Collection Form.’ The ministry has said that the received suggestions will be included in the policy formulation process. Similarly, the Department of Education is preparing to collect suggestions on the education bill by involving local governments in all seven provinces.

It is said that the expert team formed to revise the national curriculum framework has also reached the final stage of their work. The Education Minister has expressed his commitment to quickly finalise the Education Bill by listening to everyone’s concerns, learning from experts where necessary, and making decisions based on facts. He stated that the ministry is clear and firm in finding sustainable policy solutions to educational problems. It is stated that one can contact 9851014006 to participate in the ‘Education Dialogue’ programme.

title.rendered: Lumbini Chief Minister receives vote of confidence

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 17

Lumbini Province Chief Minister Chet Narayan Acharya has received a vote of confidence from the Provincial Assembly.

At Monday’s session of the Provincial Assembly, the confidence motion tabled by Chief Minister Acharya passed with 45 votes in favour and 26 against. To prove a majority, the government needed 42 votes in the 83-member Provincial Assembly.

Of the assembly’s 83 members, 71 lawmakers took part in the voting process. Chief Minister Acharya received votes of confidence from CPN-UML, the Nepal Communist Party, Rastriya Janamorcha, and Janata Samajwadi Party Nepal.

Since the 45 votes in favour constituted a majority, Speaker Tularam Ghartimagar declared that Chief Minister Acharya had received the vote of confidence.

Acharya received 29 votes from UML, 11 of 12 from the Nepal Communist Party, 4 of 5 from JSP Nepal, and 1 from Janamorcha.

Eight lawmakers were absent from the session, while 3 remained neutral. Among the ruling coalition, one NCP lawmaker was abroad and therefore absent, while JSP Nepal’s Ambika Kafle was also absent. According to the Provincial Assembly Secretariat, those absent from the session were Anurag Khadka, Ambika Kafle, Ashish Kumar Chaudhary, Khadga Basnet, Dhana Laxmi Shrestha, Nirmala Devi Tharu, Maya Pun, and Saroj Thapa.

In the Provincial Assembly, UML and the Nepal Communist Party, along with JSP Nepal and Rastriya Janamorcha Party, form the ruling coalition, while Congress and Janamat stand in opposition. RPP has remained neutral.

Although JSP Nepal’s central leadership had directed the party to withdraw from the government, the party’s parliamentary group in the province decided instead to support the government, helping preserve the UML-led administration.

If JSP Nepal’s four lawmakers had withheld their votes, Chief Minister Acharya would certainly have failed to secure a majority.

title.rendered: RSP begins local election campaign nine months before polls

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, 17 August

With around nine months remaining until the next local elections, the ruling Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) has already begun activities focused on the local polls.

The five-year term of local representatives elected in May 2022 is set to end next April if the election is held as scheduled.

The RSP launched its local election-focused Candidate Club on Monday. At the same time, federal ministers have been visiting various districts and urging locals to vote for RSP candidates in the upcoming local elections.

During an interaction with locals in Siraha on August 15, Health and Food Hygiene Minister Nisha Mehta said it had been difficult for the federal government to work effectively with only an RSP-led government at the centre.

She urged voters to elect RSP governments at the provincial and local levels as well, saying this would allow them to work in line with the federal government’s approach.

“Just as all of you young people came together and worked to give us a victory at the federal level, you now need to make another effort,” she said. “We need our government at the local and provincial levels as well.”

Mehta also urged locals to start voting for RSP candidates, saying the local elections were not far away.

“How much time is left until the election? Around six or nine months,” she said.

Home Minister Sudan Gurung has also been visiting Gorkha and appealing to voters to elect RSP candidates in the upcoming local elections.

During an interaction in a village in Gorkha on August 16, a local resident showed Gurung a social media post written by a ward chairperson.

After learning that the post had been written by a ward chairperson, Gurung said, “The local election is coming. You should think about it now.”

He then openly appealed for votes in the upcoming local election.

“The local election has already started,” Gurung said. “You will show it in the local election. You yourselves will show it.”

He also urged voters to remind leaders of other parties of their past promises if they came seeking votes, while saying the RSP had won the federal election only once and should now be given an opportunity at the local level as well.

“We were elected for the first time, and we have fulfilled our promises. We have come to your doorsteps and returned to meet you. We have come to villages to listen to your problems and meet our voters. It may seem like a small thing, but this has become history,” he said.

Gurung said those unable to deliver on small promises should not make bigger promises, accusing other parties of failing to fulfil their commitments while claiming that the RSP had delivered on its promises.

“Those spreading misinformation, you yourselves should show them the result in the election,” he said.

The Election Commission, however, has not yet begun any formal activities specifically focused on the local elections.

Election Commission spokesperson Narayan Prasad Bhattarai said preparations that can be carried out before the election date is announced, including strengthening internal capacity and management systems, have begun.

“There are things that can and should be done before the election date is announced. This includes the use of information technology and other preparations,” he said.

“Formal election preparations begin only after the election date is announced. However, work to strengthen the commission’s management capacity has already started.”

The usual practice is to announce the election date around 120 days before polling day. The Election Commission has also been telling the government that it needs around two months to prepare for an election.

Based on this timeline, the government could announce the local election date in December. The RSP, however, has already started election-focused activities and public appeals.

According to party leaders, the Candidate Club concept has been introduced to select candidates for the upcoming local elections.

People interested in contesting the local elections can apply to the Candidate Club from Monday. The party has described the application process as the first stage of candidate selection.

The RSP’s central committee had earlier decided to open applications for the Candidate Club to select qualified, honest and capable candidates for the local elections.

Applicants will have to complete classes at the party’s Leadership Academy after submitting their applications. The academy will assess areas including political conduct, policy understanding and commitment to public service.

Candidates aspiring to become mayors, deputy mayors, chairpersons or vice-chairpersons can apply through the Municipality Candidate Club.

Those seeking ward chairperson or ward member positions can apply through the Ward Candidate Club.

Applicants will also have to disclose details about their personal and legal backgrounds, including verification of educational certificates, legal marital status, allegations of abuse or digital crimes, financial integrity, potential conflicts of interest, pending cases and other legal disputes.

title.rendered: Taxpayer Incentive Award for second half of Shrawan to be announced today

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 17

The second fortnightly Taxpayer Incentive Award for Shrawan is set to be announced today. The Inland Revenue Department will organise an event at the Ministry of Finance, where Finance Minister Dr Swarnim Wagle and Finance Secretary Dr Ghanshyam Upadhyaya will announce the winners.

Consumers who engaged in legitimate transactions between Shrawan 16 and 31 will be eligible for today’s draw. According to the department, the number of consumers participating in the incentive scheme surged in its first month. During the 16-day period from Shrawan 16 to 31 alone, 357,149 cash transaction bills were registered (uploaded) for the prize draw.

Previously, only 7,077 consumer transactions had been uploaded during the first 15 days of Shrawan. Meanwhile, the number of consumer transactions automatically entered into the scheme through QR payments increased from 25,608,094 to 32,086,380.

According to the department, the total number of transactions registered for the incentive scheme during the latest 16-day period reached 32,443,229. Of these, 16 winners will be selected today. One winner for each of the 16 days from Shrawan 16 to 31 will receive Rs 133,334. After tax deductions, each winner will receive a net amount of Rs 100,000.

In addition, one winner will receive a bumper prize of Rs 1 million. A 25 per cent tax will be levied on the bumper prize. The event today will also include the presentation of cash prizes to the winners of the first fortnightly award for Shrawan.

content.rendered:
Biratnagar, August 17

The Communist Party of Nepal has finalised the names of ministers who will join the Koshi Province government. Following internal discussions, the party finalised the names of four ministers and one state minister on Monday afternoon.

According to CPN Koshi Province in-charge Rajendra Rai, Jivan Acharya will be given responsibility for the Ministry of Physical Infrastructure Development. He had also served as a minister previously.

Gita Timsina will be appointed Minister for Social Development. Gombu Sherpa will take charge of the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Law, while Khinu Langwa Limbu will be given responsibility for the Ministry of Tourism, Forests and Environment.

Sapana Darji will be appointed State Minister for Physical Infrastructure Development. According to Province in-charge Rai, the newly appointed ministers will take the oath of office today.

title.rendered: Two killed, four injured in Kavre jeep accident, rescued by helicopter

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, August 17

Seriously injured victims of a jeep accident in Syau Thali, Ward 1 of Khanikhola Rural Municipality, Kavrepalanchok, have been rescued by helicopter from Kamidanda in Bethanchok and brought to Dhulikhel Hospital.

According to Khanikhola Rural Municipality Chairman Indra Bahadur Theeng, a helicopter had been arranged to rescue the injured directly from the accident site, but thick fog made this difficult.

Since the weather at the accident site did not clear, victims were first brought by ambulance to Kamidanda in Ward 5 of Bethanchok Rural Municipality, and taken onward by helicopter from there. Bethanchok Ward 5 Chairman Rajkumar Lama said the injured were flown from Kamidanda to Dhulikhel Hospital via a Nepali Army helicopter.

Two people died in the accident: Kalak Bahadur Majhi of Khanikhola-4, and Patalimaya (Anita) Moktan, whose maternal home was in Khanikhola-2 and who lived in Banepa, Sanga. Four others were seriously injured — Rawal Tamang of Sanga, Pradip Jargamagar of Khanikhola-3, Bahutaman Rumba of Dumre, Khanikhola-5, and Dhanpati Rawal of Sukute, Sindhupalchok’s Sangachowk Gadhi Municipality.

The accident occurred after the jeep’s brakes failed and it fell roughly 200 meters down from the road.

title.rendered: Remembering Durga Lal Shrestha, the people’s poet

content.rendered:
As a musician and poet, Durga Lal Shrestha stood tall. In the struggle against the Panchayat system, he gave Nepali literature and music some of the most powerful and moving verse and songs.

That same people’s poet passed away Sunday night at his residence in Budhanilkantha, at the age of 93. Though his ancestral home was in Thamel, he had in recent years been living at his son Suman’s residence in Budhanilkantha.

He had been ill for the past five years. Continuously engaged in literary creation for the past six decades, Shrestha wrote poetry, songs, and other literary forms both in Nepal Bhasa and in Nepali.

Two decades ago, the Nepal Bhasa Parishad honoured him with the title of “Janakavi” (people’s poet). More than a dozen of his works have been published in Nepal Bhasa.

He gave the world many timeless, moving, and internationally admired songs. His song “Jhe Masini” (“We Are Not Dead Yet”) is considered one of the most powerful songs of the Nepal Bhasa movement. Among his most popular songs is “Phoolko Aankhama, Phoolai Sansar“, composed by Nhyoo Bajracharya and sung by Ani Choying Dolma.

The song appears on the album Moments of Bliss, for which Shrestha wrote all the lyrics. This particular song has found admirers well beyond Nepali-speaking audiences. Its universal appeal, warmth, emotional depth, and spiritual sensibility are what make it so striking; its power lies chiefly in the profound life philosophy embedded within Durgalal’s simple words.

For Hari Bansha Acharya’s film 15 Gatey, Shrestha wrote a song, Sayathari Baja Eutai Taal, which tells about the diversity of Nepal.

Hari Bansha has also sung two of Durgalal’s Nepal Bhasa songs. Durgalal’s son Suman and Hari Bansha are also close friends and well-wishers of one another.

The two also collaborated on establishing Model Hospital in Bagbazar. Hari Bansha recalled knowing Durga Lal for 40 years and described him as someone with a genuinely poetic mind to be around.

The defining feature of Durga Lal Shrestha’s songs, poems, and other literary works is his ability to express deep philosophy and human emotion through simple language. His creative work can be understood through a few key characteristics.

Deep philosophy and human sensitivity

His songs and poems carry little weight of difficult vocabulary. He presents profound life philosophy in language easily understood by ordinary readers and listeners.

Love, compassion, coexistence, peace, hope, and a positive outlook form important foundations of his creative work. Many of his writings carry the idea that a person’s perspective on the world shapes their experience of it.

His work is not limited to love or beauty alone; his writing is also sensitive to social inequality, injustice, poverty, human suffering, and societal contradictions.

Since Shrestha was fundamentally a poet, his songs carry a strong poetic quality. The rhythm, feeling, symbolism, and imagery of his words connect naturally with music, which is why his songs feel like poetry when read and like music when heard.

He used flowers, thorns, the world, nature, and everyday objects as symbols carrying broad human meaning. Expressing deep philosophy through simple imagery was one of his most significant creative strengths.

Indian Army Chief General Dhiraj Seth has handed over medical supplies to the Nepali Army.

According to Army Headquarters, Seth handed over both medical and military supplies. He had earlier also planted a tree at Army Headquarters.

President Ramchandra Paudel also conferred on Seth the honorary rank insignia of General of the Nepali Army.

title.rendered: Illegal Chinese liquor worth Rs 9.15 million seized in Humla in a week

content.rendered:
Humla, August 17

A monitoring team led by Chief District Officer Bholanath Guragai has destroyed illegal Chinese liquor and Budweiser canned beer worth Rs 3.966 million.

The team destroyed 606 cartons of illegal Chinese liquor, 54 cartons of Budweiser canned beer and one carton of whisky that had been hidden at Chhungsachaur in Namkha Rural Municipality-2, Humla.

According to Chief District Officer Guragai, 7,272 bottles of illegal Chinese liquor, 1,296 bottles of Budweiser canned beer and 12 bottles of whisky were destroyed.

Guragai said the illegal and inedible Chinese liquor was destroyed at Chhungsachaur in Namkha Rural Municipality in the presence of representatives from the Nepal Police, Armed Police Force, National Investigation Department, the District Treasury and Comptroller Office, Humla, the Chamber of Commerce and Industry, journalists, and Latar Lama, ward chairperson of Namkha Rural Municipality-4.

According to Guragai, on August 13, a team led by Assistant Chief District Officer Chandrabir Shahi seized 594 cartons of illegal Chinese liquor and 194 cartons of Budweiser from Nawalthang in Namkha Rural Municipality-2.

Police have seized illegal Chinese liquor worth Rs 9.159 million in Humla within a week.

title.rendered: NEPSE falls 2.25 points as turnover hits Rs 5.52 billion

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, 17 August

Nepal’s stock exchange (NEPSE) fell 2.25 points on Monday, the first trading day of the week. The NEPSE index had declined by 7.37 points on Friday.

After Monday’s trading, the NEPSE index stood at 2,641 points. The prices of 72 companies increased, while 201 declined and seven remained unchanged.

Trading turnover increased to Rs 5.52 billion from Rs 4.27 billion on the previous trading day. Monday’s turnover was the highest since July 27.

The finance sector recorded the biggest decline, falling 1.14%, while the manufacturing and processing sector gained the most, rising 1.30%.

The banking sector fell 0.50%, development banks 0.29%, hotels and tourism 0.56%, investment 0.59%, life insurance 0.36%, microfinance 0.66% and non-life insurance 0.61%.

Hydropower rose 0.45%, the other sector 0.47% and trading 0.14%.

The hydropower sector recorded the highest turnover among sectoral groups at Rs 2.23 billion. Commercial banks recorded transactions worth Rs 650 million, while manufacturing and processing companies recorded Rs 160 million in turnover.

Recently listed companies Sarbottam Paints and Mount Everest Power saw their share prices rise by 15%. Reliance Spinning Mills gained 11.17%, Sagarmatha Hydropower Company 11.06% and Development Hydropower 8.22%.

First Microfinance fell 6.63%, Mahila Laghubitta 6.57%, Khanikhola Hydropower 6.33% and Central Finance 4.54%.

In terms of turnover, Reliance Spinning Mills, Solu Hydropower, Ridi Power, Khanikhola Hydropower and Development Hydropower were the most actively traded companies.

title.rendered: Opposition lawmakers end 78-day protest after Speaker rules PM must answer questions

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, 17 August

Opposition lawmakers in the House of Representatives have ended their 78-day protest after Speaker Dol Prasad Aryal ruled that Prime Minister Balendra Shah (Balen) must answer lawmakers’ questions and attend the direct question-and-answer session as required by parliamentary rules.

Opposition lawmakers stood in protest immediately after Monday’s House meeting began, continuing their practice from previous sessions.

Speaker Aryal said he had taken note of the opposition’s long-running protest demanding answers from Prime Minister Shah on important issues related to the prime minister and his areas of responsibility.

He then issued a ruling directing the prime minister to attend the House and answer lawmakers’ questions.

“I rule that the Right Honourable Prime Minister attend the meeting of the House of Representatives and answer questions from Honourable Members in accordance with Rules 56, 57, 58, 59 and 60 of the regulations,” Aryal said.

Opposition lawmakers remained uncertain for a while even after the ruling.

They had been protesting in the House since May 31, demanding clarification from Prime Minister Shah over remarks he made about the Nepal-India border dispute.

The opposition had also repeatedly drawn the attention of the Speaker and the government to the failure to hold the direct question-and-answer session with the prime minister.

The Speaker, however, did not issue a ruling on Shah’s remarks concerning the border dispute. Instead, he directed the prime minister to be prepared for the direct question-and-answer session.

After Aryal said he had already issued a ruling in the name of the government and prime minister as demanded by the lawmakers, he asked the opposition lawmakers to take their seats.

The lawmakers then ended their protest, bringing the 78-day disruption to an end.

The opposition’s protest began after Prime Minister Shah addressed the House on May 31 and made two statements concerning Nepal’s border dispute with India.

Shah said the government had discussed the issue not only with India and China but also with the United Kingdom, arguing that Britain should have a role because the issue dates back to the time of British India.

He also said he had recently learned, after becoming prime minister, that Nepal had encroached on Indian territory in several places, in addition to India encroaching on Nepali territory.

Opposition parties immediately demanded facts and clarification from Shah over the remarks. However, the prime minister did not agree to provide the requested explanation.

The opposition continued its protest for 14 days in Jestha, all 32 days of Ashadh and all 31 days of Shrawan.

At the start of each House meeting, opposition lawmakers would stand in protest and demand that Shah respond to his remarks. They also criticised the government for failing to hold the direct question-and-answer session with the prime minister.

Under Rule 56 of the House of Representatives Regulations, the direct question-and-answer session with the prime minister is scheduled for one day during the first week of every month, during the first hour of the meeting.

Although the Speaker and the House are responsible for implementing the provision, Aryal issued the ruling after the prime minister had not appeared for the session.

With the Speaker now directing Shah to attend the House and answer lawmakers’ questions, opposition lawmakers have withdrawn their protest.

title.rendered: Speaker DP Aryal rules government must respond to lawmakers’ concerns within three days

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, 17 August

Speaker Dol Prasad Aryal (DP Aryal) has directed the government to respond within three days to issues raised in the House of Representatives by lawmakers Gopal Sharma and Ashika Tamang.

Nepali Communist Party lawmaker Sharma reminded the House that he had raised concerns on August 7 about people affected by the Jajarkot earthquake.

He said he had urged the government to take responsibility for relief and reconstruction work in Jajarkot and Salyan but had not received a response.

“On August 7, I gave the government a nine-day deadline and sought at least a response. I raised this as a shared concern. Since there has still been no response, I request the Speaker to issue an immediate ruling with a deadline,” Sharma said.

Rastriya Swatantra Party lawmaker Tamang raised the issue of the body of Santosh Rai from Dhading, which remains in Cambodia, saying the government had failed to take the necessary steps to bring it back to Nepal.

“Thirty-seven days ago, I raised the issue during the zero hour, asking that Santosh Rai’s body be brought back to Nepal from Cambodia. But the issue disappeared into the zero hour,” she said.

“I thought that once an issue was raised in the House, it would be implemented. But how long must a lawmaker keep going from one minister’s door to another secretary’s door to pursue the same issue, Speaker?”

Tamang said the Ministry of Finance had allocated a budget for managing the body but the process could not move forward because there was no procedure for using the funds.

She said she would continue standing in the House until she received a response on the matter.

Following the concerns raised by the two lawmakers, Speaker Aryal directed the government to provide a response within three days.

The Speaker issued the direction under Rule 56 of the House of Representatives Regulations for the direct question-and-answer session with the prime minister.

title.rendered: Khanikhola SUV accident: Thick fog hampers helicopter rescue of injured

content.rendered:
Kavrepalanchok, August 17

The rescue of people seriously injured in an SUV accident at Syauthali in Khanikhola Rural Municipality-1, Kavrepalanchok, has been hampered by thick fog.

Although a helicopter has been arranged to rescue the injured, the heavy fog at the accident site has made it difficult for the helicopter to land.

According to Rural Municipality Chairperson Indra Bahadur Thing, a helicopter was arranged for the rescue operation, but it has been unable to land due to the thick fog.

Kavre Chief District Officer Gopal Kumar Adhikari said efforts were underway to rescue the injured by helicopter from Kamidanda in Bethanchok-5 because of the dense fog at the accident site.

“The helicopter is ready. If conditions permit, efforts are being made to carry out the rescue from Kamidanda. The Nepal Army is currently conducting a feasibility assessment of the area,” he said.

Two people were killed, and three others seriously injured when the SUV crashed at Syaurathali in Khanikhola Rural Municipality on Monday morning. The deceased have been identified as Kalka Bahadur Majhi of Khanikhola-4 and Patli Maya Moktan of Khanikhola-2. The identities of the seriously injured have yet to be confirmed.

Police suspect that the accident may have been caused by brake failure.

title.rendered: Lekhak says Nepali Congress unity now rests with Gagan Thapa

content.rendered:
Kathmandu, 17 August

Nepali Congress leader Ramesh Lekhak has said the responsibility for uniting the party now lies with party president Gagan Kumar Thapa, warning that anything could happen if efforts are not made to bring the party together.

Lekhak made the remarks during a discussion with party leaders and cadres from Kanchanpur who had come to Kathmandu to attend the Sher Bahadur Deuba faction’s national gathering. The discussion was held at Anandabhoomi Event in New Baneshwor on Monday.

“The responsibility to bring the party together now lies with Gaganji. Anything could happen if efforts are not made to unite the party,” Lekhak said.

Lekhak said the Deuba faction had made every possible effort to unite the party but had failed to do so.

“There has been no lack of effort from our side,” he said.

According to Lekhak, former party president Sher Bahadur Deuba handed over acting responsibilities to former vice-president Purna Bahadur Khadka and also authorised him to sign documents for electoral purposes as part of efforts to keep the party united.

“There was an argument that the party could not win an election with Sher Bahadur’s signature. Was it easy to tell a party president who had won with such a large majority not to sign the tickets?” he said.

“But we asked him to give up the authority to sign in order to unite the party. He handed it over to Purna Bahadur,” Lekhak said.

Lekhak also urged party leaders and cadres from Kanchanpur to strengthen contact with members who have updated their party membership and bring them into the Deuba faction’s position.

“Strengthen contact with those who have updated their membership. Bring them to where we stand,” he said. “From today, there will be no distinction between those who have updated their membership and those who have not.”

Lekhak also asked Kanchanpur party president Padam Bogati to prepare programmes in all three constituencies of the district between Dashain and Tihar.

“If possible, organise programmes in the district between Dashain and Tihar. NP Saud and I will come together,” he said. “We will travel around all three constituencies.”
